Stir in diced pineapple. Cook 2-3 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk flour with 30 ml cold water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into the curry to thicken slightly. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot with jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: For authentic Thai flavor, use full-fat coconut cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Suspiro de Vino Dulce y Canela
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, elegant dessert presented on a pristine white bone china plate. A perfectly formed quenelle of glossy, pale caramel-hued brown sugar cinnamon cremeux anchors the composition, its creamy texture visible. Beside it, a translucent, shimmering pool of golden sweet wine fluid gel provides a vibrant color and textural contrast. Two crisp, irregularly shaped chancaca tuiles, their edges a rich amber, stand upright, adding architectural height and delicate crunch. Scattered around the main elements are three to four petite, pristine white meringue kisses, their airy, crisp form contrasting with the smooth cremeux. The composition is artfully asymmetrical, with abundant negative space. The plate rests on a polished dark wood surface, complemented by a neatly folded white linen napkin. Professional, soft light creates subtle shadows, enhancing depth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small shot of Pisco Acholado on the side for an authentic pairing.
instructions: Bloom gelatin in cold water.
Heat cream, milk, and cinnamon stick to a simmer. Remove cinnamon stick.
Whisk egg yolks and 80g brown sugar until pale.
Temper hot cream mixture into egg yolks. Return mixture to saucepan.
Cook gently over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (nappe consistency). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Strain cremeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a shallow dish. Chill minimum 4 hours, or overnight, until set.
Combine sweet wine, 20g granulated sugar, and agar-agar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly.
Boil for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow container. Chill until set, about 1 hour.
Once set, scoop gel into a blender. Blend until a smooth fluid gel forms. Transfer to a squeeze bottle. Chill until needed.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat.
Whisk melted butter, 30g brown sugar, flour, and 1 egg white until smooth.
Spread very thin circles (5-6 cm diameter) of batter onto the silicone mat.
Bake 6-8 minutes, until edges are golden brown and crisp. Cool completely on the mat. Store tuiles airtight.
Preheat oven to 100°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk 50g egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add 100g granulated sugar, whipping until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Transfer meringue to a piping bag with a small round tip. Pipe small kisses (approx. 1 cm) onto parchment.
Bake 60-75 minutes, until meringues are dry and crisp. Cool completely. Store airtight.
To assemble: Spoon a quenelle or smear of brown sugar cinnamon cremeux onto one side of each plate.
Drizzle a small amount of sweet wine fluid gel beside the cremeux.
Arrange 1-2 chancaca tuiles upright next to the cremeux, adding height.
Place 3-4 meringue kisses artfully around the elements on the plate.
notes: This dessert balances richness with lightness. Temperature contrast is key with chilled cremeux and gel, and crisp tuiles and meringues.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Advocaat Mushroom Cream
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breasts, each a golden-brown medallion, are centrally arranged on a round white porcelain plate. They are generously coated with a lustrous, pale-yellow cream sauce, rich and slightly thick. Sautéed cremini mushroom slices are nestled around and atop the chicken, their earthy brown contrasting with the sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh chives adds a pop of green and delicate texture. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The chicken is presented as whole pieces, not sliced. Natural, even lighting highlights the sauce's creamy texture and the chicken's seared crust. A simple cotton napkin and traditional European flatware are placed beside the plate on a clean wooden surface, creating a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted potatoes or rice.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15g butter to the skillet. Add diced shallots. Cook 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in heavy cream and advocaat. Simmer gently 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk egg yolk in a small bowl. Gradually whisk a ladleful of hot sauce into the egg yolk.
Pour tempered egg yolk mixture back into the skillet. Whisk constantly until incorporated. Do not boil.
Return chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat gently 1-2 minutes until warmed through.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.
notes: The subtle sweetness of advocaat is balanced by savory ingredients. Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Turkey Medallions with Aji Amarillo Potato Puree and Kidney Bean Velouté
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim, resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. The composition is minimalist, artistic, and flowing, utilizing abundant negative space. A vibrant, creamy yellow Aji Amarillo Potato Puree is artfully swirled or swooshed across one side of the plate, creating an organic, elegant curve. Adjacent to the puree, a single, perfectly seared turkey medallion, retaining its natural, thick chunk shape and exhibiting a rich, golden-brown crust, is positioned purposefully. A deep, lustrous red Kidney Bean Velouté forms a delicate, free-form pool, contrasting beautifully with the bright yellow puree. A single, irregular shard of golden-crisp chicken skin stands upright or rests artfully on the turkey, providing a textural counterpoint. The plate is sparsely dotted with a few precise drops of bright orange Aji Amarillo Oil, adding a final pop of color and flavor. The overall aesthetic is one of sophisticated simplicity, showcasing masterful technique and premium ingredients. The background is ultra-minimalist, perhaps with a soft, diffused light creating subtle shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests elegantly beside the plate. A small, refined, unglazed terracotta pinch bowl, subtly textured, is placed just off the plate, holding a tiny portion of bright Aji Amarillo paste for a cultural flourish, emphasizing authenticity without clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small, elegant ceramic pinch bowl of additional Aji Amarillo paste on the side for guests to adjust spice preference.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Place chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper, then between two baking trays. Bake 20-25 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove, drain on paper towel. Break into large shards. Set aside.

Boil potato cubes in salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. In a small saucepan, melt 20g butter. Add half of minced garlic and half of diced red onion. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add 20g Aji Amarillo paste. Cook 1 minute. Combine cooked potatoes, sautéed mixture, evaporated milk, and crumbled feta. Mash or pass through a ricer until smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.

In a saucepan, heat 10ml olive oil. Add remaining diced red onion and minced garlic. Sauté 3 minutes until translucent. Add cooked kidney beans and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes. Blend mixture until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Return to low heat. Whisk in 30g butter until emulsified and velouté is glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
In a very small saucepan, combine 10ml olive oil and 10g Aji Amarillo paste. Heat gently for 2 minutes, do not boil. Remove from heat. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Set aside.

Pat turkey medallions very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey medallions 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan, rest 5 minutes.

On each plate, place a generous swoosh of Aji Amarillo Potato Puree. Arrange one seared turkey medallion adjacent to the puree. Pour a delicate pool of Kidney Bean Velouté. Garnish with a shard of crispy chicken skin. Dot the plate with a few drops of Aji Amarillo Oil.
notes: Ensure all components are prepared and kept warm for seamless plating.
Achieve a very smooth consistency for both the potato puree and the bean velouté by passing through a fine-mesh sieve.
Do not overcrowd the plate; embrace negative space for a truly minimalist, fine-dining presentation.
traditional_techniques: Precision pureeing and sieving for refined textures
Controlled searing to achieve a perfect crust on the turkey

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Classic Beef Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular, handcrafted appearance. The stew is rich and hearty, featuring substantial chunks of dark brown, tender beef. Large, pale yellow potato cubes and vibrant orange carrot rounds are visible throughout the thick, savory, dark brown gravy. Some finely chopped green parsley, if used as a garnish, is lightly sprinkled over the top, adding a touch of freshness. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting and inviting presentation. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Adjacent to the bowl, a simple, everyday metal fork or spoon rests on a casually draped, cream-colored cloth napkin. The scene is illuminated by soft, warm kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and lived-in atmosphere typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced yellow onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add dried thyme and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours.
While stew simmers, peel and cut potatoes into large 3-4 cm cubes. Peel and cut carrots into thick 2 cm rounds.
After 1.5 hours, add potatoes and carrots to the pot. Stir well.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve hot.
notes: The stew can be made a day ahead; flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure beef is fork-tender before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely single portion of rustic chicken and tomato pasta is presented on a simple, well-loved, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim, resting on a warm, natural wooden dining table. Thick chunks of seared chicken, golden-brown and tender, are nestled among al dente penne pasta. The pasta is generously coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce, flecked with finely diced onion and minced garlic. Fresh green thyme leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and herbaceous aroma. The textures are varied, from the firm pasta to the succulent chicken and soft sauce. A fork is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in soft, inviting kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. A small bowl of grated Parmesan cheese is nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Stir in cooked pasta.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with fresh Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Creamed Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Skillet Chicken with Creamed Corn is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic dinner plate, reflecting a homely, casual style. A golden-brown, seared chicken breast, cut into two thick, rustic chunks, is nestled centrally in a generous pool of creamy, pale yellow corn. The corn sauce is thick and comforting, with visible, plump corn kernels throughout. The chicken exhibits a tender, cooked texture with a crisp exterior from searing. A sprinkle of bright green, chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The components are arranged naturally, touching and slightly overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a family kitchen setting. A casually placed, simple cloth napkin and a clear water glass are visible nearby. The lighting is warm and cozy, typical of indoor kitchen fixtures, enhancing the comforting appeal of the meal. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, add diced yellow onion. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over onions and garlic. Stir for 1 minute to create a light roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then heavy cream. Stir constantly until sauce thickens and simmers.
Add corn kernels to the sauce. Stir to combine.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, nestling them into the corn sauce.
Cover skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 10-12 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Esquites and Avocado Crema
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and juicy, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a vibrant mound of esquites showcases charred yellow corn kernels, speckled with finely diced red onion, minced green jalapeño, and fresh green cilantro. A creamy, light green avocado crema is artfully drizzled over the chicken and esquites, creating delicate streaks. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of crumbled white cotija cheese and a few fresh cilantro leaves. A bright green lime wedge sits on the plate. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table surface with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of your favorite hot sauce.
Pair with a refreshing agua fresca or horchata.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, toss chicken with 15ml olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper. Ensure even coating.
Place seasoned chicken on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes.
While chicken roasts, prepare esquites. Dice red onion finely. Mince jalapeño (if using). Mince garlic.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add corn kernels. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred, about 5-7 minutes.
Add diced red onion, minced jalapeño, and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring until fragrant.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in mayonnaise, sour cream, juice of 1 lime, and a pinch of chili powder. Mix well.
Chop half the cilantro. Crumble cotija cheese. Stir chopped cilantro and most of the cotija cheese into the corn mixture.
Prepare avocado crema. Halve avocados. Scoop flesh into a blender or food processor. Add juice of remaining 1 lime, remaining fresh cilantro, and a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth and creamy.

To serve, place a roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of esquites beside the chicken. Drizzle avocado crema over the chicken and esquites. Garnish with remaining crumbled cotija cheese and fresh cilantro leaves. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Adjust jalapeño quantity to control spice level.
For extra flavor, marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes before roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Corn & Lime Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Sweet Corn & Lime Tartlet sits centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tartlet features a crisp, golden-brown pâte sucrée shell, precisely molded with fluted edges. Inside, the filling is a smooth, pale yellow sweet corn custard, its surface even and slightly glossy. A vibrant sprinkle of finely grated fresh lime zest adorns the custard, providing a bright color contrast. The overall presentation is refined and minimalist, with ample negative space on the plate to highlight the pastry. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the delicate textures and fresh colors of the dessert. The focus is entirely on the elegantly presented tartlet, inviting immediate enjoyment.

ingredients.name: toasted coconut flakes, optional for garnish

instructions: Prepare Pâte Sucrée: Combine flour, cold butter, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl. Rub butter into dry ingredients until crumbly. Add egg yolk; mix until dough forms. Flatten into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Blind Bake Tartlet Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough to 3mm thickness. Line four 10cm tartlet molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper and fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until light golden. Let cool.

Prepare Sweet Corn Custard: Combine corn kernels and milk in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Blend mixture until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
In a bowl, whisk caster sugar, egg yolks, and cornstarch until smooth. Gradually whisk in the warm strained corn milk.
Return mixture to the saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until custard thickens significantly and boils for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in lime zest, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt.
Assemble Tartlets: Pour warm custard into the pre-baked tartlet shells. Fill almost to the brim.
Bake Tartlets: Reduce oven temperature to 160°C. Bake tartlets for 10-15 minutes, or until custard is set but still slightly wobbly in the center.

Cool and Garnish: Let tartlets cool completely on a wire rack. Chill for at least 1 hour. Just before serving, sprinkle generously with fresh lime zest. Optionally, add a few toasted coconut flakes for texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Pork Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Korean Pork Stir-fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thinly sliced pork pieces, seared and caramelized, display a rich reddish-orange hue from the chili paste. They are mixed with tender-crisp white onion slices and bright orange julienned carrots. Vibrant green pieces of green onion are scattered throughout the dish. A glossy, savory-spicy sauce coats all ingredients, reflecting light. The stir-fry is naturally mounded in the plate's center, leaving moderate negative space around the edges. A light sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds garnishes the top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a small white ceramic bowl of fluffy steamed white rice and traditional Korean metal chopsticks resting on a chopstick rest. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtle, casual restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Serve with an assortment of banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi or pickled radishes.
Can be eaten by wrapping portions in fresh lettuce leaves.
instructions: Thinly slice pork shoulder or belly against the grain.
In a large bowl, combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, minced ginger, sugar, rice wine, and black pepper. Mix well to form the marinade.
Add sliced pork to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat cooking oil in a large wok or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Add marinated pork to the hot pan. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until pork is cooked through and lightly caramelized. Ensure no pieces are fanned out; present as whole chunks or pieces.
Add sliced onion and julienned carrot to the pan. Continue to stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in the green onion pieces during the last minute of cooking.
Transfer the spicy pork stir-fry to a serving plate. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
notes: Adjust the amount of gochugaru to control the spice level according to your preference.
For best flavor, marinate the pork for at least 1 hour.
Pork shoulder or belly provides the best texture and flavor for this dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Dark Ale Stew
recipes.visual_description: A generous single serving of hearty beef and dark ale stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a rich, dark brown gravy. Large, irregular chunks of tender braised beef are prominent, interspersed with thick rounds of sweet roasted carrots, chunky pieces of soft potato, and caramelized onion. The stew's surface has a glossy sheen, indicating its rich, reduced sauce. A scattering of vibrant fresh parsley leaves provides a pop of green against the deep, earthy tones of the stew. The bowl is placed slightly off-center on a simple, light wooden table surface. A neatly folded off-white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and deep colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, showcasing the comforting nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with creamy mashed potatoes.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cut into thick 2 cm rounds

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onions to pot. Sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in dark ale. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to pot. Add beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Liquid should mostly cover beef.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover pot.
Braise for 1.5 hours.
Add carrots and potatoes to pot. Stir gently.
Continue braising, covered, for another 1 hour, or until beef and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Aji Amarillo & Peanut Consommé with Rice Noodle Pearls and Popcorn Air
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aji Amarillo & Peanut Consommé is presented in a wide, shallow, modern designer bone china bowl, resting on a premium white Carrara marble surface. The consommé is a clear, golden-yellow liquid, creating abundant negative space within the pristine white bowl. At the bowl's center, a precise cluster of delicate, white rice noodle pearls is meticulously arranged, providing a focal point without being fully submerged. A light, airy cloud of off-white popcorn air floats gracefully on a section of the consommé, offering a soft textural contrast. A few vibrant green micro cilantro leaves are strategically placed on or beside the popcorn air, adding a fresh color pop. A very thin, artful drizzle of bright red chili oil creates a subtle visual line across the consommé. The entire composition is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing clean lines and sophisticated simplicity. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the bowl. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and elegance. The background is utterly uncluttered, highlighting the dish as the sole subject.

ingredients.name: Aji Limo (or red bird's eye chili), deseeded

instructions: Prepare chicken stock: Combine chicken bones, carrots, celery, onion, and cilantro stems in a large pot. Cover with 3 liters cold water. Bring to a simmer. Skim impurities. Simmer gently for 3 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Infuse stock: Return strained stock to a clean pot. Add Aji Amarillo paste and peanut butter. Whisk until dissolved. Add corn kernels. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Do not boil. Strain again through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract flavor. Season with salt and white pepper. Chill thoroughly.

Clarify consommé: In a bowl, combine ground chicken, finely diced carrot, celery, onion, and egg whites. Mix well to form a 'raft' mixture. Gently add the chilled infused stock to a clean pot. Float the raft mixture on top. Heat slowly over medium-low heat. The raft will solidify and rise. Do not stir. Once raft forms, poke a small hole in the center to allow consommé to bubble through. Simmer very gently for 45 minutes. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Discard raft. Keep consommé warm.

Prepare rice noodle pearls: Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions until al dente. Rinse with cold water. Drain well. Using kitchen shears, cut noodles into very small, uniform 'pearls' (approx. 3-5 mm length).

Make chili oil: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add deseeded Aji Limo chili. Infuse gently for 10 minutes. Do not brown chili. Strain oil. Discard chili. Keep chili oil separate for drizzling.

Prepare popcorn air: Blend air-popped popcorn with 100 ml chicken stock (or water) until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Heat strained popcorn liquid gently. Whisk in soy lecithin until dissolved. Using an immersion blender, create a stable foam on the surface.

Assemble and serve: Warm four wide, shallow bowls. Place a small, precise cluster of rice noodle pearls in the center of each bowl. Carefully ladle hot, clear Aji Amarillo & Peanut Consommé around the noodles. Do not submerge noodles completely. Gently spoon a delicate cloud of popcorn air onto the consommé, adjacent to the noodles. Drizzle a few drops of chili oil precisely around the foam or on the consommé. Garnish with 1-2 micro cilantro leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For the consommé, ensure the stock is completely degreased and cold before clarification for best results.
The popcorn air must be made just before serving to maintain its delicate texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Pork and Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Gochujang Pork and Rice Bowl presented in a clean, off-white ceramic bowl with a wide rim. The main subject is the richly colored Gochujang-marinated pork, cooked to a tender, slightly caramelized finish. The pork, cut into irregular 2-3 cm chunks, displays deep reddish-orange hues from the gochujang, with occasional browned edges from searing. Adjacent to the pork is a generous portion of fluffy, steamed short-grain white rice, its pristine white contrasting with the meat. Arranged artfully around the pork and rice are complementary elements: a small mound of vibrant red kimchi with visible napa cabbage texture, a pile of bright yellow, thinly sliced Danmuji (pickled radish) providing a crisp counterpoint, and a small cluster of blanched, vibrant green spinach, gently seasoned. The entire dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions scattered over the pork and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds for added texture and visual interest. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. A set of elegant metal chopsticks rests over the bowl's rim, with a Korean-style shallow soup spoon beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with an assortment of banchan (small side dishes) such as various namul (seasoned vegetables) or other kimchi varieties.
Offer ssamjang (spicy dipping sauce) and fresh lettuce leaves for wrapping the pork and rice.
Accompany with a simple clear soup like Kongnamul Guk (soybean sprout soup).

ingredients.name: Blanched spinach or quick cucumber salad

instructions: Slice pork shoulder into 0.5 cm thick slices or 2-3 cm chunks. In a large bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, mirin, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, brown sugar, and gochugaru. Add pork and sliced onion. Mix well to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Combine rice and water in a medium pot. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, keep covered, and let steam for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Heat cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated pork and onions. Spread pork in a single layer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is cooked through and slightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 71°C (160°F).
Divide cooked rice among 4 individual serving bowls. Arrange cooked pork alongside the rice. Add kimchi, danmuji, and blanched spinach or cucumber salad to each bowl.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately with chopsticks and a Korean soup spoon.
notes: Adjust gochugaru amount for desired spice level.
Pork shoulder can be substituted with pork belly for a richer flavor.
traditional_techniques: Marinating meat in a chili-based paste (gochujang) for flavor penetration and tenderization.
Serving a main dish with various banchan for a balanced meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Mushroom and Tomato Ragout, Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rich Braised Beef with Mushroom and Tomato Ragout is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three substantial, fork-tender beef chunks, deeply browned from searing and then braised, are nestled within a glossy, dark red-brown ragout. The ragout is thick, featuring tender slices of mushroom, soft diced tomatoes, and remnants of aromatic vegetables, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Adjacent to the beef and ragout, a neat cluster of golden-brown roasted potato wedges is arranged. The potato wedges have a slightly crisp exterior and a fluffy interior. A light sprinkling of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded natural cotton napkin and classic silver flatware placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the deep, warm colors and inviting textures of the dish, creating an approachable yet elegant casual dining presentation.

ingredients.name: Large potatoes (e.g., Russet or Maris Piper)

instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm large chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, chopped carrots, and chopped celery. Cook for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, prepare potatoes. Wash potatoes and cut into 2-3 cm wedges. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potato wedges in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast in the oven with the beef during the last 45-60 minutes of braising, or until golden brown and tender.
Remove braised beef from oven. Skim any excess fat from the surface of the ragout. Remove bay leaves and herb sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning for the ragout.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve braised beef chunks with mushroom and tomato ragout. Arrange roasted potato wedges alongside. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Ragu with Mushrooms and Melted Provolone
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Beef Ragu with Mushrooms and Melted Provolone is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rich, savory composition. Generous chunks of fork-tender, dark brown beef are nestled among glistening, sautéed cremini mushroom slices and soft, diced red onion, all coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato ragu. A thick, bubbly layer of melted, golden-brown provolone cheese blankets the top, with some cheese pulls visible. The dish has a balanced composition, with moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the melted cheese, providing a pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and rich colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, trimmed and diced into 3 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef from skillet and set aside.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 7 minutes.
Return beef to the skillet. Stir in diced tomatoes, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, and hot sauce.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Preheat oven broiler.
Sprinkle shredded provolone cheese evenly over the beef mixture in the skillet.
Broil for 3-5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and lightly golden.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Cheesy Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, set on an everyday ceramic plate. A single modest portion of baked chicken and vegetables fills the plate, showing natural, unarranged components. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is nestled among roasted vegetables. Carrots are cut into thick, tender rounds, showing slight caramelization. Red and yellow bell peppers are roasted into soft, slightly charred chunks. Cauliflower florets are tender with browned edges. Quartered tomatoes are soft and slightly burst, releasing their juices. Melted, bubbly, golden-brown cheese generously covers parts of the chicken and vegetables. The colors are natural and earthy – rich browns, reds, oranges, and creamy whites, all glistening with cooking juices. A simple side of fresh cucumber slices, cut into thin rounds, is placed beside the main dish, offering a cool contrast. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, emphasizing comfort and a lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry. Season chicken generously with salt, black pepper, white pepper, garlic powder, and dried herbs.
Cut carrots into 2 cm thick rounds. Cut bell peppers into 3 cm chunks. Break cauliflower into small florets. Quarter tomatoes.
In a large baking dish, toss carrots, bell peppers, cauliflower, and tomatoes with olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Arrange seasoned chicken pieces among the vegetables in the baking dish.
Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle grated cheese evenly over chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is melted and golden-brown.
While the dish finishes baking, slice the cucumber into thin rounds for a simple fresh side.
Serve hot directly from the baking dish or plated individually.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Cheesy Chicken and Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of Homestyle Cheesy Chicken and Vegetable Bake sits on a slightly imperfect, everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. The dish features generous chunks of roasted chicken, nestled among tender, diced carrots, vibrant red bell peppers, and softened cauliflower florets. The entire top is covered with a golden-brown, bubbly layer of melted cheddar cheese, with some crispy edges. A hint of rich red tomato sauce peeks through the vegetables. The chicken chunks are natural, not fanned. A few flecks of dried thyme are visible on the cheese. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with rustic textures. To the side, a small bowl holds simple, fresh cucumber slices. A casually placed, folded linen napkin sits nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, casting soft shadows that emphasize the comfort and homeliness of the meal. The background is a slightly blurred, lived-in family kitchen setting, with minimal, unobtrusive clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served family-style in the baking dish with individual portions scooped onto plates.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad or crusty bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Peel carrots and cut into 1.5cm dice. Deseed bell pepper and cut into 2cm dice. Cut cauliflower into small florets (approx 3cm). Chop onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add chopped onion, diced carrot, and diced bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Add minced garlic, dried thyme, and white pepper. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Add cauliflower florets to the skillet. Gently stir into the mixture.
Season with salt to taste.
Sprinkle grated cheese evenly over the top of the chicken and vegetable mixture.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is melted and bubbly.
While bake cooks, prepare a simple cucumber salad: slice cucumber and serve alongside.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C.
This bake is excellent for meal prepping.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Green Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Vietnamese Potato and Green Bean Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of textures and colors. Diced, pale yellow potatoes form the base, interspersed with bright green, crisp-tender chopped green beans. Thinly sliced red onion adds a touch of subtle purple and a slight bite. Shredded white chicken is sparsely distributed, acting as a minor protein accent among the vegetables. The salad is lightly coated in a clear, golden-hued Nuoc Cham dressing, allowing the ingredients to shine. It is generously garnished with fresh green mint and cilantro leaves, along with coarsely crushed roasted peanuts and golden-brown crispy fried shallots, providing essential crunch. The arrangement is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space, inviting and approachable. A simple wooden table surface and soft, natural lighting complete the casual bistro setting. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light meal, appetizer, or side dish alongside grilled meats or spring rolls.
Offer additional Nuoc Cham dressing on the side for those who prefer more.
Enjoy with a side of steamed jasmine rice, though typically eaten as a stand-alone salad.
instructions: Boil or steam potatoes until tender. Cool completely. Peel and dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain and chop into 2 cm pieces.
Shred cooked chicken breast into fine strands. Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F).
Thinly slice red onion. For a milder taste, soak in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain.
For the dressing, finely mince garlic and chili. In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and water. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add minced garlic and chili.
Roughly chop fresh mint and cilantro.
Coarsely crush roasted peanuts.
In a large bowl, gently combine diced potatoes, chopped green beans, shredded chicken, and sliced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual plates. Garnish with chopped fresh mint, cilantro, crushed peanuts, and crispy fried shallots if using. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, ensure potatoes are completely cooled before mixing to prevent them from breaking apart.
Adjust chili and sugar in the dressing to suit your preferred level of spiciness and sweetness.
The salad can be prepared up to an hour in advance, but add the dressing just before serving to maintain freshness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Herb-Roasted Potatoes and Pan Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. Alongside, several substantial, rustic 2-3 cm roasted potato wedges are scattered artfully. The potatoes exhibit a deep golden crust with hints of green from finely chopped rosemary and thyme. A rich, glossy pan jus, reduced to a light amber, is generously drizzled over the chicken and potatoes, pooling slightly on the plate. A few fresh sprigs of thyme or rosemary are placed beside the chicken for garnish. The dish offers warm, earthy tones of roasted ingredients contrasted with the vibrant green herbs. The overall presentation is professional yet inviting, set on a simple wooden table with standard modern flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm wedges. Place on a baking tray.
Mince garlic. Chop leaves from 1 rosemary sprig and 2 thyme sprigs.
Toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Spread in a single layer on the tray.
Roast potatoes for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season skin and flesh with 5g salt and 2g black pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add remaining 30ml olive oil.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Pour off excess fat, leaving 1-2 tablespoons.
Add white wine to the skillet. Scrape up browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate each chicken thigh with a portion of roasted potatoes. Spoon pan jus generously over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs and remaining rosemary sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed skillet like cast iron.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Apple & Cheddar Streusel Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Spiced Apple & Cheddar Streusel Cake is presented on a clean, white porcelain dessert plate. The cake slice stands tall, revealing distinct layers: a pale golden, tender cake base studded with soft, diced apple chunks and subtle flecks of white cheddar. A thick, golden-brown streusel layer, rich with visible crumbs of butter, flour, brown sugar, and sharp cheddar, crowns the cake. A light dusting of white powdered sugar delicately covers the top of the streusel and the plate, adding a refined finish. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's textures and warm colors. The background is softly blurred, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
For the streusel: In a small bowl, combine 50 g flour, 50 g brown sugar, 2.5 g cinnamon, and 2.5 g nutmeg. Cut in 30 g cold butter until crumbly. Stir in 25 g finely grated cheddar cheese. Set aside.
For the cake: In a large bowl, cream 85 g softened butter and 150 g granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 150 g flour, 5 g baking powder, 2.5 g baking soda, and 2.5 g salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with 120 ml whole milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Peel, core, and dice the apples into 1 cm cubes. Gently fold diced apples and 50 g finely grated cheddar cheese into the cake batter.
Pour half of the batter into the prepared cake pan. Sprinkle half of the streusel mixture over the batter.
Carefully spoon the remaining batter over the streusel layer. Sprinkle the remaining streusel evenly over the top.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Fig Balsamic Glaze, Creamy Polenta, and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white round porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table surface. A grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. At the center of the plate, a generous portion of creamy, golden-yellow polenta forms a soft bed. Resting atop the polenta are thick, succulent pieces of pan-seared duck breast, showing off its deeply golden, crispy skin and a juicy pink interior. The duck is cut into thick, substantial pieces, not fanned. Draped over the duck and polenta is a rich, glossy fig balsamic glaze, glistening with hints of dark purple from the softened fig quarters. Alongside the polenta and duck are bright green, tender-crisp roasted asparagus spears, their vibrant color contrasting with the deeper tones of the duck and glaze. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The colors are natural and appealing: the rich browns of the duck skin, the creamy yellow of the polenta, the deep purple-brown of the glaze, and the vibrant green of the asparagus. The texture contrast between the crispy duck skin, tender duck meat, smooth polenta, and firm asparagus is evident.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of medium-bodied red wine, such as Pinot Noir or Merlot.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the remaining glaze and polenta.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan.
Render duck fat over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temp 60-63°C), or until desired doneness.
Remove duck from pan. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5-10 minutes.
Pour off excess duck fat from the pan, leaving about 1 tablespoon.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add balsamic vinegar, honey, and thyme sprigs to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add quartered figs to the simmering glaze. Cook for 5-7 minutes until figs soften and glaze thickens slightly. Remove thyme sprigs.
Bring stock to a simmer in a separate pot.
Gradually whisk in polenta. Cook, stirring constantly, for 3-5 minutes until thickened and creamy.
Stir in grated Parmesan and butter until melted and smooth. Season polenta with salt and pepper.
Toss asparagus with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast asparagus in the oven for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Spoon creamy polenta onto individual plates.
Arrange roasted asparagus alongside polenta.
Slice duck breasts into thick pieces.
Place duck pieces on the polenta.
Spoon fig balsamic glaze over the duck and polenta.
notes: Ensure duck breasts are scored well to render fat effectively, leading to crispy skin.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing duck; cook in batches if necessary.
Adjust cooking time for duck based on desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Tomato, Mozzarella, and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, whole and plump, rests prominently on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant medley of roasted cherry tomatoes, bright green broccoli florets, dark purple-black Kalamata olive halves, and creamy white torn fresh mozzarella pieces is artfully arranged. The tomatoes are slightly burst and caramelized, contrasting with the tender-crisp broccoli. The mozzarella pieces are soft and glistening. A few fresh, deep green basil leaves are scattered over the medley, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light drizzle of dark balsamic glaze subtly streaks across the plate, providing a refined finish. The overall composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing natural textures and colors. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a natural finish. Standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere with a minimalist background that highlights the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to sop up juices
Accompany with a glass of dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until softened and slightly caramelized.
While tomatoes roast, blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board.
In the same skillet (or a clean pan), add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté sliced garlic over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add blanched broccoli florets and roasted cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Sauté gently for 2-3 minutes to warm through.
Remove from heat. Gently fold in pitted and halved Kalamata olives and torn fresh mozzarella pieces. Mozzarella should slightly soften but not fully melt.
To plate, place one pan-seared chicken breast on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the warm tomato, broccoli, mozzarella, and olive medley alongside the chicken.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with balsamic glaze, if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken rests before serving to retain juiciness.
Mozzarella should be added off-heat to prevent it from fully melting and losing its shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece, positioned slightly off-center. Alongside the chicken are rustic, roasted potato wedges with reddish-brown skins, and vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes. Whole, soft roasted garlic cloves, their skins lightly browned, are scattered among the vegetables. A rich, glossy pan sauce, amber-hued from paprika, is lightly spooned over the chicken and vegetables. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a clean white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating a professional yet approachable culinary image.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful sauce
Pair with a glass of dry white wine or a light red wine
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. Halve cherry tomatoes. Peel and roughly chop onion.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potato wedges, chopped onion, and unpeeled garlic cloves. Season with salt and pepper. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened and fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Add chicken stock and cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them among the vegetables. Ensure chicken skin is above the liquid.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. Chicken skin should be crispy.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs adds maximum flavor and moisture.
Do not peel the garlic cloves; they become soft and sweet when roasted in their skins, easily squeezed out before eating.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Bell Pepper and Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender braised beef is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rich brown beef chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled among vibrant, substantial pieces of roasted red, yellow, and green bell peppers and softened golden onion wedges. A glossy, deep brown savory mustard sauce coats the beef and vegetables, with a slight pooling at the base. The dish has a robust, comforting appearance. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a bright green contrast. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional bistro-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes
Serve with wide egg noodles

ingredients.name: Bell peppers
ingredients.quantity: 3 (red, yellow, green), deseeded, cut into large chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add onion wedges to the pot. Sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
Add bell pepper chunks and minced garlic. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard and tomato paste. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Check occasionally and stir.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Provençal Tuna and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, neatly cut square portion of Provençal Tuna and Potato Bake is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bake features a golden-brown, slightly crisp top from the breadcrumbs and Parmesan. Visible layers along the cut edges reveal tender, pale yellow potato medallions, interspersed with flaked, pinkish-beige tuna, translucent slices of red onion, and deep purple-black halved olives, all bound by a rich, savory tomato-infused sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A set of standard silver flatware (fork and knife) rests beside the plate, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting with warm, even natural lighting that highlights the dish without distraction, creating an inviting and approachable restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette
Accompany with a crusty baguette to soak up the savory juices
Pair with a chilled glass of dry rosé wine
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes (2-3mm medallions). Boil in salted water for 5 minutes until slightly tender. Drain well.
Drain tuna, reserving the oil. Flake tuna into chunks.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add thinly sliced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce slightly.
Add vegetable broth and fresh thyme leaves. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
In the prepared baking dish, arrange a layer of par-cooked potato slices.
Crumble half of the flaked tuna over the potatoes. Sprinkle with half of the halved black olives.
Spoon half of the onion-tomato sauce over the tuna and olives.
Repeat layers: potatoes, remaining tuna, remaining olives, remaining sauce.
Top evenly with breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese. Drizzle with reserved tuna oil or a little fresh olive oil.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the top is golden brown and bubbly.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Tuna and Potato Hash
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Homestyle Tuna and Potato Hash is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The hash features an inviting mix of golden-brown, pan-fried potato cubes, tender flaked tuna, softened diced red onion, and halved dark black olives. The ingredients are casually mounded in the center of the plate, with some components naturally overlapping and touching, creating a rustic, comforting appearance. The hash is lightly seasoned with flecks of black pepper and vibrant green chopped fresh parsley scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a relaxed family kitchen setting. A simple, folded linen napkin and basic, sturdy cutlery are placed beside the plate. The lighting is soft and warm, enhancing the homely, inviting atmosphere, as if prepared for a casual weeknight dinner.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Place potato cubes in a pot. Cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook for 10-12 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain well.
While potatoes cook, finely dice the red onion.
Slice black olives in half.
Drain canned tuna, reserving the oil from one can. Flake the tuna gently with a fork.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the reserved tuna oil to the skillet. If more fat is needed, add a small splash of olive oil.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add drained potato cubes to the skillet. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are lightly browned and slightly crispy.
Add flaked tuna and sliced olives to the skillet. Stir gently to combine. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with the remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Tuna Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A generous, square slice of Hearty Tuna Potato Gratin sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The gratin reveals distinct, comforting layers: thinly sliced, creamy baked potatoes forming the base and top, interspersed with flaky chunks of light pink tuna, finely diced translucent onion, and dark, whole pitted black olives. The top layer of potatoes is golden-brown and slightly crispy, covered with bubbly, melted, golden-yellow cheddar cheese. The edges of the gratin slice are slightly browned, indicating a perfect bake. A few specks of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley are sprinkled casually over the top. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, showing natural grain. A plain, grey linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A single, sturdy silver fork is placed to the right of the plate, ready for a hearty meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Peel potatoes. Slice potatoes thinly, about 3 mm thick. Pat dry.
Drain tuna, reserving the oil. Flake tuna into large chunks.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add flour. Whisk for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually add milk, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Cook until sauce thickens.
Stir in minced garlic, half of the grated cheese, salt, and pepper. Cook until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.
Heat reserved tuna oil in a pan. Sauté diced onion until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Arrange a single layer of potato slices in the prepared baking dish. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Spread half of the flaked tuna over the potatoes. Scatter half of the sautéed onions and half of the pitted olives.
Pour one-third of the cheese sauce over the layer.
Repeat with another layer of potatoes, remaining tuna, onions, and olives. Pour another third of the cheese sauce.
Top with the remaining potato slices. Pour the final third of the cheese sauce evenly over the top.
Sprinkle remaining grated cheese over the gratin.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. If browning too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tuna Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A modest, inviting portion of rustic tuna potato gratin is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The gratin boasts a beautifully golden-brown and bubbly cheese crust, with edges showing a slightly crisp texture. Beneath the rich topping, tender, thinly sliced potato layers are visible, intertwined with flaky chunks of light pink tuna, dark halved black olives, and soft, translucent slivers of caramelized onion. The gratin maintains a comforting, slightly free-form shape. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley rests casually on top, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, natural kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere. A plain linen napkin and a simple fork are placed nearby, completing the homely scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 20x20cm baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season sliced potatoes with salt and pepper.

Arrange one-third of the potato slices in a single layer in the prepared baking dish. Top with half of the flaked tuna, half of the sautéed onion and garlic mixture, and half of the black olives. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated cheese.
Repeat the layer: another one-third of potatoes, the remaining tuna, onion-garlic mixture, and olives. Sprinkle with another one-third of the cheese.
Finish with the remaining potato slices on top.
Pour whole milk evenly over the layers. Press down gently to ensure potatoes are submerged.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the gratin is bubbly.
Remove from oven. Sprinkle the remaining one-third of cheese over the top. Return to oven for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is golden brown and bubbly.
Let the gratin rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra richness, use a mix of milk and light cream.
Ensure potatoes are sliced uniformly for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Pork Chops with Roasted Potatoes and Mustard
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in pork chop is centered on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The pork chop, cooked to a rich golden-brown, displays a slightly crisp exterior. Around the pork chop, a generous portion of roasted potato wedges, golden-crisp on the outside and fluffy within, are casually arranged. Thick, caramelized red onion wedges, soft and sweet, are nestled among the potatoes and pork. A few dark green sprigs of fresh rosemary are scattered naturally over the dish. The entire plate rests directly on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A casually folded beige linen napkin and a silver fork are placed to the left of the plate. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges. Slice onion into thick wedges. Mince garlic.
Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Spread Dijon mustard evenly over both sides of each pork chop.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, and rosemary sprigs. Toss well to coat.
Arrange seasoned pork chops among the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Pour chicken stock into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown. Flip pork chops halfway through if desired for even browning.
Remove from oven. Let pork rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Fillet with Creamy Dijon Sauce and Potato Rosti
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick, seared pork fillet chunks beside a golden-brown, crispy potato rosti on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork has a deep, caramelized crust, revealing a tender interior. A generous pour of creamy, pale yellow Dijon sauce cascades over the pork, pooling elegantly. The potato rosti is round, with visible strands of grated potato forming a beautiful, textured surface, indicating its crispness. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley adds a pop of green and freshness atop the pork and sauce. Plating is clean and professional, with appropriate negative space, presenting a refined yet approachable single individual portion. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Grate coarsely. Place grated potatoes in a clean cloth. Squeeze out excess moisture completely. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add grated potatoes. Press down to form a flat cake. Cook 8-10 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Keep warm.

Pat pork fillet dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a separate oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork fillet 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown crust forms.

Transfer pan with pork to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast 10-15 minutes until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Remove from oven. Rest pork on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5-7 minutes.
While pork rests, return the pan used for searing pork to medium heat. Add butter. Sauté minced shallot 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by one-third. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

Cut rested pork fillet into thick chunks. Place 2-3 pork chunks on each plate. Arrange a portion of potato rosti beside the pork. Spoon creamy Dijon sauce generously over the pork. Garnish with chopped fresh chives or parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Fillet with Mustard Potato Purée and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork fillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two to three thick, golden-brown seared pork medallions, exhibiting a tender, light pink interior, are neatly arranged to one side. Beside them, a generous, smooth quenelle of creamy, pale yellow mustard potato purée rests. Scattered around the plate are vibrant green, tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets, some displaying slight charring. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green chives over the pork and purée, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing distinct textures and colors. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut broccoli into florets. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp, with slight charring.
Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot saucepan over low heat for 1 minute to dry.
Mash potatoes with butter and warm milk until smooth. Stir in Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat pork fillet dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork fillet on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through and tender.
Remove pork from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Slice pork into thick medallions, approximately 2-3 cm thick.

Spoon a generous dollop of mustard potato purée onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 pork medallions beside the purée. Place roasted broccoli florets around the pork and purée. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.
notes: Resting the pork after cooking ensures it remains juicy and tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Fermented Mustard Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Pork Loin is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy, natural tone, such as cream or beige. The plate, with its subtle texture, rests on a light-colored reclaimed wood table surface. Two thick, golden-brown pan-seared pork loin medallions, cooked to a tender interior, are arranged slightly offset on one side of the plate. A glistening, slightly rustic fermented mustard glaze is spooned generously over the pork, catching the soft natural light. Alongside the pork, several roasted potato wedges, with their skins on and a light golden crust, are loosely clustered. Interspersed among the potatoes are vibrant green charred broccoli florets and tender, slightly browned broccoli stem slices, showcasing a zero-waste approach. A few fresh rosemary leaves or thyme sprigs are scattered subtly for a hint of green. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded simply beside the plate. The background is uncluttered, hinting at natural elements like soft plants or a simple wall, maintaining focus on the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, smashed garlic, and rosemary/thyme. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes.
While potatoes roast, trim broccoli. Cut florets into bite-sized pieces. Peel and slice broccoli stems into 1 cm thick rounds.
Season pork loin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan with pork to the preheated oven. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Add broccoli florets and stem slices to the baking tray with potatoes. Toss lightly with pan drippings or a touch more oil. Roast for the last 10-15 minutes of pork cooking, until tender-crisp and lightly charred.
