Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil (or the infused oil) to the pot. Brown chicken cubes in batches until lightly golden. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced carrot to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in the ancho chile paste, crushed tomatoes, and bay leaf. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Pour in chicken broth. Add diced potatoes and browned chicken cubes. Bring the soup to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished generously with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Silken Egg Crémeux, Spun Sugar 'Vermicelli', Yuzu Gel, and Yuzu Oil Pearls
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated dessert is artfully plated on an expensive bone china plate with abundant white space. A perfectly smooth, pale yellow Silken Egg Crémeux forms an organic dollop, positioned slightly off-center. Perched delicately atop the crémeux is a translucent, golden nest of finely spun sugar 'vermicelli', catching the light. Around the crémeux, vibrant yellow droplets of tart yuzu gel are precisely placed, alongside glistening, spherical yuzu oil pearls providing textural contrast and citrus burst. A single sprig of bright green micro-mint offers a pop of color and subtle aroma. The minimalist, architectural composition highlights texture and color harmony. The plate rests on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality. A precisely folded white linen napkin completes the elegant presentation.
instructions: Prepare Calcium Chloride Bath: Dissolve 2.5 g calcium chloride in 500 ml distilled water. Stir until clear. Set aside.

Prepare Silken Egg Crémeux: Whisk egg yolks and 70 g sugar until pale. Heat cream and vanilla bean paste in a saucepan until simmering. Gradually whisk hot cream into egg mixture. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon (82-84°C). Do not boil. Strain crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl set over an ice bath. Stir until cool. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill 4 hours or overnight.

Prepare Spun Sugar 'Vermicelli': Combine 150 g sugar, 50 ml water, and glucose syrup in a small saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Stop stirring. Bring to a boil. Cook until syrup reaches 160°C (320°F). Remove from heat. Dip a whisk or fork into hot syrup. Drizzle fine threads rapidly over a lightly oiled broom handle or similar elevated surface, allowing threads to fall onto a clean surface below. Gather spun sugar into small, delicate nests or bundles. Work quickly as it hardens.

Prepare Yuzu Gel: Combine yuzu juice, 20 g sugar, and agar-agar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm. Once firm, blend gel until smooth in a high-speed blender. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.

Prepare Yuzu Oil Pearls (Reverse Spherification): Create Yuzu Alginate Base: Whisk 0.5 g sodium alginate into 100 ml yuzu juice until completely dissolved and no lumps remain. Let stand 1 hour to remove air bubbles. Fill a syringe or dropper with the yuzu alginate base. Carefully drop small spheres into the calcium chloride bath. Allow pearls to set for 1-2 minutes. Gently remove pearls with a slotted spoon. Rinse briefly in a bowl of fresh water. Drain well. Store in a small amount of neutral oil.

Assemble Dish: Place a dollop of chilled Silken Egg Crémeux slightly off-center on a white plate. Carefully place a nest of Spun Sugar 'Vermicelli' on top of the crémeux. Artistically dot small amounts of Yuzu Gel around the crémeux. Arrange a few Yuzu Oil Pearls around the plate. Garnish with a single sprig of micro-mint or basil cress. Serve immediately.
notes: Precision is key for this dish. Ensure all components are chilled to optimal temperature before plating.
Work quickly with spun sugar as it is delicate and sensitive to humidity.
For spherification, ensure the sodium alginate solution is completely free of bubbles for perfect pearls.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple Streusel Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly baked Apple Streusel Tartlet rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The tartlet's shortcrust pastry is a rich golden-brown, with gently crimped edges. The apple filling peeks through the gaps in the streusel, showing tender, pale yellow apple cubes. The streusel topping is a golden-brown, crumbly texture, scattered generously over the apples. The tartlet is presented whole, showcasing its individual portion size. The plate is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a plain metal fork are casually placed beside the plate. The background is slightly blurred, showing the relaxed, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dollop of crème fraîche on the side
Serve with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Prepare pastry dough: In a large bowl, combine 200g flour, 30g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add 100g cold butter cubes. Cut butter into flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs. Add egg yolk and 30ml cold water. Mix until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap in plastic, and chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare apple filling: Peel, core, and dice apples into small cubes (about 1 cm). In a bowl, toss diced apples with 50g sugar, 5g cinnamon, 15ml lemon juice, and 10g cornstarch.
Prepare streusel: In a separate bowl, combine 75g flour, 50g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add 40g cold butter cubes. Rub butter into dry ingredients with fingertips until coarse crumbs form.

Assemble tartlets: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease four 10 cm tartlet molds. On a lightly floured surface, roll out chilled pastry dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut out four circles large enough to line the molds. Gently press dough into molds. Trim excess dough.
Fill and top: Divide apple filling evenly among the four pastry-lined molds. Sprinkle streusel topping generously over the apples.
Bake: Place tartlets on a baking sheet. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and apples are tender.
Cool: Let tartlets cool in molds for 10 minutes before carefully removing them to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Ensure butter is very cold for both pastry and streusel for best texture.
Do not overwork the pastry dough to keep it tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato Rosti with Pork Sausage Mousse, Whipped Fromage Blanc, and Aged Cheddar Crisp
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve meticulously crafted canapés are artfully arranged on a large, pristine white Carrara marble platter. Each canapé features a perfectly round, golden-brown crispy potato rosti as its base, approximately 5cm in diameter. On top of each rosti, a delicate, pale pink quenelle of smooth pork sausage mousse is precisely piped. Adjacent to the mousse, a small, pearlescent white dollop of whipped fromage blanc provides a creamy counterpoint. A thin, translucent, golden-amber aged cheddar crisp stands elegantly upright, adding architectural height and a contrasting texture. Each canapé is subtly garnished with a few vibrant green micro-chives, adding a precise touch of color. The arrangement on the platter is organic and flowing, with generous negative space between each piece, emphasizing their individual perfection. The scene is bathed in dramatic, soft professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests in the background on the minimalist marble surface.
instructions: Grate peeled potatoes coarsely. Place grated potato in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze firmly to remove excess moisture. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 10g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Place small mounds (approx. 20g each) of grated potato into the pan. Press gently to form small, round rostis, about 5cm diameter. Cook 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a wire rack lined with paper towel. Keep warm.
In a small pan, heat 5ml olive oil. Sauté minced shallot and garlic until translucent. Cool slightly.

In a food processor, combine pork sausage meat, sautéed shallot and garlic, minced thyme, egg white, and heavy cream. Process until very smooth. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a piping bag with a plain round tip.

Place cottage cheese in a fine-mesh sieve over a bowl for 15 minutes to drain excess liquid. Transfer drained cottage cheese to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Season with a pinch of salt. Transfer to a small piping bag with a small plain tip.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle small, even mounds (approx. 5g each) of grated cheddar onto the parchment, leaving space between each. Bake 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and lacy. Remove from oven. Let cool completely on the baking sheet to crisp up. Carefully peel off.

On each warm potato rosti, pipe a small, elegant quenelle or rosette of pork sausage mousse. Pipe a small dollop of whipped fromage blanc next to the mousse. Carefully insert one aged cheddar crisp upright into the mousse or fromage blanc. Garnish each canapé with a few snipped chives. Arrange 8-12 pieces artfully on a large serving platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Loaded Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of hearty loaded potato bake rests in an everyday ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The potato bake is a creamy, golden-brown mound, with visible crispy bacon bits and bright yellow corn kernels. A generous dollop of cool, white sour cream tops it, slightly melting into the warm potatoes. Beside the bowl, a small pile of freshly diced green cucumber cubes and a few torn corn tortilla triangles offer contrasting crunch. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and basic fork are casually placed nearby. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on comfort and natural textures, with no artificial arrangements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
While potatoes cook, cut bacon into small pieces. Cook bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Reserve 1 tablespoon of bacon fat.
Drain cooked potatoes. Return to the hot pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked bacon, half of the shredded cheese, and frozen corn to the mashed potatoes. Stir to combine.
Spoon the potato mixture into a small oven-safe dish or two individual ramekins. Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and potatoes are heated through.
While bake cooks, dice cucumber into small cubes.
Cut tortillas into triangles or strips. Briefly toast them in a dry pan or microwave for added crispness if desired.
Serve hot. Top each portion with a dollop of sour cream. Serve with diced cucumber and tortilla pieces on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken Roulade with Asparagus-Corn Farce, Clear Tomato-Bell Pepper Consommé, and Olive Soil
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely composed portion rests on an elegant, oversized white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. The plate is centered on a polished white Carrara marble surface. Two thick, perfectly pan-roasted chicken roulade medallions, displaying their golden-brown exterior and revealing the vibrant green asparagus and pale yellow corn within, are artfully arranged in a flowing, natural composition. They are not fanned but presented as substantial, distinct pieces. A small, clear, ruby-red pool of delicate tomato-bell pepper consommé gleams beside the chicken, reflecting the soft, dramatic professional lighting. Precisely scattered around the chicken and consommé is a dark, crumbly olive soil, offering a textural contrast. A delicate, golden-orange chili-cheddar tuile, thin and crisp, stands elegantly beside the chicken, adding a subtle architectural element and a hint of warmth. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the pristine quality and precise execution of each element. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits to the left. The background is ultra-minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole, captivating focus.

ingredients.name: hot sauce powder or cayenne pepper

instructions: Prepare the Asparagus-Corn Farce: Blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice water. Drain and pat dry. Cut asparagus into small dice. In a small pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced asparagus and corn kernels. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Deglaze with white wine. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool completely.

Prepare the Chicken Roulades: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound gently with a meat mallet to an even 5mm thickness. Spread an even layer of the cooled asparagus-corn farce over each chicken breast, leaving a 1cm border. Carefully roll each chicken breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine at intervals.

Sear and Roast Chicken Roulades: Preheat oven to 180°C. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 5 minutes. Remove kitchen twine before slicing.

Prepare the Clear Tomato-Bell Pepper Consommé: Combine chopped tomatoes, red bell pepper, shallot, garlic, basil, and cold water in a blender. Blend until smooth. Pour mixture into a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth set over a bowl. Do not press the solids. Let it drip slowly for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight in the refrigerator, to collect the clear consommé. Discard solids. Gently heat the clear consommé in a small saucepan. Do not boil. Season with white wine vinegar and salt to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare the Olive Soil: Preheat oven to 150°C. Roughly chop pitted Kalamata olives. In a small bowl, combine chopped olives, panko breadcrumbs, and olive oil. Spread mixture thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until crisp and crumbly. Let cool.

Prepare the Chili-Cheddar Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat. Sprinkle small, thin circles (about 4-5cm diameter) of grated cheddar cheese onto the prepared sheet. Sprinkle a tiny pinch of hot sauce powder or cayenne pepper on each circle. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown at the edges. Remove from oven. Let cool slightly on the baking sheet, then carefully transfer to a wire rack to crisp up completely.

Assemble and Plate: Slice each rested chicken roulade into 2-3 thick medallions. Arrange 2-3 medallions artfully on each plate, slightly off-center, allowing for abundant negative space. Spoon a small, clear pool of warm tomato-bell pepper consommé next to the chicken or slightly underneath. Sprinkle a precise amount of olive soil around the chicken. Place one or two chili-cheddar tuiles delicately on the plate, either leaning against the chicken or flat beside it. Serve immediately.
notes: For best consommé clarity, allow it to drip undisturbed overnight in the refrigerator.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C for food safety. Use a meat thermometer.
The chili-cheddar tuiles should be very thin and crisp; watch them carefully while baking as they can burn quickly.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Bacon Pasta with Toasted Almonds
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Creamy Tomato Bacon Pasta is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce. Interspersed throughout the pasta are golden-brown, crispy bacon chunks and tender, thinly sliced caramelized onions. The dish is generously garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh coriander and light brown toasted slivered almonds, providing contrasting colors and textures. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the pasta as the main subject. Standard polished silver flatware is placed neatly beside the bowl. A folded light gray cotton napkin rests to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Cut bacon into 2 cm chunks. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bacon chunks. Cook until crispy and golden. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 30 ml bacon fat in the skillet.
Thinly slice the onion. Add sliced onion to the skillet with bacon fat. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are deeply caramelized, about 15-20 minutes.
Peel and grate ginger. Add grated ginger to the caramelized onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, coconut milk, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of sugar. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
While sauce simmers, toast slivered almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown and fragrant. Set aside.

Add cooked pasta and reserved bacon chunks to the sauce. Add 60 ml of reserved pasta water. Toss well to coat the pasta. If sauce is too thick, add more pasta water, 15 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Grate lemon zest directly into the pasta. Squeeze 15 ml lemon juice into the pasta. Stir to combine. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Roughly chop fresh coriander. Serve pasta immediately. Garnish each serving with toasted slivered almonds and fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot and Onion Vinagrete Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a deep, everyday ceramic bowl, showcasing its vibrant, natural colors. Shredded carrots, a bright orange, are the dominant visual, intertwined with translucent, thinly sliced white onion. The vegetables are coated in a glistening, light golden vinaigrette, pooling slightly at the bottom. Fresh, dark green chopped parsley is sprinkled throughout, adding flecks of color. The arrangement is casual and abundant, with vegetables naturally piled high, suggesting a generous home-cooked portion. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple white ceramic plate and standard flatware. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comfortable atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside grilled meats like picanha or churrasco.
Accompany with white rice and feijão (beans).
Serve as part of a typical Brazilian lunch buffet (comida por quilo).
instructions: Shred carrots using a box grater or food processor.
Thinly slice the onion.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded carrots and sliced onion.
For the vinagrete dressing, whisk together olive oil, white wine vinegar, water, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over the carrot and onion mixture.
Toss gently to coat all vegetables evenly.
Let salad rest for 15 minutes for flavors to meld.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bean and Corn Creamy Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of creamy Bean and Corn Salad is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The salad features soft black beans and bright yellow corn kernels, coated in a rich mayonnaise dressing. Finely diced red onion, chopped fresh parsley, and chives are mixed in, adding vibrant color and texture. Grated parmesan cheese is lightly sprinkled over the top. The components are naturally arranged, showcasing a comforting, homestyle appearance. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, under warm kitchen lighting. A traditional Brazilian setting is suggested by a casual fabric napkin and simple flatware, evoking a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a side dish with rice and beans, feijoada, or grilled meats (churrasco).
Often served as part of a 'prato feito' (daily special plate).
instructions: Drain and rinse black beans thoroughly.
Drain corn kernels.
Finely dice red onion.
Chop fresh parsley and chives.
In a large bowl, combine drained black beans, drained corn, diced red onion, chopped parsley, and chopped chives.
Add mayonnaise, grated parmesan, white wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper.
Mix all ingredients gently until well combined and coated.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Vegan Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy vegan mushroom tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tagliatelle is neatly coiled in the center, generously coated in a lustrous, pale ivory cashew cream sauce. Slices of seared cremini and shiitake mushrooms, varying in earthy brown tones, are interspersed throughout the pasta, along with vibrant green, wilted spinach leaves. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space, showcasing the rich texture of the sauce and the distinct shapes of the ingredients. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A polished silver fork with pasta coiled around it is positioned to the left of the plate. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting.
instructions: Soak cashews in hot water for at least 30 minutes. Drain well.
Cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Blend soaked cashews, vegetable broth, nutritional yeast, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy. Use a high-speed blender for best results.
Pour cashew cream into the skillet with mushrooms. Stir to combine.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the skillet. Toss to coat pasta evenly with sauce.
Add spinach. Cook until spinach wilts, about 2-3 minutes.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Гречневая Каша с Колбасками и Яйцом
recipes.special_requests: Сделай очень вкусно и напиши рецепт на русском языке
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of golden-brown buckwheat kasha is mounded naturally on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Four pan-fried sausages, with their casings slightly crisped and interiors plump, are arranged casually around and nestled into the kasha. A perfectly fried egg, with a runny, vibrant yellow yolk and slightly crispy edges, rests directly on top of the buckwheat. Generous shavings of light yellow cheese are scattered over the kasha and sausages, melting slightly from the warmth. Fresh, vibrant green spearmint leaves and delicate pea shoots are casually sprinkled over the entire dish, adding pops of fresh color and texture. The presentation is homely and inviting, as if served directly from a family kitchen. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting appeal of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Часто подается с солеными огурцами или простым свежим салатом.
Лучше всего наслаждаться теплым, при желании можно добавить ложку сметаны.
instructions: Гречневую крупу промойте. Положите в кастрюлю.
Добавьте 600 мл воды и щепотку соли. Доведите до кипения.
Уменьшите огонь до минимума. Накройте крышкой. Варите 15-20 минут, пока вода не впитается.
Снимите с огня. Добавьте сливочное масло, если используете. Перемешайте. Оставьте под крышкой на 5 минут.
Колбаски обжарьте на растительном масле до золотистой корочки и готовности. Это займет 10-12 минут. Переворачивайте колбаски для равномерной обжарки.
Выньте колбаски из сковороды.
В той же сковороде пожарьте яйца до желаемой степени готовности. Желток может быть жидким.
Сыр натрите на крупной терке.
Мяту мелко нарежьте.
На каждую тарелку выложите порцию гречневой каши.
Рядом или сверху положите обжаренные колбаски.
Сверху на кашу положите жареное яйцо.
Посыпьте тертым сыром.
Добавьте свежую мяту и гороховые ростки.
Посыпьте свежемолотым черным перцем. Подавайте немедленно.

recipes.recipe_name: Гречневая каша с колбасой и яйцом
recipes.special_requests: Сделай очень вкусно и напиши рецепт на русском языке
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic individual portion of Buckwheat Kasha with Sausage and Egg, presented on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with a natural off-white glaze. The cooked buckwheat groats are fluffy and separate, showcasing their natural light brown color, interspersed generously with irregularly cut, browned sausage chunks and small cubes of sautéed onion and grated carrot. The dish is topped with a perfectly fried sunny-side-up egg, its bright yellow yolk slightly runny, contrasting with the firm white. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped dill rests over the egg and buckwheat. The components are naturally piled in the center of the plate, allowing some negative space around the edges. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its grain and minor imperfections. Nearby, a simple fork and spoon, along with a casually folded cloth napkin, complete the homely setting. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with pickled cucumbers (соленые огурцы) or sauerkraut (квашеная капуста) on the side.
Offer a dollop of sour cream (сметана).
Enjoy with rye bread (ржаной хлеб).
instructions: Промойте гречневую крупу под холодной водой до прозрачности.
Нарежьте лук мелкими кубиками.
Натрите морковь на крупной терке.
Нарежьте колбасу небольшими кубиками или толстыми ломтиками.
Разогрейте растительное масло в большой кастрюле или глубокой сковороде на среднем огне.
Добавьте нарезанный лук. Обжаривайте до прозрачности, около 3-5 минут.
Добавьте натертую морковь. Обжаривайте еще 3-4 минуты до размягчения.
Добавьте колбасу в кастрюлю. Готовьте до легкого зарумянивания, около 5-7 минут, периодически помешивая.
Добавьте промытую гречневую крупу в кастрюлю. Хорошо перемешайте с колбасой и овощами. Обжаривайте 1-2 минуты, помешивая.
Влейте 400 мл горячей воды в кастрюлю. Добавьте соль и черный перец по вкусу. Доведите до кипения.
Уменьшите огонь до минимума. Плотно накройте кастрюлю крышкой. Тушите 15-20 минут, или пока вся вода не впитается и гречка не станет мягкой. Не перемешивайте во время приготовления.
Снимите с огня. Дайте постоять под крышкой 5 минут.
Тем временем, пожарьте 4 яйца глазуньей или сделайте яичницу-болтунью на отдельной сковороде.
Разрыхлите гречку вилкой.
Разложите гречку с колбасой и овощами по индивидуальным тарелкам.
Выложите по одному жареному яйцу на каждую порцию.
Посыпьте свежим укропом или петрушкой, если желаете.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut-Banana Entremet, Toasted Walnut Praline
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, single-portion entremet stands centered on a round, white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The entremet features a flawless, glossy, opaque white coconut mirror glaze, reflecting light subtly. The sides are sharply defined, revealing the precise architectural layers within: a light golden coconut dacquoise base, a creamy pale yellow banana crémeux core, and a surrounding cloud-like white coconut mousse. The base of the entremet is encircled by a delicate ring of finely crushed, golden-brown toasted walnut praline, adding textural contrast. A single, thin, crispy banana chip is elegantly placed upright on top, beside a perfectly toasted walnut half. Abundant negative space surrounds the entremet, emphasizing its clean lines and refined presentation. The plate rests on a polished white marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the dessert's sculptural form. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed beside the plate.

ingredients.name: For the Toasted Walnut Praline Crunch

instructions: Prepare Coconut Dacquoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add granulated sugar, whip to stiff, glossy peaks. Gently fold in sifted powdered sugar, ground walnuts, desiccated coconut, and flour. Spread batter thinly on prepared tray. Bake 10-12 minutes until light golden. Cool completely. Cut into 4 discs using a desired mold size.

Prepare Banana Crémeux: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, whisk banana puree, egg yolks, and sugar. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin and lime juice. Let cool to 40°C. Add cold butter, blend with an immersion blender until smooth and emulsified. Pour into a small mold or piping bag. Freeze until firm.

Prepare Coconut Mousse: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. Gently heat coconut cream and sugar until sugar dissolves. Stir in squeezed gelatin. Let cool to room temperature. Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold whipped cream into the coconut cream mixture until smooth. Transfer to a piping bag.
Assemble Entremets (Layer 1): Place a dacquoise disc at the bottom of 4 individual entremet molds. Pipe a thin layer of coconut mousse over the dacquoise.

Assemble Entremets (Layer 2): Place a frozen banana crémeux insert (smaller than the mold) onto the mousse layer. Pipe more coconut mousse to fill the mold, ensuring no air pockets. Smooth the top. Freeze thoroughly, at least 6 hours or overnight.

Prepare Toasted Walnut Praline Crunch: Toast walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant. In a saucepan, combine sugar and water. Cook to a light amber caramel (165°C). Add toasted walnuts, stir to coat. Pour onto parchment paper. Cool completely. Once hard, break into pieces. Blend in a food processor until a fine crumb. Do not over-process to paste. Mix with feuilletine.

Prepare Coconut Mirror Glaze: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, combine glucose syrup, condensed milk, and water. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Add chopped white chocolate, squeezed gelatin, coconut extract, and titanium dioxide (if using). Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles, until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool to 30-32°C for glazing.

Glaze Entremets: Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack over a tray. Pour mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Transfer carefully to a serving plate.

Garnish: Carefully press the toasted walnut praline crunch around the base of each entremet. Garnish the top with a thin banana chip and a toasted walnut half. Serve immediately or refrigerate briefly.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin with Chicken-Parmesan Croquettes and Red Curry Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick medallion of seared beef tenderloin, exhibiting a deep mahogany crust and a rosy medium-rare interior, rests on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, two slender, golden-crisp chicken-parmesan croquettes are artfully positioned. A lustrous, deep red-brown red curry jus forms a delicate, organic pool. Scattered alongside are a few delicate, translucent pink pickled shallot rings, providing a sharp color contrast. A small sprig of vibrant green cilantro provides a final touch. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate is set on a grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision against an ultra-minimalist background, highlighting sophisticated simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an individual main course on a refined dining plate.
Present with elegant flatware.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Shallots: Thinly slice 1 shallot into rings. Combine 50ml rice vinegar, 50ml water, 1 tbsp sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, then pour over shallots. Cool and set aside.

Prepare Red Curry Jus: Mince 1 shallot and 3 cloves garlic. Sauté in a saucepan with a splash of oil until fragrant. Add red curry paste; cook for 1 minute until aromatic. Pour in coconut milk and beef stock. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, reducing by half. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth jus. Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken-Parmesan Croquettes: Poach chicken breast in simmering water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Finely dice the cooked chicken. In a bowl, combine diced chicken with finely grated Parmesan and egg yolk. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.

Form the chicken mixture into 8 small, slender cylinders, approximately 5cm long. Dredge each cylinder in flour, then lightly moisten, then roll in panko breadcrumbs until fully coated. Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry croquettes until golden brown and crisp on all sides. Drain on paper towels.

Prepare Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef tenderloin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat vegetable oil in an oven-safe pan over high heat. Sear beef on all sides until a deep, caramelized crust forms. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook until internal temperature reaches 55-60°C (131-140°F) for medium-rare. Remove from oven, add butter to the pan, and baste the beef. Rest beef for 10 minutes before slicing into 4 thick, individual portions or serving as whole pieces.

To Serve: Spoon a small, artistic pool or sweep of the red curry jus onto each pristine white bone china plate. Place one seared beef tenderloin portion beside the jus. Artfully arrange two golden-crisp chicken-parmesan croquettes on the plate. Garnish with a few delicate, translucent pink pickled shallot rings and a small sprig of fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous-Vide Beef Tenderloin, Black Garlic, Potato Pavé
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated portion is presented on a pristine, large round bone china plate with a subtle, delicate rim, set on a dark, polished wooden table. The backdrop is minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space. A perfectly seared, thick beef tenderloin medallion, cooked to a tender medium-rare, anchors the composition. Its exterior boasts a rich, dark brown crust. Adjacent to the beef, a precisely cut, golden-brown potato pavé, with visibly crisp layers, adds textural contrast. A small, artistic swoosh of deep black garlic puree provides a striking visual accent and umami depth. A glistening, rich beef demi-glace forms a small, dark pool near the beef. A few vibrant, finely sliced chive batons are meticulously placed atop the beef. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that highlight the textures and elevate the dish's sophisticated simplicity. A neatly folded, crisp white linen napkin rests beside the plate.
instructions: Prepare Potato Pavé: Peel potatoes. Slice potatoes into 2 mm thick rounds using a mandoline. Melt 50 g butter. Layer potato slices tightly in a buttered 20x10 cm baking dish. Brush each layer with melted butter. Season with salt and pepper every few layers. Press firmly. Bake at 160°C for 90 minutes, or until tender. Place a heavy weight on top. Chill overnight. Once chilled, cut into four precise 5x5 cm square pavés. Reserve.

Prepare Black Garlic Puree: Place black garlic in a small blender. Add 10 ml olive oil and 20 ml water. Blend until completely smooth. If too thick, add water sparingly until a pipeable consistency is achieved. Season lightly with salt. Reserve in a piping bag.

Prepare Beef Tenderloin: Season beef tenderloin generously with sea salt and black pepper. Place beef in a vacuum-sealable bag with two thyme sprigs and 20 g butter. Vacuum seal. Cook in a preheated water bath at 54°C for 2 hours for medium-rare.

Sear Beef Tenderloin: Remove beef from bag. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat 20 ml olive oil and remaining 30 g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until butter foams. Add beef. Sear all sides until deep golden brown and crusted, about 2-3 minutes per side. Add remaining thyme sprigs to the pan. Baste beef constantly with the foaming butter. Remove beef from pan. Rest on a wire rack for 10 minutes.

Crisp Potato Pavé: While beef rests, heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a splash of olive oil. Add chilled potato pavés. Sear until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.

Plate Dish: Cut the rested beef tenderloin into four thick medallions, approximately 150g each. Place one beef medallion slightly off-center on each warm plate. Position one crispy potato pavé next to the beef. Pipe a small, artful dot or swoosh of black garlic puree near the beef. Spoon a small pool of warm beef demi-glace onto the plate, near the beef. Garnish with a few delicate chive batons. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Caramelized Shallot Salad with Chili-Lime Glaze
recipes.visual_description: The salad is artfully composed on a pristine, wide-rimmed bone china plate, leaving ample negative space for an ultra-minimalist aesthetic. Roasted heirloom tomato wedges and halved cherry tomatoes, exhibiting vibrant reds and oranges, are interspersed with glistening, deeply caramelized shallot petals in a natural, flowing arrangement. A glossy, dark amber chili-lime glaze, derived from reduced beef stock, is artfully drizzled over and around the components, catching the light. The textures are a sophisticated interplay of soft, yielding tomatoes and tender-sweet shallots. Each plate is precisely garnished with a few emerald green sprigs of fresh cilantro and delicate mint leaves, providing a sharp color contrast and aromatic lift. The presentation exudes understated elegance, set against a polished white Carrara marble surface with dramatic, focused lighting creating soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity. Elegant, simple flatware rests beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally, Thai meals are a communal experience; however, this fine-dining salad is presented as an individual starter. It can be accompanied by a small portion of steamed jasmine rice if desired, to balance the bold flavors.

ingredients.name: Thai bird's eye chilies, finely minced

instructions: Reduce beef stock: Pour 500ml beef stock into a saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce until syrupy, about 60ml. This takes 20-30 minutes. Set aside.

Prepare tomatoes: Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut heirloom tomatoes into irregular wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 180°C for 10-12 minutes. They should be slightly softened but hold shape. Let cool slightly.

Caramelize shallots: Thinly slice shallots into rings. Heat 30ml neutral oil in a pan over low heat. Add shallots. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring often. Cook until deep golden brown and very soft. Season with a pinch of salt.

Make glaze: Combine reduced beef stock, minced chilies, lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and minced garlic in a small bowl. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust for balance: sweet, sour, salty, spicy.
Assemble salad: Gently combine roasted tomatoes and caramelized shallots in a mixing bowl. Pour half of the chili-lime glaze over. Toss gently to coat.
Plate: Arrange salad artfully on four individual plates. Create organic, flowing compositions. Drizzle remaining glaze over and around the salad. Garnish with fresh cilantro sprigs and mint leaves.
notes: Ensure the beef stock is of high quality for the best depth of flavor in the glaze.
Adjust chili quantity to personal preference for heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Potato and Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A modest, single portion of Cheesy Potato and Tomato Bake is served on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate. The dish showcases natural layers of tender, thinly sliced potato, some with lightly browned edges. Melted, bubbly, golden-brown cheddar cheese forms a comforting crust on top, with some edges slightly crispy. Soft, diced tomatoes and thinly sliced onions are nestled between and around the potato layers, their natural colors visible. The components touch and slightly overlap, creating a hearty, casual arrangement. A scattering of fresh green chopped parsley or chives adds a touch of color. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A casual, perhaps checkered, cloth napkin is loosely placed nearby. The scene is lit with warm, cozy light, evoking a lived-in family kitchen with subtle, blurred background elements suggesting a homely environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes, about 3-4 mm thick. Slice onions thinly. Mince garlic. Dice tomatoes into 1-2 cm chunks. Grate cheese.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or baking dish over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Sauté until softened and lightly golden, 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove half of the tomato-onion mixture from the skillet.
Arrange half of the sliced potatoes in a single layer over the remaining mixture in the skillet.
Sprinkle with half of the grated cheese.
Spread the reserved tomato-onion mixture over the cheese layer.
Arrange the remaining potato slices over the tomato-onion layer.
Pour vegetable broth or water over the potatoes.
Cover the skillet or dish with foil. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove foil. Sprinkle remaining cheese over the top.
Bake uncovered for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead of time and reheated.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Duck Breast with Provençal Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the Seared Duck Breast with Provençal Rice Pilaf is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The rice pilaf, a warm medley of tender long-grain rice, finely diced red bell pepper, diced onion, and small cubes of tomato, is mounded organically on one side of the plate, its natural beige and red hues visible. Nestled beside the rice are several thick medallions of seared duck breast, their skin deeply golden and crisp, contrasting with the tender, rosy pink interior. A few small sprigs of fresh thyme are scattered over the duck and rice, adding a touch of green. The arrangement is casual and inviting, as if served directly from a home kitchen. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and minor imperfections. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed next to the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft lighting, evoking a cozy family dinner atmosphere. A basic, sturdy fork and knife, typical of everyday flatware, are positioned beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Accompany with a crusty baguette.
instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crisscross pattern. Season with salt and pepper.
Place duck breast skin-side down in a cold pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes. Skin should be crispy and golden.
Flip duck. Sear flesh side for 3-5 minutes for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove duck from pan. Rest for 5 minutes. Pour off excess duck fat, reserving a small amount.
In the same pan with a little duck fat or olive oil, sauté diced onion and diced bell pepper for 5-7 minutes. Vegetables should soften.
Add minced garlic and diced tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in rice and Herbs de Provence. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff rice with a fork. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested duck breast into thick medallions.
Plate rice pilaf. Arrange duck medallions alongside. Garnish with fresh herbs.
notes: Duck fat rendered from the breast can be saved for other cooking.
Adjust duck cooking time for desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Duck Stew Provençal with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic individual portion of Duck Stew Provençal is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The braised duck leg, rich golden-brown, is nestled amongst vibrant, tender vegetables. Thick strips of red and yellow bell peppers, roughly chopped onions, and diced tomatoes create a colorful medley, coated in a glossy, savory, reddish-brown sauce. Bright green, crisp-tender green beans are interspersed throughout. A small, fluffy mound of plain white rice sits neatly alongside, ready to absorb the rich flavors. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, chopped green parsley. The presentation is warm, inviting, and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene. A simple, silver fork and knife rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette for soaking up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat duck legs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear duck legs skin-side down until golden brown and fat renders, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 5 minutes. Remove duck from pot.
Pour off excess fat, leaving about 30 ml in the pot.
Add chopped onion and bell pepper strips to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes, stock, herbs de Provence, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return duck legs to the pot. Ensure they are mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until duck is very tender.
Meanwhile, cook rice according to package directions.
Add green beans to the stew during the last 15 minutes of cooking. Stir gently.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve duck stew hot with a side of rice. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hawaiian Sausage & Egg Sliders
recipes.visual_description: A clean white rectangular ceramic platter holds four Hawaiian Sausage & Egg Sliders, each perfectly portioned as a sophisticated finger food. The golden-brown Hawaiian bread rolls are lightly toasted, their glossy tops contrasting with the soft, fluffy pale yellow scrambled eggs nestled within. A round, well-browned sausage patty sits atop the egg, its savory richness evident. Beneath, a vibrant red, thin slice of ripe tomato adds a fresh, juicy element, crowned by a single, bright green basil leaf that provides a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The sliders are arranged in a neat row, slightly staggered, allowing for moderate negative space on the platter. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, set on a light wooden table surface under natural, even lighting, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook sausage patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan.
Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt 10 g butter in the same pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in whisked eggs. Scramble gently until just set but still moist. Remove from pan.
Slice Hawaiian bread rolls horizontally. Melt remaining 20 g butter in the pan.
Place bread cut-side down in the pan. Toast lightly for 1-2 minutes until golden brown. Remove from pan.
Slice the tomato into 8 thin, round slices.
Assemble sliders: Place a bottom bun on a serving platter. Top with a portion of scrambled egg, then a sausage patty, two thin tomato slices, and a fresh basil leaf. Place the top bun.
Repeat for remaining sliders. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai-Inspired Spicy Chicken and Cashew Stir-fry with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of Thai-inspired spicy chicken and cashew stir-fry is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle, earthy tone. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy family kitchen. The stir-fry features generous, irregularly cut chunks of seared chicken, coated in a glistening, savory brown sauce. Interspersed among the chicken are vibrant, tender-crisp pieces of red and green bell pepper squares and soft, bright red tomato wedges. The dish is generously studded with golden-brown, toasted cashew nuts, providing textural contrast. The ingredients are casually mounded, allowing some components to slightly overlap, creating a natural, inviting appearance. A small mound of fluffy, white jasmine rice sits beside the stir-fry, ready to be mixed. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped spring onions adds a final pop of color. The lighting is warm and natural, as if from an overhead kitchen light, casting soft shadows that enhance the homely feel. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests across the rice bowl. The overall scene is one of comforting, expertly prepared home cooking, inviting and unpretentious.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional jasmine rice.
Offer fresh cucumber slices on the side.
Provide lime wedges for a squeeze of citrus.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Combine rice and 600ml water in a pot. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Cook 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with fork.
Toast raw cashews in a dry pan over medium heat 3-5 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Cut chicken into 2cm cubes.
Mince garlic. Thinly slice shallots. Cut bell peppers into 2cm squares. Cut tomatoes into wedges. Chop spring onions.
Rehydrate dried chilies in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and roughly chop.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and chicken stock. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan over high heat. Add minced garlic, sliced shallots, and chopped dried chilies. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes to wok. Stir-fry 5-7 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add bell pepper squares and tomato wedges. Stir-fry 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Pour sauce mixture over chicken and vegetables. Stir-fry 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and coats ingredients.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted cashews.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice. Garnish with chopped spring onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Broccoli and Leek Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, velvety green soup fills a clean, round white porcelain bowl, leaving a moderate negative space around the rim. The soup's surface is smooth and glossy, showcasing its rich, creamy texture. A delicate swirl of lighter green from a touch of crème fraîche or a sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh chives adorns the center, providing a subtle contrast. The small broccoli florets and thinly sliced leeks are completely blended, creating a uniform, inviting hue. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and a silver soup spoon placed neatly beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh appearance against a softly blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and thinly sliced leeks. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add small broccoli florets and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until broccoli is very tender.
Remove pot from heat. Carefully blend the soup using an immersion blender until completely smooth. Alternatively, transfer in batches to a stand blender.
For a silkier texture, pass the soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, pressing solids to extract liquid.
Return soup to low heat. Stir in the single cream. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat gently until warmed through; do not boil.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with toasted flaked almonds or chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Basil-Infused Peach & Fermented Honey Tartlet
recipes.visual_description: The Basil-Infused Peach & Fermented Honey Tartlet is presented as a single, perfectly portioned dessert on a handcrafted, natural beige ceramic plate with a slightly unglazed, earthy texture. The tartlet, approximately 10 cm in diameter, sits centrally. Its crust, a warm, golden-brown hue from the whole wheat and corn flour, has a subtly rustic, flaky texture. Inside, a smooth, pale green basil cream fills the shell, offering a soft color contrast. Neatly arranged atop the cream are small, bright orange cubes of fresh, diced seasonal peaches, their natural color vibrant and inviting. A delicate, glossy drizzle of fermented honey cascades over the peaches, catching the light. The plating emphasizes clean lines and negative space, allowing the natural beauty of the ingredients to stand out. The background is clean and uncluttered, featuring a light reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A hint of green from a potted plant is visible in the very soft focus background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Maple syrup or agave nectar (for dough)

instructions: Prepare Tartlet Dough: In a bowl, combine whole wheat flour, corn flour, and salt. Add cold plant-based butter, diced. Rub with fingertips until crumbly. Stir in maple syrup and cold water until dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap dough and chill 30 minutes.

Blind Bake Tartlet Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough thinly. Cut into four circles. Press into 10 cm tartlet molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with pie weights. Blind bake 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 more minutes until lightly golden. Cool completely.

Make Fermented Honey Drizzle: In a small jar, combine honey, water, and sourdough starter discard. Mix well. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 1-2 days, stirring daily, until small bubbles appear and a slight tang develops.

Prepare Basil Cream: Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend blanched basil with plant-based cream and natural sweetener until smooth. Strain if desired. In a small saucepan, whisk cornstarch into the basil cream. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Cool completely.
Prepare Peaches: Gently toss peeled, pitted peaches, diced into 1 cm cubes, with lemon juice.
Assemble Tartlets: Spoon cooled basil cream into each tartlet shell. Arrange diced peaches on top of the basil cream.
Finish: Drizzle fermented honey over the peaches. Serve immediately.
notes: To reduce food waste, peach skins can be dehydrated and ground into a powder for future use in smoothies or baking, and peach pits can be simmered in water to create a subtle peach-flavored tea base.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Buckwheat Kasha
recipes.special_requests: just make a dish with buckwheat
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Mushroom Buckwheat Kasha is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, golden-brown chicken thigh chunks are nestled into a rustic mound of fluffy, earthy buckwheat kasha. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed to a deep brown, are interspersed throughout the kasha, adding visual depth and texture. The dish is garnished with several vibrant fresh dill sprigs and a generous dollop of creamy white sour cream positioned to the side. The overall color palette is warm and natural, with rich browns, golden hues, and fresh green accents. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface with natural, even lighting from above. A white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly placed beside the plate. The composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space, showcasing the entire dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled vegetables, such as pickled cucumbers or cabbage.
Offer rye bread alongside the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion and carrot. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until vegetables soften, about 7-8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in buckwheat groats. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Return seared chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until buckwheat is tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped fresh dill. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Rojo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo Rojo is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The main focus is a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin crisp and glistening, resting atop a generous mound of vibrant reddish-orange rice. The rice is moist and tender, with visible diced carrots and flecks of herbs providing textural and color contrast. A light scattering of freshly chopped green cilantro garnishes the chicken and rice. The plating is clean and inviting, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. A small stack of warm corn tortillas and a lime wedge are placed nearby, enhancing the authentic Mexican presentation. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Accompany with a simple salsa fresca or pickled jalapeños.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly translucent.
In a blender, combine Roma tomatoes, chicken broth, tomato paste, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Blend until smooth.
Pour tomato mixture into the pot with the rice and vegetables. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf. Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The Cajun Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A mound of al dente penne pasta, coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce, forms the base. Nestled atop the pasta are several thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast chunks, each piece showing a beautiful caramelized crust. Diced red bell pepper and onion pieces are visible throughout the sauce, adding vibrant color and texture. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley covers the dish, providing a fresh contrast. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing the creamy sauce to flow slightly around the pasta. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures. A single, refined restaurant portion is shown.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic bread
Accompany with a simple green salad
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with half of the Cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 125 ml pasta water.
Dice onion and red bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and remaining Cajun seasoning. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta and seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan cheese before serving.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to personal spice preference.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Glazed Carrots and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole braised chicken thigh, with its deeply golden, crisped skin, is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Around it, several vibrant orange carrots, cut into 5 cm batons, are artfully arranged, glistening from their glaze. A rich, dark amber braising sauce pools elegantly beneath and around the chicken, highlighting its contours. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a bright pop of color. The dish showcases varied textures: crispy skin, tender chicken, slightly firm-tender carrots, and a smooth sauce. The plate rests on a simple, dark wooden table. A folded light grey cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting creates subtle shadows, suggesting a casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Drain most excess fat from the pot, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half, about 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot. Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and rosemary sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F).
While chicken braises, prepare carrots. Peel carrots and cut into 5 cm long batons.

In a separate medium pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add carrot batons. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add a splash of chicken stock from the braise (or water), season with salt and pepper. Cover and steam briefly until tender-crisp. Uncover and cook until liquid evaporates and carrots are glazed.

Remove chicken from the Dutch oven. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce braising liquid until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and discard herb sprigs.

To serve, place a braised chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange glazed carrot batons around the chicken. Spoon the reduced braising sauce generously over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Creamy, free-flowing Arborio risotto fills a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice has a tender, al dente bite and a rich, velvety texture, infused with golden chicken stock. Vibrant green broccoli florets, cooked tender-crisp, are evenly dispersed throughout the creamy rice, adding bright color and textural contrast. Finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese is gently stirred in, contributing to the dish's luxurious creaminess. A light dusting of fresh, finely chopped parsley or basil provides a final verdant garnish. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white linen napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Pair with a glass of the same dry white wine used in the recipe.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping.
instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it simmering gently.
Wash broccoli. Cut into small florets. Blanch broccoli in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil and 20g butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each ladle is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and free-flowing. The rice should be al dente (firm to the bite).
Stir in blanched broccoli florets during the last 3 minutes of cooking.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is 'mantecare'.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil.
notes: Risotto must be served immediately to maintain its creamy, fluid consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Pasta with Savory Tomato-Cocoa Sauce and Arroz Rojo
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this Mexican-inspired dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. At the center, a generous portion of short pasta, such as penne, is coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown savory tomato-cocoa sauce, showcasing its creamy texture. Thick, irregularly cut chunks of golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast are nestled within and beside the pasta, exhibiting a tender interior. To the side, a neat mound of vibrant orange-red Arroz Rojo (Mexican red rice) adds a contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of bright green fresh cilantro leaves over both the pasta and rice, along with a sprinkle of white crumbled Cotija cheese over the pasta. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a casually placed cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping up sauce and rice.
Offer a small bowl of lime wedges for a fresh squeeze over the dish.
Pair with a simple green salad with a lime vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened hot chocolate powder (or cocoa powder)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into thick chunks.

For the sauce, finely dice half the onion and mince 2 garlic cloves. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and chipotle. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, hot chocolate powder, cumin, and oregano. Pour in 250ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
For the Arroz Rojo, finely dice remaining half onion and mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add rinsed rice. Toast rice 3-4 minutes, stirring, until opaque. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Cook 2 minutes.

Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute. Pour in remaining 250ml chicken broth. Add salt to taste. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during cooking. Fluff with a fork.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add chicken chunks to the pasta and sauce. Gently combine.
Plate individual portions of pasta and chicken. Serve with a side of Arroz Rojo. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and crumbled Cotija cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Balsamic Blueberry Stuffed Chicken with Toasted Pine Nuts
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, pan-seared and oven-finished chicken breast, generously stuffed, rests as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented whole, its natural shape maintained, with a slight opening revealing glimpses of the creamy, herb-flecked cream cheese and sun-dried tomato stuffing. A rich, glossy balsamic blueberry glaze pools attractively around the base of the chicken and is drizzled over the top, showcasing vibrant purple-red hues and softened, burst blueberries. Scattered over the dish are golden toasted pine nuts, adding textural contrast and warmth. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space around the chicken, emphasizing its role as the main subject.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Toast pine nuts: Lightly toast 30g pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat. Stir constantly until golden. Remove and set aside.
Prepare stuffing: In a bowl, combine cream cheese, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, chopped fresh basil, and 20g of the toasted pine nuts. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Prepare chicken: Butterfly each chicken breast to create a pocket. Do not cut all the way through.
Stuff chicken: Spoon the cream cheese mixture evenly into each chicken pocket. Secure openings with toothpicks if needed. Season chicken exterior with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken: Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add stuffed chicken breasts. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Finish cooking: Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Make sauce: Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add blueberries, balsamic vinegar, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and blueberries burst. Gently mash some blueberries to release more flavor.

Serve: Remove toothpicks from chicken. Place one stuffed chicken breast on each plate. Drizzle generously with the balsamic blueberry sauce. Sprinkle remaining toasted pine nuts over the chicken and sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Balsamic Glazed Stuffed Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes and Pine Nuts
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown seared chicken breast is centrally positioned on a round white porcelain plate.
