Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a vibrant color contrast. The dish sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, alongside a standard metal fork and a casually placed, folded linen napkin. Warm, inviting light from a nearby kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting colors of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice bell pepper, onion, and eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms.
Toss diced bell pepper, onion, eggplant, and sliced mushrooms with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Mince garlic. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and vegetable stock. Add dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes.
Stir in roasted vegetables and cooked macaroni into the tomato sauce.
Transfer mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle diced mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chopped basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mushroom and Lentil Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Mushroom and Lentil Shepherd's Pie rests on a simple, well-worn ceramic plate. The mashed potato topping is golden brown with rustic peaks and valleys, showing slight browning from baking. The rich, deep brown lentil and mushroom filling peeks out from beneath the creamy potato. The vegetables within the filling, including diced carrots and celery, are tender and well-integrated. A small sprig of fresh parsley is casually placed on the side. The plate sits on a warm, natural wooden kitchen table. The lighting is soft and inviting, mimicking natural kitchen light, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, emphasizing the hearty, comforting nature of the dish. The portion is modest and approachable, fitting for a family meal.
instructions: Peel and quarter potatoes. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Mash with butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
While potatoes cook, prepare filling. Dice onion, carrots, and celery into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Slice mushrooms. Rinse lentils thoroughly.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, thyme, and rosemary. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rinsed lentils and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Stir occasionally.
Season lentil mixture with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Spread lentil and mushroom filling evenly in the bottom of the pot or transfer to a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Carefully spoon mashed potatoes over the filling. Spread evenly with a fork, creating peaks.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the potato topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Comforting Lentil Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Vegetarian Shepherd's Pie is presented in a rustic, well-used ceramic bowl. The golden-brown mashed potato topping, with its natural fork ridges, creates a comforting, textured surface. Some areas of the potato are deeply browned, contrasting with the softer, creamy interior. The rich, dark, earthy lentil and mushroom filling is visible along the edges where it meets the bowl, hinting at its hearty depth. The diced carrots, celery, and mushrooms are discernible within the thick, savory base. A sprinkle of bright green fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a warm-toned, worn wooden dining table, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen. A simple ceramic side plate with a slice of crusty bread and a casually folded linen napkin complete the homely setting. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal.
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice onion, carrots, and celery into small cubes. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Cook lentils: Rinse lentils. Place in saucepan with 750 ml water. Bring to boil, then simmer 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain.
Prepare potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in large pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to boil, cook 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Make mashed potatoes: Return hot potatoes to pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Cover to keep warm.
Sauté vegetables: Heat olive oil in large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add mushrooms: Stir in sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned.
Add garlic and herbs: Stir in minced garlic, fresh thyme, and fresh rosemary. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Build filling: Stir in tomato paste. Add cooked lentils and vegetable stock. Bring to simmer. Cook 10-15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble pie: Preheat oven to 190°C. Pour lentil mixture into a 2-liter baking dish.
Top with mash: Carefully spoon mashed potatoes over lentil mixture. Spread evenly to edges. Use a fork to create ridges on top.
Bake: Bake 25-30 minutes, or until filling is bubbly and potato topping is golden brown.
Serve: Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Four vibrant bell peppers, halved lengthwise, are baked until tender, holding their shape on a rustic ceramic baking dish. Each half is generously filled with a hearty, rustic mixture of cooked white rice and brown lentils, mixed with diced red onion, minced garlic, and diced mushrooms. The rich red of the crushed tomatoes and the fresh green of chopped basil, oregano, and parsley are visible within the filling. A golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella cheese and crisp breadcrumbs tops each pepper. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with an everyday ceramic plate. A casually folded cloth napkin and simple cutlery complete the homely, comforting scene. Natural, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the modest, satisfying portions, highlighting the dish's inviting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any remaining sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in rinsed lentils and rice. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, until most liquid is absorbed and lentils/rice are partially cooked.
Stir in chopped basil, oregano, parsley, and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling generously into each bell pepper half.
Top each filled pepper with shredded mozzarella and breadcrumbs.
Add 100 ml water to the bottom of the baking dish to prevent sticking.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Shepherd's Pie is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The golden-brown, slightly peaked mashed potato topping, with its rustic, fork-tined texture, covers the rich, savory lentil and vegetable filling peeking out from the sides. The potato has a few crispy, darkened peaks and edges, contrasting with the softer, creamy interior. Underneath, visible through the golden crust, are chunks of vibrant orange carrots, earthy brown mushrooms, and flecks of green lentils, all nestled in a thick, reddish-brown sauce. A few fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed on the side of the plate as a functional garnish. The dish sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, showing subtle signs of wear. A simple, folded off-white linen napkin is placed beside the plate, along with a standard metal fork. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
instructions: Place quartered potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Return potatoes to the hot pot. Add evaporated milk and butter. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender and have released their liquid.
Add rinsed green lentils, tomato paste, vegetable stock, dried thyme, dried rosemary, and bay leaf to the pan. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender and most liquid is absorbed. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Preheat oven to 190°C. Spread the lentil mixture evenly in the bottom of the oven-safe pan. Carefully spoon the mashed potato topping over the lentil filling, spreading it to the edges. If using, sprinkle grated Cheddar cheese over the mashed potatoes.
Place the pan in the preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the filling is bubbling and the potato topping is golden brown. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty lentil and vegetable curry is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The curry, rich with earthy brown lentils, features clearly visible chunks of tender, bright orange diced carrots, soft white diced potatoes, and vibrant red diced bell pepper, all coated in a golden-yellow, slightly creamy sauce from the coconut milk and spices. Wilted green Swiss chard leaves are interspersed throughout the curry, adding depth of color. The curry is spooned into the center of the plate, allowing its natural flow and slight overflow. Alongside, a modest mound of fluffy, pale brown cooked brown rice sits, separate but touching the curry. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander leaves is scattered over the curry for a functional garnish. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, dark grey cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate, and a basic metal fork rests on the napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen at mealtime, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the dish. The overall presentation is homely and unpretentious, reflecting a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or roti on the side
Offer a dollop of plain yogurt or a simple pickle as an accompaniment
instructions: Rinse brown lentils. Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat 30 ml oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 20 g curry powder, 5 g turmeric, 5 g cumin powder, and 5 g coriander powder. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add diced carrots, diced potatoes, and diced red bell pepper. Stir well to coat with spices.
Add rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, and 500 ml vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 25-30 minutes, or until lentils and vegetables are tender. Stir occasionally.
Stir in 400 ml coconut milk and chopped Swiss chard or spinach. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until chard or spinach wilts and curry thickens slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot with cooked brown rice. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Roasted Vegetables and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: The baked rigatoni is presented in a rustic ceramic gratin dish, showcasing a golden-brown, bubbling cheese crust. Beneath the melted mozzarella and Parmesan, tender roasted eggplant, zucchini, and red bell pepper cubes are nestled amongst al dente rigatoni pasta, all coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. Creamy white dollops of ricotta cheese peek through the pasta. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered generously on top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere. A traditional fork and knife are placed to the right of the plate, completing the inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut eggplant, zucchini, and bell pepper into 2 cm cubes. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Toss eggplant, zucchini, and bell pepper with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Set aside.
Meanwhile, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir roasted vegetables into the tomato sauce. Add cooked rigatoni. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine ricotta cheese with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spoon half of the pasta mixture into a 2.5-liter baking dish or four individual gratin dishes. Dollop spoonfuls of ricotta over the pasta. Sprinkle with half of the mozzarella and Parmesan.
Add remaining pasta mixture. Top with remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and golden brown on top. Internal temperature should be at least 75°C.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Feel free to substitute other seasonal vegetables like mushrooms or spinach.
For an extra layer of flavor, a splash of white wine can be added to the tomato sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Roasted Vegetables and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Baked Penne with Roasted Vegetables and Ricotta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The penne pasta is thoroughly coated in a vibrant reddish-orange tomato sauce. Large, tender 2 cm cubes of roasted eggplant, red, and yellow bell peppers are interspersed throughout, showing slight caramelization. Creamy, melted ricotta cheese dollops are visible, alongside gooey strands of mozzarella. The top boasts a golden-brown, bubbly crust of baked mozzarella and grated parmesan. Fresh, roughly chopped basil leaves provide a pop of vibrant green. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, set against a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of crusty bread.
Pair with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice eggplant, red and yellow bell peppers into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked penne, roasted vegetables, tomato sauce, 100g shredded mozzarella, 25g grated parmesan, and ricotta cheese. Mix gently.
Transfer mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Top with remaining 100g shredded mozzarella and 25g grated parmesan.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with chopped fresh basil.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead of time and baked just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: South Indian Lentil and Vegetable Curry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant South Indian Lentil and Vegetable Curry is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, nestled beside a mound of fluffy brown rice. The curry itself is a rich, creamy orange-yellow hue from turmeric and coconut milk, dotted with deep red from bell pepper, purple from eggplant, and bright orange from carrot rounds. The vegetables are cut into distinct 2 cm cubes and 1 cm rounds, cooked to tender perfection but retaining their shape. The curry has a moderate viscosity, allowing the ingredients to be clearly visible within the sauce. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green coriander leaves provides a contrasting pop of color on top. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside it. A small, traditional katori (small bowl) of a bright green lime pickle or mango chutney sits nearby, offering an authentic accompaniment. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting restaurant-style atmosphere. The overall presentation is clean and professional, focusing on the natural appeal of the wholesome ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm steamed brown rice.
Offer a side of lime pickle or mango chutney.
Serve in individual katoris (small bowls) if preferred for sharing.
instructions: Rinse red lentils. Place in a pot with 750ml water. Bring to boil. Skim foam. Reduce heat. Simmer 15 minutes until tender. Drain. Set aside.
Cook brown rice according to package directions. Typically 250g rice with 500ml water. Simmer until water absorbed.
Heat oil in large pot over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. Let them pop.
Add cumin seeds. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add eggplant cubes, bell pepper cubes, and carrot rounds. Sauté 5 minutes.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and paprika. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked lentils and tamarind paste. Stir well.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Cook 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender and curry thickens slightly. Stir occasionally.
Season with salt to taste. Add slit green chili if using.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Corn and Chickpea Fritters with Chipotle Lime Aioli
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, pan-fried fritters are arranged casually on a rustic light wooden board. Each fritter, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick, is studded with vibrant yellow corn kernels, small diced red bell pepper, and specks of green coriander, showcasing a crisp exterior and a tender, moist interior. A small white ceramic ramekin holds a creamy, pale orange chipotle lime aioli, positioned alongside the fritters. Fresh lime wedges and a scattering of bright green coriander leaves garnish the board, adding freshness and contrasting color. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space, evoking a casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors of the snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as an appetizer or part of a 'botanas' (Mexican snack) platter.
Accompany with extra lime wedges for squeezing.
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some texture.
Combine corn kernels, mashed chickpeas, diced red bell pepper, minced red onion, minced garlic, and chopped coriander in a large bowl.
Whisk together flour, egg, baking powder, salt, and black pepper in a separate bowl until smooth.
Add wet mixture to dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly to form 5-6 cm fritters.
Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan.
Transfer cooked fritters to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the aioli, combine mayonnaise, minced chipotle chile, and juice from half a lime in a small bowl. Stir until smooth.
Serve fritters warm with chipotle lime aioli and lime wedges.
notes: Adjust the quantity of chipotle chile in adobo to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Tofu Skewers with Peanut-Coconut Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, rectangular white ceramic plate, showcasing two perfectly grilled skewers. Each skewer holds golden-brown tofu cubes, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper squares, slightly charred red onion pieces, and sweet pineapple chunks. The tofu has distinct grill marks, indicating a professional sear. A rich, creamy, light brown peanut-coconut sauce is generously drizzled over the skewers, with some pooling elegantly on the plate's surface. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of thinly sliced green scallions and a small cluster of bright green sunflower sprouts, adding freshness and height. A lime wedge is placed neatly beside the skewers. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere. The focus remains entirely on the food, highlighting its appealing colors and textures.
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares. Cut red onion into 2 cm squares. Cut pineapple into 2 cm chunks.

For marinade: Mince ginger and garlic. Thinly slice lemongrass. Combine soy sauce, half of minced ginger, half of minced garlic, and sliced lemongrass in a bowl. Add tofu cubes. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Thread tofu, bell peppers, onion, and pineapple onto skewers, alternating components. Create 8 skewers.

For peanut-coconut sauce: In a blender, combine roasted peanuts, remaining minced ginger, remaining minced garlic, coconut milk, gochujang, brown sugar, and juice from half a lime. Blend until smooth. Add water if needed for desired consistency.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or preheat grill to medium-high.
Cook skewers for 3-4 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until tofu is golden brown and vegetables are tender-crisp with slight char marks.
Thinly slice scallions for garnish. Cut remaining lime into wedges.
Arrange cooked skewers on a serving plate. Drizzle generously with peanut-coconut sauce. Garnish with sliced scallions and sunflower sprouts. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Red Pepper & Ricotta Dip with Herbed Chickpea Crisps
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, round, rustic white ceramic plate. A generous portion of the creamy, vibrant red roasted red pepper and ricotta dip is spooned into a shallow, off-white ceramic bowl, placed centrally on the plate. The dip’s texture is smooth and velvety, with subtle specks of roasted red pepper. Around the bowl, golden-brown herbed chickpea crisps are artfully arranged, some leaning against the bowl, others scattered alongside. The crisps are irregularly shaped, showcasing their artisanal, hand-broken quality, with visible flecks of dried herbs. A few fresh green basil leaves are placed atop the dip, alongside a scattering of dark, glossy Kalamata olives. A final drizzle of golden-green extra virgin olive oil glistens over the dip. The overall presentation is clean, inviting, and approachable, set on a light wooden surface with soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small plates for individual portions.
Offer with a selection of crudités alongside the crisps.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil.
Roast peppers 25-30 minutes. Skin should blister.
Transfer peppers to bowl. Cover tightly with cling film 10 minutes.
Peel roasted peppers. Discard skin.
Combine peeled peppers, ricotta, garlic, lemon juice, 30ml olive oil, fresh basil, dried oregano in food processor.
Process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
For the Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk chickpea flour, water, 15ml olive oil, dried oregano, dried basil, salt in bowl. Mix until smooth batter.
Pour thin layer of batter onto prepared tray. Spread evenly.
Bake 15-20 minutes. Crisps should be golden and firm.
Remove from oven. Let cool. Break into irregular pieces.
notes: Crisps can be prepared up to 2 days in advance. Store in airtight container.

recipes.recipe_name: Arancini al Pomodoro e Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown arancini are arranged organically on a round, white porcelain plate. Each arancino is a perfectly spherical, crisp ball, showing the textured breadcrumb coating. A small, separate ramekin or a neat dollop of vibrant red tomato sauce sits beside the arancini. A few fresh, deep green basil leaves are scattered over the arancini and sauce. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds subtle flecks of white. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting from above. The focus remains on the food, showcasing its inviting colors and textures.

ingredients.name: Mozzarella
ingredients.quantity: 150 g, low-moisture, diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Prepare the tomato sauce: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add 1 minced garlic clove. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes. Stir in torn basil. Set aside.
Make the risotto: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped shallot. Cook 3 minutes until softened. Add remaining minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add Arborio rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast rice. Rice grains should be translucent at edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add warm vegetable stock, 125 ml at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until liquid is almost absorbed before adding more. Continue until rice is al dente, about 20 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Spread risotto onto a large baking sheet. Cool completely in refrigerator for at least 2 hours.

Form the arancini: Take about 50 g of cooled risotto. Flatten into a disc in your palm. Place 2-3 mozzarella cubes in the center. Carefully form risotto around mozzarella to create a tight ball. Repeat for all risotto.
Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Roll each arancino first in flour, then in egg, then in breadcrumbs. Ensure full coating.
Fry the arancini: Heat enough olive oil for deep frying in a large pot or deep fryer to 170°C (340°F).
Carefully place arancini in hot oil, 3-4 at a time. Do not overcrowd. Fry 4-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with the prepared tomato sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegetable Pakora with Mint-Yogurt Chutney
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents golden-brown Vegetable Pakoras arranged organically on a rustic, light-colored ceramic platter. Small florets of broccoli and cauliflower, along with thinly sliced onions, are visible within the crispy, irregularly shaped fritters. Each pakora features a rich, golden-brown crust contrasting with a tender, aromatic interior. A small, white ceramic bowl, placed beside the pakoras, holds a vibrant green Mint-Yogurt Chutney, its smooth texture garnished with a single fresh mint leaf. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the platter. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting. A folded cotton napkin rests nearby, complementing the casual yet refined aesthetic. The colors are natural and appealing, highlighting the freshness of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve pakoras hot as a snack or appetizer.
Traditionally shared from a common platter.
Accompanied by various chutneys, such as mint, tamarind, or chili.
instructions: Wash and dry broccoli and cauliflower florets. Cut into small, bite-sized pieces. Thinly slice the onion. Finely chop green chili, ginger, and garlic.
In a large bowl, combine chickpea flour, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and salt. Whisk to combine.
Gradually add water to the flour mixture. Whisk until a thick, smooth batter forms. It should be thick enough to coat vegetables.
Add chopped broccoli, cauliflower, onion, green chili, ginger, and garlic to the batter. Mix well to coat all vegetables.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 170°C. Test oil with a small drop of batter; it should sizzle immediately.
Carefully drop spoonfuls of the vegetable mixture into the hot oil. Fry in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan.
Fry pakoras for 4-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure vegetables are cooked through.
Remove pakoras with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. Keep warm.
For the chutney: Combine yogurt, fresh mint leaves, fresh coriander leaves, and lime juice in a blender. Blend until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt.
Serve hot pakoras immediately with the Mint-Yogurt Chutney.
notes: Chickpea flour (besan) is essential for authentic pakora texture.
Adjust green chili quantity for desired spice level.
Ensure oil is at correct temperature for crispy, non-greasy pakoras.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Lentil Arancini with Basil Marinara
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown arancini spheres are arranged artfully on a clean, white ceramic sharing plate. A small, round ramekin of vibrant red basil marinara sits beside them. Each arancino is approximately 5 cm in diameter, with a crispy, irregularly textured exterior from the breadcrumbs. They are a deep golden-brown, indicating a perfectly fried crust. A hint of melted mozzarella subtly oozes from one, showcasing the cheesy center. The marinara is a smooth, rich red, flecked with finely chopped fresh green basil. A few small, fresh basil leaves are scattered over the arancini and beside the ramekin, adding a pop of green and aromatic freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese is visible on top of the arancini. The plate rests on a light-colored wooden table surface. A simple folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is placed to the side. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot as an antipasto or snack.
Offer with small forks or toothpicks for easy handling.
instructions: Soak dried porcini mushrooms in 100 ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, chop finely. Reserve liquid.
Cook green lentils according to package directions until tender. Drain.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan. Sauté 150 g diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add 2 cloves minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add brown rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in the reserved porcini liquid. Stir until absorbed.
Gradually add hot vegetable stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Allow each addition to absorb before adding more. Cook until rice is al dente, about 20-25 minutes.
Stir in chopped fresh mushrooms and chopped porcini. Cook until softened.
Remove rice from heat. Stir in cooked lentils, 100 g Parmesan cheese, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Spread rice mixture on a baking sheet. Chill completely for at least 2 hours.
Prepare the marinara: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a saucepan. Sauté 75 g diced onion until soft. Add 1 clove minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped fresh basil. Keep warm.
Once rice mixture is chilled, take small portions. Flatten in your palm. Place 1-2 mozzarella cubes in the center. Form into a sphere, about 5 cm diameter. Repeat for all arancini.
Set up a dredging station: one bowl with beaten eggs, one bowl with breadcrumbs.
Dip each arancino in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, ensuring full coverage.
Heat olive oil for frying in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C. Oil depth should cover arancini.
Fry arancini in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 4-6 minutes per batch. Do not overcrowd.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with warm basil marinara.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Gochujang Tofu Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, modern bistro setting frames the Crispy Gochujang Tofu Bites, presented on a clean white porcelain platter. Each 2.5 cm tofu cube, pan-fried to a golden-brown crisp, glistens under a sticky, rich red-orange gochujang glaze. The cubes are arranged organically yet neatly, allowing moderate negative space. Thinly sliced bright green scallions are scattered, providing fresh contrast. A delicate cluster of vibrant green sunflower sprouts adds feathery texture. The plating is clean, professional, emphasizing the dish's vibrant colors and appealing textures. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with an unobtrusive background. This snack is designed for sharing, reflecting a casual yet refined Korean-inspired culinary experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes like kimchi or pickled radish.
Offer alongside a light beer or soju.
Best enjoyed as an appetizer or a shared snack.
instructions: Press tofu: Drain tofu. Wrap in paper towels. Place heavy object on top. Press for 30 minutes to remove excess water.
Cut tofu: Cut pressed tofu into 2.5 cm cubes.
Coat tofu: Toss tofu cubes with cornstarch until evenly coated.
Heat oil: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 175°C.
Fry tofu: Fry tofu in batches until golden brown and crispy. This takes 4-6 minutes per batch.
Drain tofu: Remove tofu with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Make glaze: In a small saucepan, combine gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, grated ginger, and minced garlic.
Simmer glaze: Bring glaze to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Toss tofu: Add crispy tofu to the glaze. Gently toss to coat all cubes evenly.
Plate: Arrange coated tofu cubes on a serving platter.
Garnish: Sprinkle with sliced scallions and sunflower sprouts. Serve immediately.
notes: Properly pressing the tofu is crucial for a crispy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Masoor Dal with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Masoor Dal is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with an earthy glaze, centered on a well-worn wooden dining table. The dal is a creamy, golden-yellow hue, studded with tender, roasted potato and carrot chunks. Its surface is slightly rippled, showing its rich, thick consistency. Alongside the dal, a mound of fluffy brown rice rests directly on the table surface next to the bowl, creating a natural, home-style arrangement. The roasted vegetables within the dal maintain their distinct shapes, exhibiting browned edges from the roasting process. Fresh, vibrant green coriander leaves are generously sprinkled over the dal, providing a burst of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge is casually placed on the rim of the bowl. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm, inviting light from an overhead fixture. The background is minimal, suggesting a homely dining area with natural clutter. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. The entire plate, including the rice and bowl, is visible, showcasing a comforting, authentic Indian home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or raita to cool the palate.
Accompany with Indian pickles (achar) or chutney for added flavor complexity.
Traditionally eaten with flatbreads like roti or naan, in addition to rice.
Often consumed using hands, scooping with rice or bread.
instructions: Rinse red lentils until water runs clear. Soak in water for 20 minutes. Drain.

Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 1.2 litres of water in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and cut potatoes and carrots into 3 cm chunks. Toss with 30 ml vegetable oil, 2.5 g turmeric, 2.5 g ground coriander, and salt. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly browned.
While vegetables roast, finely chop onions. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Dice tomatoes.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onions. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, remaining 2.5 g turmeric, and remaining 7.5 g ground coriander. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking down tomatoes.

Add drained lentils to the pot. Pour in 1.5 litres water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender and creamy. Add more water if dal becomes too thick.
Prepare tadka: Heat remaining 15 ml vegetable oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. When they splutter, add cumin seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour hot tadka over the cooked dal. Stir in garam masala. Season dal with salt to taste.
Gently fold roasted potatoes and carrots into the dal. Do not mash.
Chop fresh coriander. Serve dal warm with brown rice. Garnish with fresh coriander and a lemon/lime wedge.
notes: Adjust the consistency of the dal by adding more hot water if you prefer a thinner consistency.
For an extra layer of flavor, a pinch of asafoetida (hing) can be added to the tadka after the mustard and cumin seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Mozzarella Arancini
recipes.visual_description: A trio of golden-brown arancini, each approximately 5 cm in diameter, is artfully arranged on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The arancini exhibit a crisp, textured exterior from the breadcrumbs, with a rich, uniform golden hue. One arancino is gently cut in half, revealing a creamy, off-white risotto interior with visible mushroom pieces, and a perfectly melted, gooey white mozzarella core. A small, elegant pool of vibrant red marinara sauce is presented beside the arancini, ready for dipping. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm marinara sauce for dipping.
Accompany with a simple mixed green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and liquid evaporates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in 120ml warm vegetable stock. Stir until absorbed.
Continue adding stock, 120ml at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to absorb before adding more. This takes about 20-25 minutes until rice is al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread risotto onto a large baking sheet. Cool completely in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Take a spoonful of cooled risotto. Flatten it in your palm.
Place one mozzarella cube in the center. Cover with more risotto. Form into a tight ball, about 5 cm in diameter.
Repeat for all risotto, making about 12-16 arancini balls.
Place beaten eggs in one shallow dish. Place breadcrumbs in another.
Roll each arancino first in egg, then in breadcrumbs. Ensure full coverage.
Heat olive oil for frying in a deep pot to 175°C (350°F). Oil should be at least 8 cm deep.
Fry arancini in batches, 3-4 at a time, for 4-6 minutes. Turn occasionally. Fry until golden brown and crisp.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the risotto is fully chilled before forming the arancini; this prevents them from falling apart during frying.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom & Mozzarella Arancini with Basil Tomato Dip
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, perfectly spherical Mushroom & Mozzarella Arancini are presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Each arancini ball, about 6 cm in diameter, boasts a crisp, textured breadcrumb crust. A small, elegant white bowl filled with vibrant red Basil Tomato Dip sits beside the arancini. The dip, subtly chunky from the crushed tomatoes, is adorned with fresh, torn basil leaves. A light sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese dusts the arancini. The arrangement is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, showcasing the arancini as the focal point. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and a neatly folded cotton napkin, illuminated by natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an antipasto (appetizer) before a meal.
Enjoy as street food or a casual snack.
Offer with additional grated Parmesan cheese for sprinkling.
instructions: In a large pot, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat. Sauté finely diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are softened and liquid evaporates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add brown rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes until rice is lightly toasted. Pour in white wine. Cook until wine is fully absorbed.

Begin adding hot vegetable stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 30-40 minutes, or until rice is tender but still has a slight bite.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan, 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread risotto onto a baking sheet. Chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until completely cold.

Take a handful of cold risotto (about 50g). Flatten it in your palm. Place a 1 cm mozzarella cube in the center. Carefully form the risotto around the mozzarella, creating a compact ball, about 5-6 cm in diameter. Ensure no mozzarella is exposed. Repeat with remaining risotto and mozzarella.

Set up a breading station: one bowl with beaten eggs, another with breadcrumbs. Roll each arancini ball first in the beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Then roll in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

In a deep pot or Dutch oven, heat at least 5 cm of olive oil to 170°C. Fry arancini in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 4-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

For the dip: In a small saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir in fresh basil leaves just before serving.
Serve arancini hot with the warm basil tomato dip on the side.
notes: Ensure risotto is completely cold before forming balls; this prevents them from falling apart during frying.
Maintain consistent oil temperature for even browning and proper cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Eggplant Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, individual portion of Classic Eggplant Parmesan, baked golden brown, sits on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features thick, tender slices of pan-fried eggplant, not fanned, layered with rich, deep red tomato sauce, melted creamy mozzarella, and grated golden parmesan cheese. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves adorns the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The eggplant retains its structural integrity, showcasing distinct layers. The sauce peeks through the sides. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished traditional Italian-style flatware are beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background suggests a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Slice eggplant into 1 cm thick rounds. Place on paper towels. Sprinkle generously with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry thoroughly.
Prepare tomato sauce: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot. Sauté diced onion until translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, oregano, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up dredging stations: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in another, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each eggplant slice: First coat in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Finally, coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry eggplant slices in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and tender. Drain on paper towels.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Arrange a single layer of pan-fried eggplant slices over the sauce. Top with a layer of sliced mozzarella, a sprinkle of grated Parmesan, and some fresh basil.
Repeat layers: sauce, eggplant, mozzarella, Parmesan, basil. Finish with a final layer of sauce, mozzarella, and Parmesan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the top is golden brown. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with extra fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Root Vegetables and Fermented Cabbage Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone, leaving ample negative space. A single portion features several substantial, golden-brown miso-glazed tempeh chunks, arranged organically as a central anchor. The tempeh boasts a rich, glossy sheen from the thickened miso glaze, hinting at its savory depth. Alongside, vibrant roasted root vegetables – thick-cut potato wedges, vibrant orange carrot chunks, and deep crimson beet wedges – are artfully scattered, showcasing their caramelized edges and soft textures. Interspersed are soft, translucent onion wedges. Their natural colors create an earthy palette. A fresh, crisp mound of thinly shredded, pale green fermented cabbage salad with flecks of orange grated carrot and green dill provides a bright, tangy contrast in texture and color. The entire composition is garnished lightly with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped chives or parsley and a delicate cluster of pale green sunflower sprouts, adding a touch of freshness and height. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The setting includes a simple, undyed linen napkin and a single, unadorned fork, maintaining a minimalist and eco-conscious aesthetic. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its organic beauty and the vibrant colors of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of plain brown rice or quinoa for extra sustenance.
Offer a simple, light broth made from reserved vegetable trimmings as a starter.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cabbage Salad (can be done days ahead):
Combine shredded cabbage, grated carrot, and salt in a large bowl.
Massage mixture vigorously with clean hands for 5-10 minutes. Cabbage will soften and release water.
Pack mixture tightly into a clean glass jar, pressing down to remove air pockets. Ensure cabbage is fully submerged in its brine.
Seal jar with a lid, leaving slight gap for gas release, or use an airlock.
Ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days, or until desired sourness is achieved.
Refrigerate once fermented.
Prepare Miso Glaze:
In a small bowl, whisk together red miso paste, soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, grated ginger, minced garlic, sesame oil, and water. Set aside.
Prepare Tempeh:
Cut tempeh into thick rectangles or large cubes.
Steam tempeh for 10 minutes to soften and reduce bitterness.
Pat dry thoroughly.
Roast Vegetables:
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
On a large baking sheet, toss carrot, potato, beet, and onion wedges with olive oil, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 30-40 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Cook Tempeh:
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add a splash of oil. Sear tempeh pieces until golden brown on all sides.
Pour miso glaze over tempeh. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, turning tempeh to coat evenly, until glaze thickens and coats tempeh beautifully.
Assemble and Serve:
Divide roasted vegetables among 7 plates.
Arrange miso-glazed tempeh chunks alongside vegetables.
Add a generous portion of fermented cabbage salad to each plate.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley/chives and sunflower sprouts.
Serve warm.
notes: The fermented cabbage salad can be prepared several days or weeks in advance. Its flavor will deepen over time.
Reserved vegetable trimmings (carrot tops, beet greens, potato peels, onion skins) can be used to make a flavorful zero-waste vegetable stock.
This recipe is naturally gluten-free if using tamari instead of soy sauce.
For an even deeper flavor, marinate the tempeh in the miso glaze for at least 30 minutes before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Roots and Fermented Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A single, generously sized, golden-brown seared tempeh steak, glazed with a rich, glossy miso sauce, is the focal point. The tempeh is presented as a whole, thick rectangle. Alongside are roasted root vegetables: rustic chunks of tender, caramelized carrots and potatoes, their natural colors of deep orange and light beige visible. A vibrant, slightly mounded portion of pale green fermented cabbage, with subtle variations in color, is placed next to the tempeh, adding a bright, tangy contrast. A sprinkle of roughly chopped, toasted peanuts provides a natural, textural element on top of the tempeh and cabbage. The composition is clean, with ample white space on the plate, emphasizing the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and soft, diffused natural lighting, with a hint of green from a minimalist plant in the background, creating an eco-conscious and serene atmosphere. The plate is viewed from a slightly elevated angle, showing the entire dish without overcrowding.
instructions: Prepare fermented cabbage: Thinly slice 500g cabbage. Place in a large bowl. Add 10g salt. Massage cabbage until water releases. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Ensure cabbage is submerged in its liquid. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tanginess achieved.
Prepare tempeh glaze: Grate ginger and mince garlic. Combine miso paste, grated ginger, minced garlic, brown rice vinegar, soy sauce, and 60ml water in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Cut tempeh: Slice tempeh into 7 equal thick rectangles or 'steaks'.
Preheat oven: Set oven to 200°C.
Prepare vegetables: Peel and cut carrots and potatoes into 2-3 cm rustic chunks. Toss with 30ml oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
Sear tempeh: Heat remaining 30ml oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear tempeh steaks 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Glaze tempeh: Pour miso glaze over seared tempeh in the pan. Simmer 2-3 minutes, turning tempeh to coat evenly, until glaze thickens and coats tempeh.
Prepare peanut crumble: Roughly chop peanuts. Lightly toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.
Assemble dish: Arrange roasted vegetables on plates. Place a glazed tempeh steak alongside. Top with a spoonful of fermented cabbage. Sprinkle toasted peanuts over the tempeh and cabbage.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork with Cheesy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Pork with Cheesy Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Rich, dark brown braised pork chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled in a glossy, deeply colored sauce with caramelized onion slivers and mushroom quarters. Beside the pork, a generous, neatly scooped mound of creamy, golden-yellow cheesy mashed potatoes sits, showing melted Gruyère. Fresh chopped parsley garnishes both, adding vibrant green contrast. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the warmth. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a professional, approachable restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread to soak up the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, peeled, cut into 3 cm cubes

instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return pork to the pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until pork is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While pork braises, prepare potatoes. Boil potato cubes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes well. Return to hot pot.
Add butter and half of the grated Gruyère cheese to potatoes. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Once pork is tender, remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Adjust seasoning of pork stew if needed.
Serve braised pork and its sauce alongside a generous scoop of cheesy mashed potatoes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The braising time may vary based on pork cut and tenderness desired.
Ensure beer is robust but not overly bitter.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chickpea & Lentil Fritters with Spicy Tomato-Tamarind Chutney
recipes.visual_description: A collection of golden-brown, irregularly shaped Fermented Chickpea & Lentil Fritters are casually arranged on a large, handcrafted, unglazed ceramic platter in a soft cream hue. Each fritter, about 4cm in diameter, boasts a visibly crisp, textured exterior from pan-frying. They are nestled with natural spacing, showcasing their earthy tones. A generous, rustic dollop of the deep reddish-brown Spicy Tomato-Tamarind Chutney, thick with small diced tomato pieces, rests beside the fritters. The presentation is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the natural beauty and texture of the ingredients. A few fresh coriander leaves are scattered sparingly for a subtle green accent. The platter sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, illuminated by soft, natural light from the side, with a simple, undyed linen napkin in beige placed nearby. The background is clean and unobtrusive, hinting at natural elements.
instructions: Soak chickpeas and red lentils overnight in separate bowls. Drain thoroughly.
Blend soaked chickpeas and lentils with 100ml water until a coarse paste forms. Do not over-blend.
Transfer to a large bowl. Stir in chickpea flour, finely diced onion, minced garlic, chopped fresh coriander, cumin powder, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Cover the bowl with a clean cloth. Let the batter ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours. The batter will become slightly bubbly and tangy.
Heat 200ml vegetable oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Spoon small portions of batter, approximately 30g each, into the hot oil.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
For the chutney, heat 15ml oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. Let them splutter.
Add finely chopped small onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, and finely chopped Thai chili. Sauté until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add diced ripe tomatoes, tamarind paste, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and the chutney thickens.
Adjust seasoning with sugar if desired.
Serve warm fritters with a side of spicy tomato-tamarind chutney.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chickpea and Peanut Crunch
recipes.visual_description: A generous pile of golden-brown, crispy roasted chickpeas and light brown, crunchy peanuts fills a rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The mixture is loosely arranged, showcasing the natural textures of the ingredients. Specks of vibrant orange and yellow spices, from turmeric and chili powder, are visible, clinging to the chickpeas and peanuts. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded beige cloth napkin rests beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely, typical of a casual snack served at a family kitchen table. The entire bowl is visible, with ample negative space around it to highlight the dish as the focal point. Portions are generous and approachable, inviting sharing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Drain and rinse canned chickpeas. Pat them very dry with a kitchen towel.
Spread dried chickpeas in a single layer on a baking tray. Drizzle with 15 ml vegetable oil. Toss to coat.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Chickpeas should be crispy and golden brown. Stir halfway through.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine roasted chickpeas and peanuts.
In a small bowl, mix ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, red chili powder, amchoor, and salt.
Sprinkle spice mixture over chickpeas and peanuts. Toss well to coat evenly.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Loin with Potato Pavé, Beer Jus and Parmesan Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated dish is presented on a large, round, pristine white bone china plate with ample negative space. A perfectly seared, golden-brown block of pork loin, revealing a tender blush-pink interior, rests prominently. Adjacent to it is a precise, golden-brown rectangular block of layered potato pavé, its exterior crisp and multi-textured. A rich, dark amber beer jus is artfully pooled beside the pork, creating an organic, flowing shape. A delicate, almost translucent, irregularly shaped Parmesan crisp stands elegantly against the pork or pavé, adding a subtle vertical element. A few precise dots of vibrant green chive oil are strategically placed on the plate, providing a contrasting color accent. The composition is off-center, emphasizing architectural precision and minimalist elegance. The setting features a premium grey-veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting casting intentional shadows. The background is ultra-minimalist, maximizing negative space to highlight the dish as the sole focus.
instructions: For the Pork Loin:
Season pork loin with salt and pepper. Place in a vacuum-sealable bag with a sprig of thyme. Vacuum seal.
Cook in a sous vide bath at 60°C for 2 hours. Remove pork, pat dry thoroughly.
Sear pork loin in a hot pan with 15 ml neutral oil until deep golden-brown on all sides. Rest pork for 5 minutes.
For the Potato Pavé:
Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel potatoes. Slice thinly using a mandoline, about 2 mm thick.
Toss potato slices with 50 g melted butter, salt, and pepper. Layer tightly into a small, parchment-lined loaf pan or terrine mold (approximately 15x8 cm).
Press firmly. Bake for 60-75 minutes until tender. Place a heavy weight on top. Chill overnight.
Once chilled, cut the potato pavé into 4 equal rectangular portions. Sear each portion in a pan with 15 ml neutral oil until golden and crisp on all sides.
For the Beer Jus:
In a saucepan, sauté diced shallot and minced garlic in a drizzle of oil until fragrant. Add remaining thyme.
Deglaze with dark beer. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Reduce until slightly thickened and glossy.
Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the Parmesan Crisps:
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sprinkle small mounds of grated Parmesan cheese onto the parchment, leaving space between each. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely on the parchment paper. They will crisp as they cool.
For the Chive Oil:
Blanch chopped chives briefly in boiling water. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.
Blend blanched chives with 30 ml neutral oil until smooth and vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for clear oil.
Assembly:
Slice each seared pork loin portion into thick medallions or serve as a single piece. Arrange a portion of seared potato pavé on one side of a large, white plate.
Place the seared pork loin next to the pavé. Spoon a generous pool of beer jus beside the pork.
Carefully place a Parmesan crisp leaning against the pork or pavé. Drizzle a few dots of chive oil around the plate for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Red Lentil & Coconut Curry with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting portion of Hearty Red Lentil & Coconut Curry is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The curry, a rich, earthy orange-red, is ladled over a bed of fluffy brown rice. The red lentils are plump and softened, interspersed with clearly visible, tender diced carrots, diced potatoes, and diced bell pepper chunks. The sauce is thick but still fluid, clinging to the rice and vegetables. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander leaves is scattered over the top. A quarter lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The bowl is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, heavy-bottomed stainless steel spoon rests on a folded, off-white linen napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, evoking a cozy kitchen family dinner.
instructions: Rinse red lentils under cold water until clear. Drain.
Cook brown rice: Combine 420g brown rice with 1 liter water in a pot. Bring to boil. Reduce heat. Simmer covered 35-40 minutes until water absorbed. Let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with fork.
Prepare curry: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. Cook until they pop.
Add diced onions. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cumin, turmeric, and coriander powders. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add diced carrots, diced potatoes (2cm cubes), and diced bell pepper. Stir to coat.
Add rinsed lentils, canned diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, and coconut milk. Stir well.
Bring curry to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer partially covered 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender and vegetables are cooked through. Stir occasionally.
Season curry with salt to taste.
Serve curry hot over brown rice. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie is served on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The golden-brown mashed potato topping, slightly mounded, shows peaks and valleys from a fork, with a light crispness on its surface and scattered melted Parmesan. Below, the rich, savory lentil and vegetable filling, visible where the mash is slightly uneven, reveals diced carrots, onions, and mushrooms in a thick, herb-flecked gravy. The colors are warm and earthy: deep brown for the filling, golden-cream for the potato, and flecks of green from fresh herbs. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. In the background, the full ceramic baking dish of the pie is visible, suggesting a family meal. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, natural light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served directly from the baking dish at the family table.
Often accompanied by a simple side of steamed green vegetables like peas or green beans.
instructions: Prepare lentils: Rinse lentils. Boil lentils in 1 litre water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Prepare vegetables: Dice carrots, onions, celery. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add diced onions, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5 more minutes.
Build base: Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes. Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute.
Add liquids and lentils: Gradually whisk in vegetable stock. Add cooked lentils, chopped thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Cook filling: Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare mash: Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes: Return hot potatoes to the pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble pie: Preheat oven to 190°C. Pour lentil filling into a large oven-safe baking dish (approx. 30x20 cm). Spread mashed potato evenly over the filling.
Bake: Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the potato. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let pie rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Red Lentil Dal with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of rich, golden-yellow red lentil dal is served in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The dal is thick and creamy, with visible softened pieces of tomato, onion, and a scattering of fresh green coriander leaves on top. A vibrant tempering of dark mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and a few dried red chilies glistens on the surface. Alongside the dal, on the same plate, a mound of fluffy, earthy brown rice is placed. Scattered around the plate are roasted vegetables: golden-brown potato cubes with slightly crispy edges, bright orange carrot rounds, and tender-crisp green broccoli florets, and red bell pepper squares, all showing hints of browning from roasting. The overall presentation is warm, inviting, and abundant, as if served for a family meal. The colors are natural and appealing, with the warm hues of the dal and roasted vegetables contrasting with the green coriander and brown rice. The plate is a simple, off-white ceramic dish, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl, and a casually folded cloth napkin completes the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm brown rice.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or a simple cucumber raita.
Serve with Indian flatbread like naan or roti.
Eat using hands or a spoon, often mixing the dal and rice.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium, cut into 2 cm thick rounds

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato cubes, carrot rounds, broccoli florets, and bell pepper squares with 60 ml oil, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, salt, and pepper on a large baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Stir halfway.

Rinse 500 g brown rice. Combine with 1.25 L water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
In a large pot, heat 30 ml oil over medium heat. Add diced onions and sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in 2 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp cumin, and 2 tsp coriander powder. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Add chopped tomatoes and red lentils to the pot. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are very soft and broken down. Stir occasionally.
Stir in coconut milk. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the dal to thicken to a creamy consistency. Season with salt to taste.

In a small pan, heat 30 ml oil over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. Once they begin to splutter, add cumin seeds and dried red chilies (if using). Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add curry leaves (if using) and cook for a few more seconds until crisp.

Pour the hot tadka directly over the cooked dal. Stir gently. Ladle the dal into individual serving bowls. Serve immediately with a side of brown rice and roasted vegetables. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Red Lentil & Vegetable Patties
recipes.visual_description: A rustic ceramic plate holds two round, golden-brown lentil patties. Each patty is about 8 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, with a slightly irregular, homemade shape. The exterior shows a crisp, textured surface, revealing flecks of grated carrot and green coriander. The patties are placed slightly overlapping, creating a natural arrangement. A creamy white dollop of yogurt dip sits adjacent, garnished with fresh, chopped green coriander. Beside the patties, a modest portion of vibrant green salad leaves, loosely arranged, adds a fresh contrast. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table, slightly worn, with visible grain. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling plain yogurt or raita.
Offer with a simple green salad or pickled vegetables.
Can be eaten with hands or fork.
instructions: Rinse red lentils under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine lentils and 1 litre water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until lentils are soft and water is absorbed. Drain any excess water. Mash lentils lightly.
Heat 15 ml oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds. Cook until they splutter.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated carrot, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and optional minced Thai chili. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer cooked vegetable mixture to the mashed lentils.
Add chopped coriander and breadcrumbs to the lentil mixture. Season with salt and black pepper.
Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into 14-16 patties, about 2 cm thick.
Heat remaining vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry patties in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
For the dip: Combine yogurt with lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a small amount of chopped coriander. Mix well.
Serve patties warm with yogurt dip and fresh salad greens.
notes: Ensure lentils are not overcooked to prevent mushiness.
Adjust chili amount to desired spice level.
Patties can be prepared in advance and refrigerated before frying.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Dip
recipes.visual_description: A small, inviting portion of a rustic, golden-orange roasted carrot and chickpea dip sits in a simple, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl. The dip has a creamy, textured consistency, showing flecks of roasted carrot and chickpea, indicative of its homely preparation. It is garnished simply with coarsely chopped fresh green parsley, providing a vibrant color contrast. The bowl is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle signs of wear. Adjacent to the bowl, a few slices of toasted, crusty bread are casually arranged, some with a light golden-brown crust. A simple cloth napkin is folded loosely nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and lived-in atmosphere, reflecting a comfortable family meal setting. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, emphasizing the wholesome, homemade quality of the starter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with various types of crusty bread or pita bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel carrots. Cut carrots into 2 cm chunks.
Peel and quarter the onion.
Peel garlic cloves.
On a large baking tray, combine carrot chunks, onion quarters, and garlic cloves.
Drizzle with 60 ml olive oil. Season with 10 ml ground cumin, 10 ml ground coriander, 5 ml salt, and 2 ml black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until carrots are tender and slightly caramelized.
Drain and rinse the canned chickpeas.
Transfer roasted vegetables and chickpeas to a food processor.
Add remaining 90 ml olive oil and 60 ml fresh lemon juice.
Process until smooth or slightly chunky, based on desired texture.
Taste the dip. Adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed.
Spoon the dip into a serving bowl.
Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley.
Slice crusty bread. Toast bread slices lightly.
Serve the roasted carrot and chickpea dip with toasted bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Chickpea & Herb Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown chickpea fritters are casually arranged on a rustic wooden board or a simple, off-white ceramic serving platter. The fritters are small, irregularly shaped disks, showcasing a crispy exterior and a tender, herb-flecked interior with visible green specks of chopped tatsoi and fresh coriander. A small, unglazed ceramic bowl of creamy, white yogurt-lime dip sits nestled among the fritters, garnished with a vibrant lime wedge and a few fresh coriander leaves. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, reflecting a homely, inviting atmosphere. A casually draped linen napkin in a neutral tone completes the comforting presentation. The focus is on the natural textures and inviting warmth of the homemade comfort food.
instructions: Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Chop fresh coriander. Finely chop tatsoi.
In large bowl, combine chickpea flour, diced onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped coriander, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Gradually whisk in water until smooth, thick batter forms. Stir in chopped tatsoi.
Heat 2 cm oil in large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Drop tablespoonfuls of batter into hot oil. Do not overcrowd pan.
Fry 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove and drain on paper towels.
For dip, combine yogurt, lime juice, pinch of salt in small bowl. Stir well.
Serve warm fritters with yogurt-lime dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Parsnip Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust portion of fork-tender braised beef short ribs is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The bone-in short rib, deep brown and glistening, rests atop a creamy, smooth, off-white parsnip puree. Beside the rib, two or three vibrant orange glazed baby carrots are neatly arranged. A rich, glossy, dark brown reduction sauce pools around the base of the rib and is generously spooned over its top, highlighting the meat's tender texture. A small sprig of fresh green thyme garnishes the dish. The plate is presented on a simple, light wooden table, accompanied by a folded dark grey linen napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its colors and textures in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Liquid should almost cover the ribs.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven and braise for 3 to 4 hours, or until ribs are fork-tender.
While ribs braise, prepare parsnip puree. Boil chopped parsnips in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash or blend parsnips with 50g butter and heavy cream until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
