recipes.visual_description: The dish features two golden-brown, pan-seared cashew and cheese patties per plate, positioned slightly overlapping on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Each patty boasts a crisp, textured exterior from the pan-searing, hinting at a creamy interior. A glossy, amber-hued soy-mustard glaze is artfully drizzled over the patties, creating appealing streaks. A small mound of vibrant, lightly blanched green asparagus spears is neatly arranged beside the patties, adding a fresh contrast. The bright green of thinly sliced fresh green onions is sprinkled generously over the patties, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and refined, with moderate negative space on the plate. The table setting includes a simple wooden surface, a crisp white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Boil diced potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Mash until smooth.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, crushed cashews, grated cheese, and sliced green onions. Mix well.
Add beaten egg, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper. Mix until a cohesive mixture forms.
Divide mixture into 8 equal portions. Form each portion into a round patty, about 2 cm thick.
Lightly dust each patty with flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pan-sear patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
While patties cook, prepare the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, Dijon mustard, and maple syrup.
Arrange two cooked patties on each plate. Drizzle generously with soy-mustard glaze.
Serve immediately with blanched asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Blueberry Apple Honey Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Blueberry Apple Honey Tart is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tart slice features a golden-brown, flaky pastry crust with a visible crimped edge. The filling is a harmonious mix of thinly sliced, tender baked apples and plump, bursting blueberries, all glistening with a warm honey glaze. The apple slices are arranged artfully, partially overlapping, showcasing their soft, cooked texture. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly highlights the tart's top, and a small, fresh mint sprig is placed beside the slice for a touch of vibrant green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and a neatly folded cotton napkin, creating a classic bistro setting. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting textures and warm colors.

ingredients.name: medium apples (e.g., Gala, Honeycrisp), peeled, cored, thinly sliced (2-3 mm thick)

instructions: Prepare Pastry: In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, and salt. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add ice water, mixing until dough just comes together. Form into a disc, wrap in plastic, and chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare Filling: In a separate bowl, combine sliced apples, blueberries, 60 ml honey, lemon juice, and cornstarch. Add cinnamon if desired. Mix gently to coat fruit.

Assemble Tart: Preheat oven to 190°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll out chilled dough to a 30 cm circle. Carefully transfer dough to a 23 cm tart pan with a removable bottom. Press dough into bottom and up sides. Trim excess dough.
Fill and Bake: Pour fruit filling into the tart shell. Spread evenly. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and fruit is tender and bubbling.
Prepare Glaze: While tart is still warm, combine 50 ml honey and hot water in a small bowl. Stir until smooth.
Glaze and Cool: Brush honey glaze over the warm tart. Let tart cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving.
notes: For best results, use a firm-fleshed apple variety that holds its shape when baked, such as Gala, Honeycrisp, or Granny Smith.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Salmon and Dill Pasta Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Four golden-brown Smoked Salmon and Dill Pasta Fritters are neatly arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each fritter is approximately 5 cm in diameter, exhibiting a crispy, irregular edge and a visible mix of small pasta shapes and pink salmon flakes. A small dollop of crème fraîche or plain Greek yogurt sits beside the fritters. A few fresh dill sprigs are scattered artfully over and around the fritters. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A folded grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the fritters' texture. The background is softly blurred, showing a hint of a casual restaurant environment. No overcrowding; elements are well-proportioned.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to cool quickly. Drain again thoroughly.
In a large bowl, combine cooked pasta, flaked or finely diced smoked salmon, egg, flour, dill, red onion, lemon zest, and softened cream cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into small patties, about 5 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat a generous amount of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry patties in batches. Cook 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Drain cooked fritters on paper towels. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Veal Loin, Pearl Barley Risotto, Pea Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously plated portion rests on a pristine white bone china plate. The plate, set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, is framed by a folded, crisp white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware. A central, elongated quenelle of creamy, off-white pearl barley risotto forms the base. Beside it, a thick-cut, perfectly pan-seared veal loin medallion, boasting a rich golden-brown crust and a tender pink interior, is precisely placed. A vibrant, deep green pea essence, smooth and lustrous, is artfully drizzled as a contrasting arc along the plate's edge, emphasizing the negative space. A few delicate micro pea tendrils are meticulously placed atop the veal, adding a final touch of fresh green. The scene is bathed in dramatic, professional lighting, casting subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated minimalism. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing all focus to the refined composition.
instructions: Prepare Pea Essence: Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch fresh green peas for 1 minute. Immediately transfer peas to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well. Blend blanched peas with 50 ml of hot vegetable stock until very smooth. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Season pea essence with salt. Keep warm.

Cook Pearl Barley Risotto: In a medium saucepan, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add pearl barley. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine is fully absorbed. Begin adding hot vegetable stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 25-30 minutes until barley is al dente and creamy. Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan (if using) until melted and incorporated. Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid.

Sear Veal Loin: Pat veal loin dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Once oil shimmers, carefully place veal loin in the skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and a crust forms. For medium-rare, internal temperature should reach 57°C. Reduce heat if browning too quickly. Remove veal from skillet. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest for 5-7 minutes. Cut the veal into four thick-cut medallions.

Plate Dish: Place a generous quenelle or elegant smear of pearl barley risotto slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange one thick-cut veal loin medallion beside the risotto. Carefully drizzle or swirl a small amount of the vibrant pea essence around the plate. Garnish with a few delicate micro pea tendrils placed precisely on top of the veal or risotto. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Coriander Green Chili Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coriander Green Chili Chicken Curry is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Large 4 cm chunks of tender chicken are nestled within a rich, vibrant green-brown curry sauce, which pools elegantly around the chicken. The sauce has a glossy sheen, indicating its depth. Fresh, bright green coriander leaves are scattered atop the chicken and sauce, along with thin, shimmering julienned ginger, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate, a small white ceramic katori bowl holds fluffy white basmati rice, perfectly mounded. A section of golden-brown, soft naan bread is folded and placed to the side. A small white ceramic bowl contains creamy, white raita, garnished with a single sprig of mint. Traditional Indian metal flatware, a spoon and fork, rest beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface under natural, even lighting. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere, completing an authentic and refined culinary scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with basmati rice.
Accompany with fresh naan bread for scooping the curry.
Offer a side of raita (yogurt with cucumber or boondi) to cool the palate.
Serve with pickled onions (achaar) for an authentic accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Fresh green chilies (Serrano or similar), deseeded and roughly chopped
Red chili powder (Kashmiri or similar), optional

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large 4 cm chunks. Season with 0.5 teaspoon salt. Set aside.
Combine chopped green chilies and 80g fresh coriander leaves in a blender. Add a splash of water. Blend to a smooth, vibrant green paste. Set aside.
Heat oil or ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add whole cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add finely diced onions to the pan. Sauté, stirring frequently, for 10-12 minutes until deeply golden brown and caramelized. This is crucial for flavor (bhunao technique).
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant, ensuring it does not burn.

Reduce heat to low. Add coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder (if using). Stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast spices. Add a tablespoon of water if mixture is too dry to prevent burning.
Add chicken chunks to the pan. Increase heat to medium-high. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides. This locks in juices.

Whisk yogurt until smooth. Reduce heat to low. Gradually add yogurt to the pan, stirring continuously to prevent curdling. Cook for 2-3 minutes until yogurt is fully incorporated and sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the prepared green chili-coriander paste. Mix well. Cook for 2 minutes.

Pour in 150ml water or chicken stock. Add salt to taste. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pan and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F). Stir occasionally. If sauce is too thick, add more water.
Stir in garam masala. Cook uncovered for 2 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf) if desired before serving.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and julienned ginger.
traditional_techniques: Bhunao (sautéing onions and spices until oil separates)
Tadka (tempering whole spices in hot oil)

recipes.recipe_name: Zuppa di Pomodoro e Pasta Piccola
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Zuppa di Pomodoro e Pasta Piccola is presented in a clean, smooth white porcelain soup bowl, positioned centrally on a light, distressed wooden table. The soup displays a rich, warm reddish-orange hue, characteristic of ripe San Marzano tomatoes, with a velvety smooth consistency. Small, al dente ditalini pasta shapes are visible, suspended throughout the vibrant liquid. A small cluster of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves rests gently on the surface, offering a fragrant contrast. A delicate swirl of golden-green extra virgin olive oil glistens on the soup's surface. Freshly grated pale yellow Parmigiano Reggiano cheese is lightly sprinkled over the basil and oil. A polished silver soup spoon is placed neatly beside the bowl on a folded natural linen napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, warm bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with crusty Italian bread (pane casereccio) for dipping.
Offer additional grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in San Marzano tomatoes. Break tomatoes with a spoon. Add sugar. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 15 minutes.
Carefully transfer half of the soup to a blender. Blend until smooth. Return blended soup to the pot.
Bring a separate pot of salted water to a boil. Cook small pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add cooked pasta to the soup. Season soup with salt and black pepper.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh basil leaves, a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti alle Vongole
recipes.visual_description: The dish features spaghetti swirled in the center of a white porcelain shallow bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent emulsion of olive oil and clam liquor, speckled with finely minced parsley and red chili flakes. Whole, steamed clams in grey-flecked shells are nested naturally around the pasta, showcasing plump, tender meat. The plate sits on a light oak bistro table. Beside the bowl is a small side plate for shells and a piece of crusty bread. A silver fork rests on a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the shells and the silky sauce. The arrangement is clean with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Provide a side plate for discarded shells
Serve with crusty bread for 'scarpetta' to soak up the sauce
instructions: Soak clams in cold salted water for 1 hour.
Rinse clams thoroughly to remove sand.
Boil 4 liters of water with 10g salt.
Cook spaghetti until 2 minutes before al dente.
Sauté garlic and chili flakes in olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add clams and white wine to the pan.
Cover with a lid and steam until all clams open.
Transfer pasta directly to the clam pan using tongs.
Add 50ml of reserved pasta water.
Toss vigorously over high heat until the sauce emulsifies and coats the pasta.
Stir in chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.
notes: Discard any clams that do not open after steaming.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Olives and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, braised chicken thighs are positioned centrally, their crispy skin glistening. A rich, deep red sauce generously coats the chicken and pools around it. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes and dark purple Kalamata olives are nestled within the sauce, adding pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The chicken is served whole, not sliced. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and basic silverware are placed beside the plate, creating a casual yet refined bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken stock, halved cherry tomatoes, pitted Kalamata olives, rosemary, and thyme. Stir to combine.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Transfer pot to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Browning the chicken skin thoroughly before braising adds significant flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom-Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken exhibits a perfectly seared crust, showcasing its savory preparation. A rich, creamy mushroom-thyme sauce is artfully spooned around the base of the chicken, allowing its natural contours to remain visible. Alongside, vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to tender-crisp perfection, are neatly arranged. A fresh sprig of thyme garnishes the chicken, adding a pop of green. The overall color palette is inviting, featuring the golden chicken, earthy brown sauce, and bright green vegetables. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimal, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add minced shallot and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add 2 sprigs of fresh thyme. Simmer 5 minutes until sauce slightly reduces.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, blanch asparagus spears. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus. Cook 2-3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Serve chicken breasts with mushroom-thyme sauce spooned over and around. Arrange blanched asparagus alongside. Garnish with remaining fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon Orzo is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, crisply roasted chicken pieces, a thigh and a drumstick, are positioned atop a creamy bed of al dente orzo pasta. The chicken skin is taut and caramelized, showing clear signs of high-heat roasting. Scattered around the chicken and orzo are vibrant, burst roasted cherry tomatoes and glossy, deep purple Kalamata olives. The orzo has a slight sheen from lemon juice and olive oil. Fresh, finely chopped parsley is generously sprinkled over the entire dish, adding a pop of bright green. A fresh lemon wedge rests beside the chicken. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, casual dining ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Offer a simple Greek salad with cucumber, tomato, red onion, and feta.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
In a large bowl, toss chicken with 30 ml olive oil. Arrange chicken, skin-side up, on a large baking sheet.
Add cherry tomatoes and Kalamata olives to the same bowl. Toss with remaining 30 ml olive oil and minced garlic. Spread around chicken on the baking sheet.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden brown and crispy. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).

While chicken roasts, cook orzo. Bring chicken broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add orzo. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until liquid is absorbed and orzo is al dente, about 10-12 minutes.
Remove orzo from heat. Stir in zest of one lemon and juice of one lemon. Add half of the chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, spoon a bed of lemon orzo onto each plate. Top with roasted chicken pieces, roasted cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a fresh lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust lemon juice and seasoning in the orzo to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Rice Pilaf is presented on a rustic, matte ceramic plate. A mound of fluffy, golden-hued rice, subtly colored by turmeric, forms the base, with visible flecks of soft, caramelized diced onions mixed throughout. Two seared bone-in chicken thighs, boasting deeply golden-brown and slightly crisped skin, rest naturally atop the rice. The chicken appears moist and tender. A fresh sprinkle of vibrant green chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the dish, providing a bright contrast. The entire plate is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a rustic fork are casually positioned alongside the plate. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting, homely appeal. A small, plain ceramic bowl with a dollop of plain white yogurt is subtly placed to the side, suggesting an optional accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple green salad.
Enjoy as a comforting family meal, served directly from the pot.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice until well coated with the spices and onion, about 1-2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth. Scrape any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture, skin-side up.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the pilaf after cooking allows the rice to fully absorb moisture and become perfectly fluffy.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Skoblyanka
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown pan-fried chicken chunks, rustic potato wedges, and earthy sautéed mushrooms and thick-cut onions are arranged naturally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken and potatoes exhibit a crisp exterior and tender interior, while the mushrooms and onions are soft and caramelized. A vibrant green fresh dill sprig garnishes the dish. A generous dollop of rich, white Smetana (sour cream) is placed to the side. The composition features warm browns, golden yellows, and a touch of green, creating a hearty yet refined appearance. The plate is set on a simple dark wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the textures and inviting warmth of the meal. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a generous dollop of Smetana (sour cream).
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or sauerkraut.
Serve with dark rye bread.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into rustic 3 cm wedges. Roughly chop onion.
Quarter mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add remaining oil to skillet. Add potato wedges. Fry, turning occasionally, until golden brown and tender, about 10-12 minutes. Remove potatoes from skillet.
Add chopped onion and quartered mushrooms to skillet. Sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken and potatoes to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Stir in half of the fresh dill, chopped. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately with a dollop of Smetana and remaining fresh dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Apple Banana Upside-Down Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Caramelized Apple Banana Upside-Down Cake rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The cake showcases a rich, golden-brown caramelized topping of thinly sliced apple half-moons and 1cm thick banana rounds, slightly overlapping in a rustic pattern. The fruit is tender and glistening. Below, the pale yellow cake crumb is visibly moist, studded with soft banana pieces. The thick slice reveals distinct layers. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. In the background, the remaining whole cake is visible on a cooling rack, hinting at a freshly baked, homely dessert. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the inviting scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 18 cm round cake pan.
Melt 40g butter in a small saucepan. Pour into the bottom of the prepared cake pan. Sprinkle 50g brown sugar evenly over the butter.
Peel and core the apple. Slice apple into 5mm thick half-moons. Peel bananas and slice into 1cm thick rounds.
Arrange apple and banana slices over the brown sugar in the pan. Create a rustic pattern.
In a large bowl, cream 60g softened butter and 100g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gently spoon the cake batter over the fruit layer in the pan. Spread evenly to cover all fruit.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.
Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes on a wire rack.
Carefully invert the cake onto a serving plate. Let it cool completely before slicing and serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple & Banana Spiced Loaf Cake with Apple Peel Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick slice of the Apple & Banana Spiced Loaf Cake is centrally placed on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice is light golden-brown with visible specks of darker banana and apple, showcasing a moist, tender crumb. A subtle, translucent sheen of apple peel glaze lightly coats the top, catching the soft, natural light. The plate is set on a textured light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, emphasizing natural materials. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring a hint of soft green from a leafy houseplant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. The overall composition is simple, clean, and highlights the cake's natural beauty and texture without any elaborate garnishes. The cake itself has a rustic, home-baked appeal, inviting and wholesome.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a small loaf pan (approx. 18cm x 9cm).
Cream softened butter and sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Stir in mashed bananas and grated apple.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared loaf pan. Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
While cake bakes, prepare apple peel glaze. Combine apple peels, cores, and water in a small saucepan. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Strain liquid. Discard solids (compost). Return liquid to saucepan. Add sugar and apple cider vinegar. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
Once cake is cool, drizzle with apple peel glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Caramelized Apple and Banana Pudding Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant wedge of warm caramelized apple and banana pudding cake rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The top surface of the cake showcases beautifully caramelized 1cm apple cubes and 1cm banana rounds, glistening with a deep amber caramel. The cake itself is a uniform golden-brown, revealing a soft, tender interior. A small, neat scoop of vanilla bean ice cream or a dollop of crème fraîche is positioned beside the cake, slowly melting into a creamy pool. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly graces the plate. The dish is presented on a simple, light-colored wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dessert, highlighting its warm colors and inviting textures. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, perfect for a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 15cm round baking dish.
Peel and core the apple. Cut into 1cm cubes. Peel bananas. Slice into 1cm thick rounds.
Melt 20g butter and 50g granulated sugar in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook until amber caramel forms.
Add apple cubes to the caramel. Cook for 3 minutes. Add banana slices. Cook for 2 minutes. Stir gently. Pour the fruit and caramel mixture into the prepared baking dish.
In a separate bowl, whisk 40g melted butter and 50g granulated sugar until combined. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract.
In another bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, baking powder, ground cinnamon, and salt.
Alternate adding the dry ingredients and milk to the wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter evenly over the fruit in the baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cool for 5 minutes. Invert the pudding cake onto a serving plate. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Apple and Banana Crumble with Crème Anglaise
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm caramelized apple and banana crumble is presented in a clean white porcelain ramekin. The crumble topping is a rich golden brown, showing distinct textures of baked rolled oats and flour, with some slightly darker, crispier edges. Below, the fruit filling peeks through, showcasing soft, glossy, caramelized small diced apple and thick banana slices. A smooth, pale yellow crème anglaise pools elegantly around the base of the ramekin on the white plate. A small, vibrant green mint sprig is placed delicately beside the ramekin. The setting is a simple wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural light, with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver dessert spoon beside the dish, creating an inviting bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly butter three individual ramekins.
Peel and small dice the apple. Peel and cut bananas into thick slices.
For the fruit filling: Melt 20g butter in a pan over medium heat. Add 30g granulated sugar. Cook until sugar dissolves and turns light amber.
Add diced apple to the pan. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly softened. Add banana slices. Cook 1 minute more. Stir in ground cinnamon. Remove from heat.
Divide fruit mixture evenly among the prepared ramekins.
For the crumble topping: In a bowl, combine all-purpose flour, rolled oats, 50g granulated sugar, and a pinch of salt. Cut in 50g cold unsalted butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Spoon crumble topping evenly over the fruit in each ramekin.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and fruit filling is bubbling.
While crumble bakes, prepare crème anglaise: Whisk egg yolks and 50g granulated sugar in a bowl until pale.
Heat whole milk in a saucepan over medium heat until simmering, but not boiling.
Gradually whisk hot milk into egg yolk mixture to temper. Pour mixture back into saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of the spoon. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Serve warm crumble with crème anglaise poured around the base. Garnish each with a small fresh mint sprig.
notes: Use firm, ripe bananas for best results, they hold their shape better during caramelization.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana and Apple Tarte Tatin
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Banana and Apple Tarte Tatin rests on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, puffed and flaky. Beneath, caramelized banana rounds and apple wedges are visible, glistening with deep amber caramel. The fruit is tender, showing distinct shapes. A small dollop of crème fraîche or a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream sits beside the tart, offering a creamy contrast. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface. A linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the warm tones of the tart. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche
Serve with vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Peel bananas. Slice into 2 cm thick rounds.
Peel, core, and cut apple into 1.5 cm thick wedges.
In a 20 cm oven-safe skillet, melt butter and sugar over medium heat.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until a rich amber caramel forms.
Remove skillet from heat.
Carefully arrange banana rounds and apple wedges in a single layer over the caramel.
Place puff pastry sheet over the fruit. Tuck pastry edges down around the fruit.
Whisk egg yolk with 1 tablespoon water. Brush pastry with egg wash.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Let tart cool in skillet for 5 minutes.
Carefully invert the tart onto a serving plate.
notes: Ensure caramel is not burnt for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Banana Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown Apple and Banana Fritters are piled casually on a rustic ceramic plate, nestled on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. Each fritter is irregularly shaped, showing crispy edges and a soft, fluffy interior studded with small, tender diced apple pieces and mashed banana. A light dusting of white icing sugar covers some of the fritters, contrasting with their warm, inviting color. The plate is slightly off-center, allowing for glimpses of a simple cloth napkin and a well-used fork beside it. Warm, natural light fills the scene, suggesting a cozy home kitchen. The overall presentation is unpretentious and generous, inviting immediate enjoyment, typical of a comforting homemade snack.
instructions: Peel and mash bananas in a large bowl. Ensure no large lumps remain.
Peel, core, and finely dice the apple into small cubes. Add to mashed bananas.
Add granulated sugar, melted butter, and egg to the banana mixture. Whisk until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to the wet mixture. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or Dutch oven over medium heat to 175°C.
Carefully drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm. Dust with icing sugar if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage, Pancetta, and Pecorino Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage, Pancetta, and Pecorino Cream is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, reddish-orange creamy tomato sauce, generously studded with browned, crumbled spicy Italian sausage and golden-brown diced pancetta. Flecks of vibrant green chopped parsley and white grated Pecorino Romano are visible throughout. The pasta is piled organically in the center of the plate, allowing for moderate negative space. The dish is topped with additional crispy pancetta and fresh parsley. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, natural even lighting, and a subtle restaurant-style background. A folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware are placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into small pieces.
Dice pancetta into 1 cm cubes.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage, set aside.
Add diced pancetta to the same skillet. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta, set aside.
Drain most fat, leaving about 15 ml. Add diced onion to skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 10 minutes.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 240 ml pasta water.
Stir heavy cream into tomato sauce. Add cooked sausage back to sauce.
Drain rigatoni. Add pasta directly to the sauce. Add half of the grated Pecorino Romano and 120 ml reserved pasta water.
Toss well to combine. Cook 2 minutes, stirring, until sauce coats pasta. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Stir in most of the crispy pancetta and chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining crispy pancetta, more grated Pecorino Romano, and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Beef and Carrot Soup with Thyme
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of velvety, warm orange Creamy Beef and Carrot Soup is presented in a clean, pristine white porcelain bowl. The soup's surface is smooth and inviting, hinting at its rich, pureed texture. A small, artful sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley and a few delicate fresh thyme leaves are arranged neatly in the center of the soup, providing a vibrant color contrast and a fresh aromatic touch. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the bowl, set on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and inviting texture. The focus remains entirely on the elegantly presented soup, showcasing its natural colors and refined simplicity.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped carrots and fresh thyme leaves. Sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until carrots are very tender.
Remove pot from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until completely smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer soup to a regular blender in batches and blend until smooth.
Stir in mayonnaise until fully incorporated. The soup will become creamy.
Return soup to low heat. Heat gently, do not boil. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish each bowl with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley and a few fresh thyme leaves.
notes: For a richer flavor, roast the carrots before adding them to the soup.
Adjust the amount of mayonnaise to your preferred creaminess and tang.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Corn-Fed Chicken Breast with Saffron Risotto, Heirloom Tomato Confit, and Caramelized Onion Soubise
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Seared Corn-Fed Chicken Breast is presented on an elegant, matte white bone china plate. A golden-skinned, tender chicken breast half, perfectly seared, rests beside a flowing, vibrant orange-red saffron risotto, artfully composed in a natural, organic form, not a ring. Three glossy, deep red heirloom tomato confit halves are meticulously placed near the chicken, their forms slightly collapsed and glistening. A delicate, pale cream-colored smear of caramelized onion soubise provides a subtle accent of contrasting texture and color. A sparse drizzle of golden garlic oil creates subtle pools around the components. A few vibrant green micro-basil leaves offer a precise, singular garnish. The entire composition features abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision of each element. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture. The background is ultra-minimalist and uncluttered, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in small oven-safe dish. Add 4 crushed garlic cloves, 2 thyme sprigs, and 50ml olive oil. Season with salt. Bake for 60-75 minutes until tender and slightly shriveled. Set aside.

Prepare Caramelized Onion Soubise: Thinly slice 2 yellow onions. Heat 20ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Add 50ml chicken stock. Simmer briefly. Transfer to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Keep warm.

Prepare Garlic Oil: Thinly slice remaining 4 garlic cloves. Combine with 80ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Heat gently over very low heat for 15 minutes, do not brown garlic. Remove from heat. Let cool and infuse. Strain garlic oil, discard solids.

Prepare Saffron Risotto: Finely chop 1/2 yellow onion. Heat 20g butter and 20ml olive oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent. Pour in white wine. Cook until absorbed. Add tomato paste. Stir well. Dissolve saffron threads in 50ml warm chicken stock. Add saffron stock to rice. Begin adding remaining warm chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladle to be absorbed before adding next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy. Remove from heat. Stir in 60g butter and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated 180°C oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate: Place a generous quenelle or elegant smear of saffron risotto slightly off-center on each plate. Slice each chicken breast into two thick pieces (not fanned). Place one or two pieces of seared chicken next to the risotto. Arrange 3-4 confit tomatoes artfully beside the chicken. Add a small, precise dot or smear of caramelized onion soubise. Drizzle garlic oil sparingly around the dish. Garnish with a few micro-basil leaves or finely snipped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Tonno e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni al Tonno e Pomodoro is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente rigatoni is generously coated in a rustic, vibrant tomato and tuna sauce. The sauce features tender, flaked tuna pieces and brightly colored halved cherry tomatoes, some gently burst. The pasta displays a rich reddish-orange hue from the tomato base, with visible flecks of deep green fresh basil and pale yellow grated Parmesan. A subtle sheen of olive oil enhances its appeal. The rigatoni is arranged loosely in a central mound, allowing the sauce to pool slightly. A scattering of freshly grated Parmesan and a few whole basil leaves garnish the top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and comforting textures, set against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until reduced.
Add halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and burst. Gently crush some with a spoon.
Add drained tuna to the sauce. Break tuna into flakes. Stir to combine.
Add cooked rigatoni to the pan with the sauce. Add half of the reserved pasta water. Toss well to coat.
Continue tossing, adding more pasta water as needed, until sauce coats pasta beautifully.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the fresh basil and half of the grated Parmesan.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining basil and Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Romaine Southwestern Chopped Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Romaine Southwestern Chopped Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally mounded. Crisp chopped romaine lettuce forms the base, generously interspersed with bright yellow roasted corn kernels, diced ripe red tomatoes, creamy green avocado cubes, and a scattering of dark black beans. Thinly sliced red onion and shredded sharp cheddar cheese add contrasting colors. The salad is lightly coated with a glistening chili-lime vinaigrette. Crushed, golden-brown corn tortilla chips are sprinkled over the top, adding visible crunch, alongside a few bits of crispy crumbled bacon. The balanced composition showcases varied textures and vibrant colors. The plate sits on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting. A fork is placed beside the plate. A small, rustic ceramic bowl containing extra chili-lime dressing enhances the Southwestern theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a small bowl of fresh salsa or guacamole as an accompaniment.
instructions: Prepare bacon: Cook bacon until crispy. Drain fat. Crumble into small bits. Set aside.
Prepare vegetables: Wash and chop romaine lettuce. Dice tomatoes. Dice avocado. Thinly slice red onion. Drain and rinse black beans.
Roast corn: If using fresh or frozen corn, roast kernels in a dry pan over medium-high heat until slightly charred. Let cool.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Combine salad: In a large bowl, combine chopped romaine, roasted corn, diced tomatoes, black beans, red onion, shredded cheddar cheese, and diced avocado.
Dress salad: Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Plate and serve: Divide salad among four plates. Top each serving with crushed corn tortilla chips and crumbled bacon.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Bake is served on a modest, round, off-white ceramic plate with subtle imperfections, resting on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. The dish features tender, roasted chicken chunks, golden-orange 2 cm cubes of butternut squash, vibrant red 2 cm squares of bell pepper, soft diced onion, and thinly sliced celery, all coated in a rich, creamy, lightly spiced sauce with visible flecks of red paprika and chili. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color and freshness. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin and simple, everyday stainless steel fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed family dining area with a lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Peel butternut squash. Cut squash into 2 cm cubes. Deseed red bell pepper. Cut bell pepper into 2 cm squares. Dice yellow onion. Thinly slice celery stalk. Mince garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken chunks, squash cubes, bell pepper squares, diced onion, and sliced celery.
Add mayonnaise, chili powder, smoked paprika, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and black pepper to the bowl.
Toss all ingredients until well coated.
Spread the mixture evenly in a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Roasted Butternut Squash
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared pork loin medallions rest on a clean white porcelain plate. The pork, cooked to a tender pink interior with a golden-brown crust, is presented as two thick, unsliced pieces per serving. Alongside, vibrant orange roasted butternut squash cubes display caramelized edges. Tender-crisp celery batons are arranged nearby. A creamy, pale green celery remoulade is artfully dolloped beside the pork, garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley. The dish features a balanced composition with moderate negative space, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and polished silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, focusing entirely on the plated dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel butternut squash. Cut squash into 2cm cubes.
Toss squash cubes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and caramelized. Set aside.
Finely dice one celery stalk. Set aside for remoulade. Slice the second celery stalk into 2cm batons. Set aside.

Prepare celery remoulade: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Stir in the finely diced celery and 10g chopped fresh parsley. Mix well. Refrigerate until serving.
Pat pork loin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear pork loin for 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden brown all over. Add butter, thyme sprigs, and crushed garlic clove to the skillet. Baste pork with melted butter.

Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 65°C. Remove from oven. Loosely tent with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes (temperature will rise to 70-75°C).
While pork rests, add celery batons and 50ml water to the skillet with pan drippings. Simmer over medium heat for 3-5 minutes, until celery is tender-crisp and water has reduced.
Slice pork loin into 2cm thick medallions. Do not fan slices.
Arrange pork medallions on plates. Place roasted squash cubes and celery batons alongside. Add a dollop of celery remoulade. Garnish with remaining chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Butternut Squash and Celery Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Butternut Squash and Celery Risotto is presented in a shallow, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a warm, inviting golden-orange hue from the squash, is fluid and free-flowing, settling naturally in the bowl without being molded. Visible throughout the creamy rice are small, tender 1 cm cubes of roasted butternut squash, their edges slightly caramelized, and thin, vibrant green slices of fresh celery, adding both color and a delicate crunch. A scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a bright green contrast. The texture is rich and velvety, with individual al dente rice grains discernible. The dish is placed on a simple light wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. Beside the bowl, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a set of classic silver flatware (fork and spoon) are arranged. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting illuminating the dish from above, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately upon preparation to maintain optimal creamy texture.
Enjoy with a glass of the same dry white wine used in the recipe.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table for additional seasoning.

ingredients.name: Butternut Squash
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled, deseeded, cut into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Heat 10ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add squash cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened and lightly caramelized. Remove squash from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 5ml olive oil and 10g butter to the same pan. Add diced shallot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic and half of the sliced celery. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Begin adding warm vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
After about 10 minutes, add the cooked squash back into the risotto. Continue adding broth.
When the risotto is creamy and the rice is al dente (has a slight bite), remove from heat. This should be after approximately 18-20 minutes total cooking time for the rice.
Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to create a creamy texture (mantecatura).
Stir in the remaining half of the fresh, thinly sliced celery and chopped fresh parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta, Russian Style
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. Thick chunks of pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden hue, are interspersed among al dente fettuccine pasta strands. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced onions are evenly distributed, coated in a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. Fresh, vibrant green dill sprigs are generously scattered over the top, providing a striking color contrast and aromatic garnish. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the pasta to flow naturally. The setting is a modern bistro, with a folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors. In the background, a subtle, casual restaurant atmosphere is visible, ensuring the focus remains on the food. A small, rustic ceramic bowl with additional fresh dill is placed nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of dark rye bread.
Offer a side of pickled cucumbers (ogurtsy).
instructions: Cook fettuccine according to package directions. Reserve 125ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken breast into thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add finely diced onion and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in sour cream until fully combined and sauce is smooth. Do not boil.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir in half of the chopped fresh dill.
Add drained pasta to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly with the sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh dill.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Milk Crémeux, Coffee Gel, Teff Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is elegantly presented on a matte black ceramic plate, resting on a grey veined marble surface. In the center, a perfectly set, pale ivory Spiced Milk Crémeux (6 cm diameter, 3 cm high) gleams softly. Beside it, a cluster of glistening, dark amber Coffee Gel cubes (1 cm squares) provides striking color and textural contrast. A delicate, golden-brown Teff Crisp, thin and irregularly shaped, stands partially upright, offering architectural height. Scattered sparingly around the base are tiny, translucent pieces of finely diced candied ginger, adding sparkle. The asymmetrical composition features abundant negative space, emphasizing precision. A folded white linen napkin and a modern silver dessert spoon complete the setting. Dramatic professional lighting with shadows highlights the dish, against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of traditional Ethiopian coffee (Buna) on the side.
instructions: Prepare Spiced Milk Crémeux:
Combine milk, cream, crushed cardamom, cinnamon stick, and vanilla bean in a saucepan. Heat to a simmer. Remove from heat. Steep 20 minutes.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until pale.
Strain infused milk mixture into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (82°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Strain crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Pour into small ramekins or molds. Chill 4 hours, or until set.
Prepare Coffee Gel:
Combine brewed coffee, sugar, and agar-agar in a small saucepan. Whisk well.
Bring to a boil. Simmer 1 minute, whisking.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, cut into small cubes or blend until smooth for a gel.
Prepare Teff Crisp:
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk teff flour, sugar, melted butter, and egg white until smooth.
Spread thin layers of batter onto parchment paper using an offset spatula. Create irregular, organic shapes.
Bake 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp.
Remove from oven. Immediately shape over a rolling pin or bottle if curved crisps are desired. Cool completely.
Assemble Dish:
Unmold crémeux onto center of each plate.
Arrange coffee gel cubes or a swoosh of blended gel beside the crémeux.
Place a teff crisp artfully on or next to the crémeux.
Garnish with finely diced candied ginger.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at precise temperatures for optimal texture and setting.
For the crémeux, precise cooking to 82°C is crucial to prevent curdling and achieve perfect consistency.
The teff crisp batter must be spread very thinly for maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti with Burst Cherry Tomatoes and Confit Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of golden spaghetti, gently coiled, rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Vibrant red burst cherry tomatoes, some whole, some crushed, are scattered throughout, creating pockets of glossy sauce. Soft, golden confit garlic cloves are nestled among pasta strands. Fresh green basil leaves, torn, are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color. Spaghetti is coated in a glistening, emulsified sauce, clinging beautifully to each strand. Pasta appears al dente; tomatoes are soft and juicy. A fine dusting of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese lightly covers the dish. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is beside it. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting textures. This is a single, generous individual portion, presented as a satisfying main course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Serve with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as a Chianti.
instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Peel garlic cloves from 2 heads. Place in a small saucepan. Cover completely with extra virgin olive oil. Simmer gently over low heat for 30-40 minutes, until garlic is very tender and golden. Do not brown. Let cool slightly.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Sauté Tomatoes: While pasta cooks, heat 30ml confit garlic oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add cherry tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until tomatoes soften and burst, releasing their juices. Lightly crush some tomatoes with a spoon.
Combine Sauce: Add confit garlic cloves to the skillet. Gently mash a few cloves into the sauce. Add drained spaghetti to the skillet. Toss well to coat.
Adjust Consistency: Add reserved pasta water, 50ml at a time, tossing continuously until a glossy sauce forms and pasta is well coated.

Finish and Serve: Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves (torn). Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Plate immediately. Garnish each serving with more fresh basil leaves and a generous grating of Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken, Saffron Risotto, Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, artfully composed serving is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The centerpiece is a perfectly seared chicken breast, displaying a rich golden-brown crust and moist interior, positioned slightly off-center. Beside the chicken, a generous, fluid 'swoosh' of vibrant, sun-yellow saffron risotto creates a soft, inviting curve, showcasing its creamy texture. Scattered delicately around the chicken and risotto are ruby-red confit cherry tomatoes, some whole and glossy, others gently burst, adding a pop of color and softness. A sparse, precise scattering of delicate, golden-brown crispy shallots provides a textural contrast and a subtle onion note. A tiny, fresh thyme sprig is placed with architectural precision as a final verdant accent. Abundant negative space on the plate emphasizes the dish's sophisticated minimalism. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates elegant shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, and elegant silver flatware complete the refined, ultra-minimalist dining experience.
instructions: Preheat oven to 140°C. For Tomato Confit: Place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Add 1 minced garlic clove and 2 thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 45-60 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly shriveled. Remove and set aside.

For Crispy Shallots: Thinly slice shallots into rings. Heat 30ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add shallots and fry gently, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. This takes 10-15 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.

For Saffron Risotto: In a medium saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add remaining minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until translucent at the edges. Pour in white wine. Cook until wine is absorbed.

Dissolve saffron threads in a small amount of hot chicken stock. Add a ladleful of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is almost absorbed. Continue adding stock ladle by ladle, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy. Stir in remaining butter and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

For Seared Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Once shimmering, place chicken breasts in skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and a crust forms. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing thickly or serving whole.

To Plate: Create an elegant pool or 'swoosh' of saffron risotto on a large, minimalist plate. Place one seared chicken breast (whole or sliced thickly into 2-3 pieces) beside the risotto. Arrange a few confit cherry tomatoes artistically around the chicken and risotto. Garnish with a sprinkle of crispy shallots and a small fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Gouda and Onion Stuffed Chicken with Grilled Watermelon and Cacao-Hazelnut Dust
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Gouda and Onion Stuffed Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. Each pan-seared chicken breast is cut into two thick, distinct angled pieces, revealing the melted, golden Gouda and rich, dark caramelized onions within. The chicken has a beautiful golden-brown crust. Beside the chicken, a neat cluster of vibrant red grilled watermelon cubes displays subtle char marks, adding a contrasting pop of color and texture. A light, glossy pan sauce is drizzled artfully over the chicken. A delicate sprinkle of dark brown cacao-hazelnut dust lightly covers parts of the chicken and watermelon, providing textural interest and a subtle earthy hue. Fresh green thyme leaves are scattered as a garnish. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting features a simple cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate and standard silver cutlery. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Thinly slice onions. In a large pan, melt 5g butter and 15ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside to cool slightly.
Grate Gouda cheese.
Butterfly each chicken breast: slice horizontally almost all the way through, opening like a book. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Fill each chicken breast with an even amount of caramelized onions and grated Gouda. Fold chicken over and secure with toothpicks if needed.

In an oven-safe pan, heat remaining 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and let rest on a cutting board.
While chicken bakes, cut watermelon into 2cm cubes.

Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high. Grill watermelon cubes for 2-3 minutes per side until grill marks appear and watermelon slightly softens. Remove from heat. Squeeze lemon juice over grilled watermelon. Season with a pinch of salt.
Toast hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned. Let cool. Roughly chop hazelnuts.
Combine chopped hazelnuts and cacao powder. Mix well to create a dust.
Deglaze the pan used for chicken: add chicken stock and scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced. Stir in remaining 10g butter until melted. Remove thyme sprigs.

To serve, slice each chicken breast into two thick, angled pieces to expose the filling. Arrange two chicken pieces on each plate. Place grilled watermelon cubes beside the chicken. Drizzle pan sauce over chicken. Sprinkle cacao-hazelnut dust over chicken and watermelon. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Ginger Glazed Pork Loin with Apple and Blue Cheese Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown cross-section of roasted pork loin sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The exposed interior reveals a vibrant, savory stuffing of tender, small-diced apple chunks, crumbled blue cheese, and finely minced onion and ginger, creating a textural and color contrast. The pork exterior is seared to a deep caramel, then roasted, showcasing a slight sheen from the honey-ginger glaze that pools lightly at the base of the pork and is drizzled sparingly over the top. A small sprig of fresh thyme rests beside the pork. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against a softly blurred, casual bistro background.

ingredients.name: Apples, firm (e.g., Honeycrisp or Granny Smith)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Prepare stuffing: Heat 15 ml olive oil and butter in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced ginger and garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add small-diced apples to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened. Remove from heat.
Transfer apple mixture to a bowl. Stir in crumbled blue cheese and breadcrumbs. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.

Prepare pork loin: Butterfly the pork loin roast. Make a lengthwise cut almost all the way through, then open it like a book. Cover with plastic wrap. Pound lightly to an even thickness of about 2 cm.
Spread stuffing evenly over the flattened pork loin, leaving a small border. Roll the pork loin tightly from one long side. Secure with kitchen twine at 3 cm intervals.
Season the outside of the rolled pork loin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the skillet with the pork loin to the preheated oven. Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.

While pork roasts, prepare glaze: In a small saucepan, combine honey, minced ginger (additional 5g if desired for stronger ginger flavor in glaze), and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Once pork is cooked, remove from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Remove kitchen twine. Slice the pork loin into thick cross-sections. Serve individual portions with a drizzle of the honey-ginger glaze. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Cottage Cheese Ravioli with Sage Butter
recipes.visual_description: Six to eight golden-yellow ravioli are neatly arranged on a round, pristine white porcelain plate, slightly overlapping. A glossy, amber sage butter sauce gently coats each ravioli, pooling slightly at the base. Several vibrant green, crisp-fried sage leaves are artfully scattered over the dish. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The dish showcases rich golden pasta, deep brown mushroom filling peeking from inside a few open ravioli, bright green sage, and creamy white cheese. The plate rests on a warm, light-toned wooden table. A simple, folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle highlights on the pasta. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a Primi Piatti (first course) or a light main course.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Prepare pasta dough: Combine flour and salt on a clean surface. Make a well in the center. Crack eggs into the well. Gradually incorporate flour into eggs with a fork. Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in plastic wrap. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

Prepare mushroom filling: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced shallot and garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add finely diced mushrooms. Cook until softened and all liquid has evaporated, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
In a bowl, combine cooled mushrooms, cottage cheese, 50g grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, and egg yolk. Mix well until combined. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Roll out pasta: Divide dough into four portions. Using a pasta machine or rolling pin, roll each portion into thin sheets (setting 6 or 7 on most machines).

Form ravioli: Lay a pasta sheet flat. Place small spoonfuls of filling (about 10g each) evenly spaced on one half of the sheet. Leave space between mounds. Lightly brush water around the filling mounds. Fold the other half of the pasta sheet over the filling. Press gently around each mound to seal, removing air. Use a ravioli cutter or knife to cut individual ravioli. Ensure edges are well sealed.

Cook ravioli: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add ravioli in batches. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until they float and are al dente. Reserve 60 ml pasta cooking water. Drain ravioli.

Make sage butter sauce: While ravioli cooks, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add fresh sage leaves. Cook until butter is lightly browned and sage leaves are crisp, about 3-5 minutes. Be careful not to burn. Remove sage leaves. Add reserved pasta cooking water to the butter. Stir well.
Finish dish: Add cooked ravioli to the skillet with the sage butter sauce. Gently toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with crisp sage leaves and extra grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure the mushroom filling is completely cooled before mixing with cheese to prevent melting.
Do not overfill the ravioli; a small amount is sufficient for proper sealing.
If not serving immediately, place cooked ravioli on a lightly oiled plate to prevent sticking.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple Mango Chocolate Goat Cheese Cookies
recipes.visual_description: The cookies are round and irregularly shaped, with a rustic, homemade appearance. Their color is a warm, light golden-brown, with darker edges. Visible throughout the cookie dough are generous pockets of melted dark chocolate chunks, some slightly oozing, and vibrant orange specks of diced dried mango. Small, creamy white pieces of goat cheese are also visible, some slightly caramelized on the surface. The texture appears chewy in the center with slightly crisp edges. They are casually arranged on a simple ceramic plate, some overlapping slightly, as if just taken from the oven. A few stray chocolate crumbs might be visible on the plate. The entire plate is visible, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table, under warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Cream softened butter and maple syrup in a bowl until smooth.
Beat in the egg. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, whisk together buckwheat flour, almond flour, baking soda, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in dark chocolate chunks, diced dried mango, and crumbled goat cheese.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto prepared baking sheets. Leave space between cookies.
Bake for 12-15 minutes. Edges should be golden. Centers should be set but soft.
Remove from oven. Let cool on baking sheets for 5 minutes.
Transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Braised Pork Belly with Kabocha Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Red Braised Pork Belly with Kabocha Squash is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. On one side, a mound of fluffy white steamed jasmine rice.
