instructions: Rinse red lentils under cold water. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chopped chili, cumin, coriander, and paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in chicken broth. Add rinsed lentils. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender and chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle stew into a bowl.
Top with crumbled feta cheese.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust chili amount for desired spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Pici with Sausage Reduction, Pickled Shallot, and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, off-white bone china plate with a subtle, irregular rim, resting on a polished grey marble surface. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition. A neat swirl of hand-rolled Pici pasta forms the base, its pale golden hue contrasting with the deep, glossy, mahogany-brown Italian sausage reduction that lightly coats and pools beneath it. Precisely arranged, translucent, pale rose-hued pickled shallot rings scatter atop the pasta, adding subtle color and textural contrast. An irregular, golden-amber Parmesan crisp stands upright. A few vibrant green micro basil leaves are strategically placed. The composition is organic and flowing. Dramatic lighting casts soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, sits to the left. An elegant silver fork completes the minimalist setting.

ingredients.name: Shallots, very thinly sliced into rings

instructions: Combine flour and salt. Gradually add warm water. Knead dough 10 minutes until smooth. Cover, rest 30 minutes.
Roll dough thinly. Cut into strips. Roll strips into thick spaghetti-like strands (pici). Dust with semolina to prevent sticking.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add sausage, breaking it up. Brown deeply on all sides. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, 5-7 minutes. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken stock, thyme, bay leaf. Simmer gently 45-60 minutes, until liquid reduces to a concentrated sauce.
Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Return liquid to clean pan. Reduce further until it coats a spoon. Season to taste. Keep warm.
Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over sliced shallots. Let cool.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line baking sheet with parchment paper. Form small mounds of grated Parmesan. Bake 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pici. Cook 3-5 minutes until al dente. Drain, reserving a little pasta water.
Toss cooked pici with a few spoonfuls of sausage reduction. Add a splash of pasta water if needed to emulsify.

Swirl pasta onto the center of each plate. Drizzle with remaining reduction. Arrange a few pickled shallot rings artfully. Place one Parmesan crisp upright. Garnish with micro basil leaves. Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
notes: This recipe elevates humble ingredients through precise technique and careful reduction, focusing on intense flavor and textural contrasts.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Red Lentil and Feta Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Red Lentil and Feta Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly uneven, earthy glaze, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew is a rich, warm reddish-orange, showcasing the creamy, tender red lentils. Small, soft pieces of diced onion and minced garlic are visible, along with flecks of vibrant red chili. The stew has a hearty, slightly thick consistency, appearing natural and comforting. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered generously over the top, creating a beautiful contrast in color and texture. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl. A slice of crusty, artisanal bread is casually placed on the table next to the bowl. The setting is a homely family kitchen, bathed in warm, cozy lighting, with a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the dish and its inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Garnish with fresh parsley or mint leaves
instructions: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water. Drain.
Dice the onion into small cubes. Mince the garlic cloves. Thinly slice the red chili.
Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion to the saucepan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced chili to the saucepan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the saucepan. Stir well.
Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Cook until lentils are tender and stew has thickened. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Season the stew with salt and black pepper to taste.
Crumble the feta cheese.
Serve the hot stew in a bowl. Top with crumbled feta cheese.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.
Lentils will absorb liquid; add a splash more broth or water if the stew becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Lentil Patties with Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single serving of two round, golden-brown red lentil patties, perfectly seared with a slightly crisp exterior. They rest on a bed of vibrant, gently wilted baby spinach, providing a natural green contrast. Each patty is generously topped with a heap of translucent, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onion, its soft pink hues offering a subtle pop of color and delicate texture. Over the pickled onion, a scattering of creamy white feta cheese crumbles adds a textural counterpoint. The composition is clean and minimalist, centered on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The natural textures of the seared patties, the crisp-tender onion, and the soft feta are highlighted. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural light.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Chili-Garlic Paste: Combine chopped chilies, 50g garlic, 5g sea salt, and 50ml filtered water in a clean jar. Seal loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until bubbling and tangy. Blend into a smooth paste. (For a quick version, blend chilies, garlic, a pinch of salt, and a splash of vinegar/lemon juice.)

Prepare Quick-Pickled Red Onion: In a small saucepan, combine 120ml apple cider vinegar, 120ml water, 10g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Cook Lentils: Combine rinsed red lentils and 600ml vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid, reserving if desired.

Sauté Aromatics: While lentils cook, heat 30ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add finely diced 1 medium onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced 2 garlic cloves and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.

Form Patties: Transfer cooked lentils to a large bowl. Add sautéed onion and garlic, breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, 15-30g of the fermented chili-garlic paste (adjust to taste), salt, and pepper. Mix well to combine. Form the mixture into 8 equal-sized patties.
Cook Patties: Heat a large non-stick pan with a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
Assemble and Serve: Arrange 2 patties per plate. Top with a generous spoonful of quick-pickled red onion and crumbled feta cheese. Serve with a side of seasonal greens or roasted vegetables.
notes: Reserved lentil cooking liquid can be used as a base for soups or sauces, contributing to zero-waste.
Any leftover fermented chili-garlic paste can be stored in the refrigerator for weeks and used in other dishes.
Use stale bread for breadcrumbs to reduce food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs are centered, featuring deeply seared, golden-brown skin glazed with a vibrant red tomato ragu. The sauce is thick and rustic, containing visible chunks of softened yellow onion, earthy-brown halved cremini mushrooms, and blistered red cherry tomatoes. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered loosely over the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a small plate of crusty ciabatta bread. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the glossy texture of the sauce and the organic arrangement of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta or focaccia to mop up the sauce.
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
Present in a wide shallow bowl to highlight the rustic braise.
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion and halved mushrooms to the skillet.
Sauté for 5 minutes until onions are translucent and mushrooms are browned.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in fresh torn basil and serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality canned San Marzano tomatoes for the most authentic flavor profile.
Do not remove the chicken skin, as it provides essential fat and flavor to the braising liquid.
If the sauce is too thick, add a splash more chicken stock at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Corn and Brown Rice Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, set on a well-used, light-toned wooden dining table. Three golden-brown, irregularly shaped Cheesy Corn and Brown Rice Fritters are casually arranged on the plate, slightly overlapping, creating a natural, homely feel. Each fritter is roughly 8cm in diameter and 1.5cm thick, showcasing visible whole corn kernels and the distinct texture of brown rice grains embedded within their crispy, slightly irregular surfaces. A generous dollop of creamy white sour cream is placed beside the fritters. A light sprinkling of finely chopped fresh green chives adds a pop of color over the sour cream and fritters. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with golden browns, creamy whites, and vibrant greens. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggesting natural light from a kitchen window. A casually placed, folded beige cloth napkin and a simple fork are nearby, reinforcing a relaxed, family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, focusing entirely on the comforting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of sour cream or plain yogurt.
Garnish with chopped chives or spring onion.
instructions: Combine flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Whisk well.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg and milk.
Add egg mixture to flour mixture. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in corn kernels, cooked brown rice, and shredded Cheddar cheese.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls (about 50g each) of batter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly to form round patties.
Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Roulade, Tomato Confit, Mozzarella Cloud
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated starter. Two thick-cut medallions of golden-seared chicken roulade, revealing a subtle filling of finely diced roasted red bell pepper, black olive, and red onion, are positioned centrally on a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent, a small, vibrant mound of slow-roasted cherry tomato confit glistens with olive oil. A delicate quenelle of creamy white mozzarella sits nearby, its soft texture contrasting with the other elements. A precise, glossy swirl of amber-hued mustard-thyme jus encircles the components. A few bright green sunflower sprouts are meticulously placed for verticality and fresh color. The presentation is architectural and minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate rests on a cool white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a crisply folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware, under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Finely dice roasted red bell pepper, black olives, and red onion. Roughly chop fresh oregano.

Pound chicken breasts thin and even. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Spread diced bell pepper, olive, onion, and oregano evenly over each pounded chicken breast. Roll each breast tightly into a roulade.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades until golden brown on all sides. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest roulades for 5 minutes before slicing.

For the tomato confit, toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast in the same 180°C oven for 20-25 minutes, until softened and slightly shriveled.

For the mozzarella cream, gently melt fresh mozzarella with milk or light cream in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Blend with an immersion blender until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Chill slightly.

For the mustard-thyme jus, deglaze the chicken searing pan with chicken stock. Add Dijon mustard and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, until slightly thickened and glossy. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Swirl in cold butter until emulsified.

To plate, slice each rested chicken roulade into two thick medallions. Arrange two chicken medallions on each plate. Spoon a small mound of warm tomato confit beside the chicken. Form a delicate quenelle of chilled mozzarella cream and place it on the plate. Drizzle the mustard-thyme jus around the components. Garnish meticulously with a few sunflower sprouts.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy, golden-white risotto fills a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid and spreads naturally, displaying its al dente texture. Thick, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are arranged organically on top of the risotto, showcasing their crust and tender interior. The risotto is flecked with bright green chopped parsley and thyme, with hints of yellow from lemon zest. The chicken pieces are substantial and clearly defined. A light sprinkling of fresh green parsley and a few delicate sprigs of thyme are scattered over the chicken and risotto. A small mound of freshly grated Parmesan cheese sits beside the chicken. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Standard polished silver flatware (fork and knife) is positioned to the right. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up any remaining sauce.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80g, freshly grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it simmering gently.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large, deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed completely.
Add one ladle of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir constantly until absorbed.

Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter, grated Parmesan, lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped parsley, and thyme.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Slice the rested chicken breasts into thick chunks or medallions. Do not fan.
Serve risotto immediately in warm bowls. Top with chicken chunks. Garnish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken stock is hot before adding to risotto to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is key for creamy risotto.
Risotto should be served immediately as it continues to cook and thicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Orecchiette with Ricotta, Peas, and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain pasta bowl on a simple wooden table surface. The orecchiette pasta is cooked al dente, retaining its distinctive ear shape, and coated in a creamy, off-white ricotta sauce. Vibrant green peas are evenly dispersed throughout the pasta, providing pops of color. The texture is luscious and slightly rustic from the ricotta. A light sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese rests atop the pasta. Fresh, finely chopped oregano leaves are scattered over the dish, adding an aromatic green garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and creamy texture. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Offer additional grated Parmesan at the table.

ingredients.name: Vegetable broth or pasta cooking water

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add green peas to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in ricotta cheese, 60 g of grated Parmesan, lemon zest, and half of the chopped oregano.

Add the cooked and drained orecchiette to the skillet. Gradually add reserved pasta water or vegetable broth, stirring to create a creamy sauce that coats the pasta. Start with 150 ml, add more if needed.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh oregano and a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice can be added just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Mushroom and Potato Bowl with Spicy Crumb and Garlic Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A hearty plant-based bowl is presented on a clean white porcelain bowl, set on a simple wooden table. Roasted potato wedges, golden-brown and slightly crispy, are arranged alongside tender, earthy roasted mushroom halves. Bright green broccoli florets, roasted to tender-crisp perfection, add a vibrant contrast. Nestled beside the roasted vegetables is a portion of creamy, garlic-infused macaroni, its pale yellow strands glistening. The entire dish is generously topped with a golden-brown, coarse spicy jalapeno breadcrumb crumble, adding a textural crunch. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of color. The composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing natural colors and distinct textures. A cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl, with natural, even lighting illuminating the scene, creating an approachable yet refined casual dining presentation.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, cut into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, oregano, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Toss mushrooms with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to the baking tray with potatoes after 15 minutes, or on a separate tray.
Roast potatoes and mushrooms for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.
Toss broccoli florets with remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to the baking tray for the last 10-12 minutes of roasting, or roast on a separate tray until tender-crisp.
While vegetables roast, prepare the spicy crumb. Pulse torn bread, chopped pickled jalapenos, and a pinch of salt in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Heat a small pan over medium heat. Add the breadcrumb mixture. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crisp. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 50 ml pasta water.
In the empty pasta pot, melt vegan butter over medium heat. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cooked macaroni, vegetable stock, and reserved pasta water. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
To serve, arrange roasted potato wedges, mushrooms, and broccoli florets in wide bowls. Add a portion of garlic macaroni.
Top generously with the spicy jalapeno crumb. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Penne
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic pasta bowl. One large, tender chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening with rich tomato sauce, rests prominently atop a generous bed of al dente penne pasta. The vibrant red sauce, infused with diced onions and substantial pieces of red and green bell peppers, coats the pasta and chicken. The sauce has a natural, slightly chunky texture. Fresh, roughly torn green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping in a homely, inviting manner. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a hearty, satisfying portion. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, with a simple cloth napkin casually placed beside the bowl and a traditional fork resting nearby, reflecting a relaxed, family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: small bunch, roughly torn, for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper pieces to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through.
While chicken simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore directly over the cooked pasta. Garnish each portion with fresh torn basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce benefits from a longer, slower simmer, allowing flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Fig and Garlic Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single individual portion. A neat mound of fluffy jasmine rice, studded with vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes and subtle flecks of minced garlic, anchors the left side of the plate. To its right, several golden-brown, seared pork medallions, glistening with a rich, dark soy-fig glaze, are arranged organically. The pork pieces are thick chunks, not sliced. Around the main components, fresh fig quarters with their deep purple skin and pale pink flesh are artfully placed, adding a contrasting color and natural sweetness. A small sprig of fresh green coriander rests atop the pork or rice, providing a fresh garnish. The color palette is balanced with rich browns, deep reds/purples, and bright greens against the white rice. The textures are varied: tender pork, soft rice, and the smooth glaze. The composition features moderate negative space, providing a professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation. The entire plate is visible, set on a simple wooden table surface with a clean cotton napkin placed beside it. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant-style background.
instructions: Trim pork tenderloin. Cut into 3-4 cm thick medallions. Season pork medallions with salt and pepper.
Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, and grated ginger in a small bowl. This is the glaze.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove pork from pan. Set aside.

Pour glaze mixture into the hot pan. Bring to a simmer. Return pork medallions to the pan. Coat pork evenly with glaze. Cook 1-2 minutes until glaze thickens slightly and coats pork. Remove pork. Keep warm.
Rinse jasmine rice under cold water until water runs clear. Mince garlic cloves. Halve cherry tomatoes.
In a medium saucepan, heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté minced garlic 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add rinsed rice to the saucepan. Stir 1 minute to coat grains. Add 600ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover saucepan tightly. Cook 15 minutes until all water is absorbed. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Gently stir in halved cherry tomatoes into cooked rice. Fluff rice with a fork.
Quarter fresh figs.

To plate, spoon a mound of garlic tomato rice onto each plate. Arrange 3-4 glazed pork medallions beside the rice. Scatter quartered figs around the pork and rice. Garnish with fresh coriander sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Pork and Tomato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of the Filipino Pork and Tomato Stew is artfully plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. The stew features succulent 3-4 cm pork cubes, tender from braising, coated in a rich, glossy reddish-brown sauce. Visible within the sauce are softened diced tomatoes and fragrant minced garlic. A neatly mounded portion of fluffy, pure white jasmine rice sits beside the stew. The dish is vibrantly garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green onions, adding a contrasting green pop. A set of modern, polished stainless steel fork and spoon are placed to the right of the plate. The overall composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, illuminated by natural, even lighting, hinting at a casual yet refined restaurant atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of fresh sliced cucumber or pickled green papaya (atchara) to balance the richness.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, or by hand.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder or belly, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Fresh green onions, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Cut pork shoulder or belly into 3-4 cm cubes.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté chopped onion until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add pork cubes to the pot. Brown pork on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce, vinegar, and water or broth. Add diced tomatoes, bay leaves, and whole black peppercorns.
Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until pork is very tender.
While pork simmers, cook jasmine rice according to package instructions.
Once pork is tender, remove the lid. Increase heat slightly and simmer for 10-15 minutes to reduce the sauce to desired consistency.
Serve the Filipino Pork and Tomato Stew hot with steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with chopped fresh green onions.
notes: The flavor of the stew often improves overnight, making it a great make-ahead dish.
Adjust the amount of vinegar and soy sauce to suit your personal taste preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Chicken Noodles with Quick Pickles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a handcrafted, earthy ceramic bowl, showcasing a single generous portion. Springy egg noodles form a loose base. Tender, browned chicken chunks (2-3 cm) are arranged naturally atop the noodles. Vibrant green bok choy quarters, crisp-tender from stir-frying, are placed alongside. Bright julienned quick-pickled carrots and daikon add a fresh, tangy contrast. A soft-boiled egg, halved cleanly to reveal a creamy, golden yolk, nests among ingredients. A light drizzle of savory sweet soy sauce coats elements. Garnish is minimal: thinly sliced green scallions and a few small cilantro leaves. The composition is unforced, with ample white space. The scene features a light bamboo surface, undyed linen napkin, and simple wooden chopsticks. Soft, natural lighting highlights ingredients' beauty and textures, with a clean, minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with wooden or bamboo chopsticks.
Offer additional sweet soy sauce or chili oil on the side for personal preference.
instructions: Prepare quick pickles: Julienne carrot and daikon radish. In a bowl, combine rice vinegar, sugar, and salt. Stir until dissolved. Add julienned vegetables. Let sit for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare chicken stock: Trim chicken thighs. Reserve any bones and trimmings. Simmer bones and trimmings with 500ml water for 30 minutes to make a quick stock. Strain and set aside 100ml for the sauce. Compost remaining solids.
Prepare chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with 2g white pepper and a pinch of salt.
Prepare aromatics: Mince garlic and ginger. Thinly slice shallots. Quarter bok choy heads.
Cook eggs: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 7 minutes for soft-boiled. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel carefully.
Cook noodles: Cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.

Stir-fry chicken: Heat 15ml oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides and cooked through, reaching 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from wok and set aside.

Stir-fry vegetables and aromatics: Add remaining 15ml oil to the wok. Add minced garlic, ginger, and sliced shallots. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant. Add bok choy. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.

Make sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together sweet soy sauce, fermented chili bean paste, 3g white pepper, and 100ml chicken stock. In a separate small bowl, mix cornstarch with 15ml water to make a slurry.

Combine: Pour sauce into the wok. Bring to a simmer. Add cooked chicken back to the wok. Stir to coat. Stir in cornstarch slurry gradually until sauce slightly thickens and coats ingredients. Add cooked noodles. Toss well to combine.
Plate: Divide noodles, chicken, and bok choy among 4 serving bowls. Arrange julienned quick pickles alongside. Halve each soft-boiled egg and place one half on top of each serving.
Garnish: Thinly slice green parts of scallions. Roughly chop cilantro. Garnish each bowl with scallions and a few cilantro leaves.
notes: This recipe minimizes waste by utilizing chicken trimmings for stock and preserving vegetables through quick pickling.
Adjust the amount of fermented chili bean paste to your preferred spice level.
Consider composting any remaining vegetable scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemongrass Chicken Supreme with Crispy Sticky Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemongrass Chicken Supreme is precisely arranged on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate. A golden-skinned, pan-seared chicken supreme, cooked to tender perfection, anchors the left side. Its skin is visibly crisp, showcasing delicate crackle. Adjacent, a compact, golden-brown crispy sticky rice cake offers textural contrast. A vibrant, deep red charred tomato-bird's eye chili jam, with visible flecks of chili and softened tomato, is artfully placed, offering a burst of color. A small, carefully composed cluster of fresh, vibrant green micro cilantro, Thai basil, and mint leaves rests atop the jam, providing a fresh, delicate accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing the minimalist and sophisticated composition. The plate sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant dark wood chopsticks. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies and lime juice) on the side for individual seasoning adjustment.
instructions: Rinse glutinous rice. Soak in cold water for 4 hours, or overnight. Drain well.
Steam soaked rice for 25-30 minutes until tender. Press rice into 4 compact rectangles (approx. 8x4cm). Set aside.
Pat chicken supremes dry. Season with salt and pepper. Gently rub with bruised lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Let infuse for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Place cherry tomatoes and bird's eye chilies on a baking tray. Char in oven for 10-15 minutes until blistered. Cool slightly. Roughly chop chilies. Keep tomatoes whole.

Finely dice shallots and garlic. Heat 10ml oil in a small saucepan. Sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add charred tomatoes, chopped chilies, fish sauce, palm sugar, and 15ml lime juice. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened into a jam-like consistency. Adjust seasoning. Set aside.

Heat 20ml oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken supremes skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
In a separate pan, heat a small amount of oil. Pan-fry pressed sticky rice cakes for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel.
Combine micro cilantro, Thai basil, and mint leaves. Lightly dress with remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt.

To plate, place one crispy sticky rice cake on a plate. Position one chicken supreme next to it. Spoon a generous dollop of charred tomato-chili jam beside the chicken. Garnish with a small, artfully arranged cluster of the fresh herb salad. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For the crispy sticky rice, pressing it firmly before frying is key to achieving a good crust.
The charring of tomatoes and chilies is crucial for the jam's depth of flavor.
traditional_techniques: Balancing Thai flavors (sweet, sour, salty, spicy)

recipes.recipe_name: Sous-Vide Chicken Supreme with Pea Velouté and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared chicken supreme, with its golden-brown, crispy skin and succulent white flesh, is positioned slightly off-center on a pristine, large white modern designer plate. A vibrant emerald green, velvety pea velouté forms an elegant, organic pool beside the chicken. Three to four glistening, halved confit cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled and caramelized, are strategically placed to add pops of deep ruby red. A delicate sprinkle of golden-brown toasted cashew crumble provides textural contrast. A few tiny, fresh micro basil leaves are precisely placed on or near the chicken for a final touch of color and freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a white Carrara marble surface with a modern, minimalist bone china plate. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, lies neatly beside elegant silver flatware. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's contours against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course in an elegant, modern Italian dining setting.
Pair with a light-bodied, crisp Italian white wine, such as a Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Micro basil or chervil for garnish

instructions: Preheat a water bath to 63°C for sous-vide cooking. Season chicken supremes generously with salt and pepper. Place each supreme with a thyme sprig into individual vacuum-sealable bags. Seal bags, removing all air.
Cook chicken in the water bath for 1.5 hours. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Prepare tomato confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add 20ml olive oil, 2 thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper. Bake at 140°C for 45-60 minutes, until softened and slightly caramelized.
Toast cashews: Spread cashews on a baking sheet. Toast in oven at 160°C for 8-10 minutes, until golden. Cool, then coarsely chop to create a crumble.
Prepare pea velouté: Melt 20g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Do not brown.
Add frozen green peas to the saucepan. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, until peas are tender. Remove from heat.

Transfer pea mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until perfectly smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan for extra silkiness. Reheat gently. Whisk in remaining 30g butter until incorporated and glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Remove chicken from sous-vide bags. Pat skin very dry with paper towels. Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear flesh-side down for 1 minute to finish.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before plating.

To plate: Spoon an organic pool or an artful swipe of pea velouté onto each plate. Carefully place one whole seared chicken supreme beside the velouté. Arrange 3-4 halved confit cherry tomatoes around the chicken. Sprinkle a small amount of toasted cashew crumble over the velouté and around the chicken. Garnish with a few micro basil or chervil leaves.
notes: Precision in sous-vide cooking ensures perfectly tender and juicy chicken.
Passing the velouté through a sieve is crucial for its ultra-smooth texture.
Ensure chicken skin is thoroughly dried before searing for maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Bacon Consommé, Pork Sausage Quenelle, Carrot Essence
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, deep white bone china bowl holds a luminous, amber-hued smoked bacon consommé. The liquid is crystal clear, reflecting light. Centered within the consommé are two perfectly formed, pale, oval-shaped pork sausage quenelles, their smooth surfaces contrasting with the liquid. Scattered sparsely around the quenelles are tiny, vibrant orange carrot brunoise, their precise cuts evident. On the immaculate white rim of the bowl, or delicately placed next to a quenelle, is a single, precise dot of dark, glossy Worcestershire gel, offering a bold visual accent. A few delicate green micro-herbs, like chervil or dill, are artfully placed on the quenelles, providing a subtle pop of color and freshness. The presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, showcasing the purity and elegance of each meticulously prepared element. The bowl sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft shadows, creating a sophisticated and ultra-minimalist tableau. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests nearby.
instructions: Prepare Consommé Base: Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Render bacon fat in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Remove crisp bacon bits; reserve for another use or discard. Leave rendered fat in the pot. Add finely chopped onion and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.

Build Consommé Raft: In a bowl, combine lean pork mince, egg whites, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Add this mixture to the pot with the rendered bacon fat and sautéed aromatics. Pour in 1.5 litres of cold water. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.

Clarify Consommé: Bring the mixture slowly to a simmer over low heat. Do not stir once it starts to heat. A 'raft' will form on the surface, trapping impurities. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes without disturbing the raft. The broth should become clear.

Strain Consommé: Carefully make a small hole in the raft. Ladle the clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a damp cheesecloth into a clean pot. Discard the raft and solids. Season the consommé with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare Sausage Quenelles: Take premium pork sausage meat. If not finely ground, pass through a food processor briefly to create a very smooth paste. Season lightly with salt and white pepper. Using two spoons, form small, elegant quenelles (oval shapes) from the sausage paste.

Cook Sausage Quenelles: Bring a separate pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully drop the sausage quenelles into the simmering water. Poach gently for 5-7 minutes, or until cooked through and firm. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Keep warm.

Prepare Carrot Brunoise: Peel carrots. Cut into very precise 2 mm x 2 mm x 2 mm brunoise (tiny cubes). Blanch the carrot brunoise in boiling water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well.

Prepare Worcestershire Gel: In a small saucepan, combine Worcestershire sauce with 100 ml water. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in agar-agar powder until fully dissolved. Simmer for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish and chill until set. Once firm, cut into small cubes and process in a blender until a smooth, thick gel forms. Transfer to a small piping bag.

Assemble Dish: Ladle a precise amount of hot, clear consommé into the centre of a deep, warm premium bone china bowl. Carefully place two perfectly formed sausage quenelles in the consommé. Scatter a small amount of vibrant carrot brunoise around the quenelles. Pipe one or two tiny, precise dots of Worcestershire gel onto the rim of the bowl or delicately near the quenelles. Garnish with a few delicate micro-herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Loaded Chicken & Cheese Potato Bites
recipes.visual_description: Twelve golden-brown, rustic potato halves are arranged casually on a well-used wooden cutting board. Each potato half is generously mounded with a savory, creamy filling. The filling features visible chunks of tender, cooked chicken, flecks of vibrant green very finely chopped broccoli, and small pieces of red tomato, all bound together with mashed potato. A layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese forms a golden crust on top of each bite. A few scattered, finely chopped fresh green herbs (basil and oregano) are casually sprinkled over the top, adding a touch of color. The arrangement is organic and natural, with some pieces slightly overlapping, creating a homely, inviting appeal. The wooden board rests on a warm, slightly worn wooden dining table. A loosely folded, simple beige linen napkin is casually placed nearby. The lighting is soft and warm, mimicking natural kitchen light, enhancing the comforting textures of the dish. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, free of distractions.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Pierce each potato several times with a fork. Bake for 45-60 minutes until tender.
While potatoes bake, prepare chicken. Cut chicken breast into 1cm cubes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Season with salt and pepper. Remove chicken from pan.

In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté finely diced onion for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and very finely chopped broccoli. Cook for another 3 minutes. Add finely diced tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Carefully cut baked potatoes in half lengthwise. Scoop out potato flesh into a bowl, leaving a thin shell in each half. Mash the scooped potato flesh.

Add cooked chicken cubes, sautéed onion-broccoli-tomato mixture, 100g grated cheddar, finely diced jalapeno, oregano, basil, milk or cream, salt, and pepper to the mashed potatoes. Mix well to combine all ingredients.
Spoon the mixture back into the potato shells, mounding slightly to create a full, generous bite.
Place the filled potato halves on a baking sheet. Sprinkle the remaining 50g grated cheddar on top of each filled potato bite.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the filling is heated through.
Serve warm on a platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Roasted Chicken and Broccoli with Cheesy Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of pan-seared chicken breast chunks, golden-brown and juicy, are artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Alongside, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets and tender, thick-cut roasted carrot wedges are neatly placed, showcasing their caramelized edges. A rich, creamy cheesy garlic sauce is elegantly drizzled over the chicken and vegetables, creating a luscious sheen. Fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, and a sprinkle of dried oregano provide a fresh aromatic garnish. The dish presents a balanced composition with moderate negative space, inviting and professional. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin, and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut chicken breast into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano.
Cut broccoli into florets. Peel carrots and cut into thick 2-3 cm wedges. Peel and quarter the onion.
Toss broccoli, carrots, and onion with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Finely mince garlic cloves and red chili. Add to the same skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Stir in remaining 1 teaspoon dried oregano.
Reduce heat to low. Gradually whisk in shredded mozzarella cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return chicken chunks to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat.
To serve, plate a portion of chicken chunks with roasted vegetables. Spoon generous amount of cheesy garlic sauce over the top. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Pork Belly, Pea Puree, Compressed Tomato, Potato Foam
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly rectangular block of crisped smoked pork belly, its skin a deep golden-brown crackle, rests precisely offset on a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent, a vibrant emerald-green quenelle of velvety pea and mint puree adds a contrasting splash of color. Scattered around the pork are a few jewel-like, translucent pieces of compressed heirloom tomato, their rich red hues catching the light. An ethereal cloud of airy potato foam gently nestles against the other elements. The composition is clean, architectural, with abundant negative space. A single, delicate pea shoot or microgreen sprig provides a final touch of fresh green. The plate sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing depth, against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Rehydrate dried green peas: Soak peas in cold water overnight (at least 8 hours). Drain.

Prepare Smoked Pork Belly: Score the pork belly skin deeply in a diamond pattern. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Place skin-side up on a rack in a roasting tray. Slow roast in a preheated oven at 140°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender. Increase oven temperature to 220°C for 15-20 minutes to crisp the skin. Remove from oven, place a weighted tray on top, and refrigerate overnight to press and compact. Cut into 4 equal rectangular blocks (approximately 5cm x 4cm).

Make Pea and Mint Puree: In a saucepan, combine rehydrated peas with vegetable stock. Simmer until peas are very tender. Drain most of the liquid, reserving a small amount. Add fresh mint leaves and 20g butter to the peas. Blend until extremely smooth using an immersion blender or high-speed blender. Pass the puree through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any skin or fibrous parts. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Compressed Tomatoes: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Blanch cherry tomatoes for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel the skin from the tomatoes. Halve or quarter the tomatoes, carefully removing seeds. In a small bowl, whisk together white balsamic vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add the peeled and deseeded tomato pieces. If available, vacuum seal the tomatoes with the liquid for 30 minutes to compress. Otherwise, marinate for 1 hour.

Make Potato Foam: Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Pass the hot potatoes through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Heat milk and remaining 30g butter until butter is melted. Gradually add hot milk mixture to the riced potatoes, whisking until smooth and light. Season with salt and pepper. Pass the potato mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie or warm water bath.

Finish Pork Belly: Just before serving, preheat oven to 200°C. Place pork belly blocks skin-side up on a baking tray. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until skin is perfectly crispy and crackling. Alternatively, pan-sear skin-side down in a hot, dry pan until crispy.

Plate the dish: On each pristine white plate, place one crisped smoked pork belly block slightly off-center. Create a delicate quenelle or a small, organic swoosh of the vibrant pea and mint puree beside the pork. Artistically scatter 3-4 pieces of compressed tomato around the pork. Gently dispense a cloud of potato foam next to the other elements. Garnish each plate with one or two delicate pea shoots. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pork belly is pressed overnight for even cooking and crisping.
Passing the pea puree and potato mixture through a fine-mesh sieve is crucial for a smooth, refined texture appropriate for fine dining.

recipes.recipe_name: Patatas con Huevos y Frijoles Negros
recipes.special_requests: Spanish cuisine, gluten free. use fried eggs.
recipes.visual_description: A homely, large, off-white ceramic platter rests on a well-used rustic wooden kitchen table. Warm, golden-brown potato rounds, cut into 1 cm thick slices, are casually arranged across the platter, some slightly overlapping. A generous dollop of dark, creamy black bean mixture sits atop each potato. Each bean mound is crowned with a freshly fried egg, its vibrant yellow yolk runny and contrasting with the crisp, white edges. A light sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh accent. A folded linen cloth napkin in a muted tone is casually placed beside the platter. Warm, inviting lighting from above fills the scene, creating a cozy family dining atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 1 cm thick rounds.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add potato rounds in a single layer.
Cook potatoes for 15-20 minutes. Turn occasionally until golden brown and tender. Season with salt. Remove potatoes from pan and keep warm.
In the same pan, add a little more olive oil if needed. Add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed black beans, ground cumin, and gluten-free soy sauce to the pan. Mash beans slightly with a fork.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in cream cheese until melted and combined. Season with salt and black pepper. Keep warm.
Heat a separate frying pan with 20ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Carefully crack eggs into the hot oil. Fry eggs sunny side up until whites are set and edges are slightly crispy. Yolks should remain runny. Season with salt.
Arrange warm potato rounds on a large serving platter.
Spoon a generous amount of black bean mixture onto each potato round.
Carefully place a fried egg on top of each bean mound.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately as a sharing snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Poached Egg & Black Bean Bites
recipes.special_requests: Spanish cuisine, gluten free. use poached eggs.
recipes.visual_description: A collection of small, inviting Spanish-inspired bites arranged casually on a rustic wooden dining table. Each serving is presented in a modest, imperfect ceramic tapas bowl. The base is a thick, creamy mixture of coarsely mashed black beans, infused with sautéed garlic and onion, and blended with soft cream cheese. Its dark, rich hue contrasts with the vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley. Perched atop each bean mound are two golden-yellow quartered poached egg halves, their soft, delicate texture evident. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely, with natural light highlighting the inviting textures. Alongside, a small basket of crisp, golden gluten-free corn tortilla chips is casually placed, ready for scooping. The scene evokes a relaxed family gathering, with simple, comforting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as tapas, small individual portions for sharing
Accompanied by crusty bread or corn tortilla chips for scooping

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Gluten-free corn tortilla chips or toasted gluten-free bread

instructions: Heat olive oil in a medium pan over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed black beans to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Coarsely mash the black beans with a fork or potato masher.
Stir in softened cream cheese and gluten-free tamari until well combined.
Season the black bean mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Fill a large pot with water and bring to a gentle simmer. Add white vinegar.
Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl or ramekin.
Gently slide each egg into the simmering water. Poach eggs for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Remove poached eggs with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water.
Divide the black bean mixture onto four small serving plates or bowls.
Cut each poached egg into quarters. Arrange two quartered egg pieces on top of each black bean mound.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with gluten-free corn tortilla chips or toasted gluten-free bread for dipping.
notes: For best results, use fresh eggs for poaching.
Adjust the amount of cumin and tamari to your preference.
Ensure black beans are well-rinsed to remove excess sodium.

recipes.recipe_name: Huevos Endiablados con Frijoles Negros Especiados
recipes.visual_description: A simple, slightly off-white ceramic platter or rustic wooden board displays six halved deviled eggs. Each egg half is generously filled with a creamy, textured mixture of mashed egg yolks, dark black beans, and cream cheese, subtly spiced with cumin. The filling has a natural, slightly uneven surface, indicating a homemade touch. A light dusting of smoked paprika and a few chopped parsley leaves adorn the top, adding warm color and freshness. The firm, bright egg whites contrast with the darker, richer filling. The arrangement is casual, with eggs nestled together, leaving appropriate negative space. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, warm kitchen light. A casually placed linen napkin rests nearby. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, showcasing natural textures and colors of comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a tapas spread.
Offer alongside crusty gluten-free bread or corn tortilla chips.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes for firm yolks.
Drain eggs. Transfer to an ice bath. Cool completely.
Peel eggs. Cut each egg lengthwise in half.
Gently scoop out yolks. Place yolks in a small bowl.
Place egg whites on a serving platter.
Mash yolks with a fork.
Add black beans to yolks. Mash beans into yolk mixture. Leave some texture.
Add softened cream cheese, soy sauce, and ground cumin to the yolk mixture.
Mix well until combined. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon or pipe the yolk mixture back into the egg white halves.
Garnish with a pinch of smoked paprika and fresh herbs, if desired.
Serve immediately or chill until ready to serve.
notes: Ensure black beans are well-drained to prevent a watery filling.
Adjust cumin and soy sauce to personal preference.
For a smoother filling, blend a portion of the black beans before mixing.

recipes.recipe_name: Pastel de Papas (Chilean Shepherd's Pie)
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Pastel de Papas, presented in a rustic yet refined white ceramic oven-safe dish or deep bowl. The top layer of mashed potato is golden-brown and slightly crusted from baking and broiling, showing subtle peaks and valleys. Below, the rich, savory beef 'pino' filling is visible, revealing dark brown ground beef studded with darker olives and a hint of lighter raisins. The mashed potato is creamy light yellow, contrasted by the deep reddish-brown of the beef layer. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley or cilantro adds a vibrant green contrast. The dish rests on a simple, natural wood table surface with a crisp white cotton napkin and polished traditional flatware. A subtle, blurred modern bistro background suggests a casual, inviting atmosphere. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple Chilean salad (ensalada chilena) of sliced tomatoes and onions.
Accompany with a glass of Chilean red wine, such as Carmenere or Merlot.
Offer a small side of pebre (Chilean salsa) for those who prefer more heat.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash hot potatoes with butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onions. Cook until translucent, 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add ground beef to the pan. Break it apart. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in pitted black olives and raisins (if using). Remove from heat.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a large oven-safe dish or individual ramekins.
Spread half the beef filling evenly on the bottom. Arrange sliced hard-boiled eggs over the beef. Add remaining beef filling.
Spread mashed potatoes evenly over the beef layer. Smooth the top.
Sprinkle grated cheese over the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and the cheese is golden brown.
Briefly broil for 2-3 minutes for a deeper golden crust, watching carefully.
Let rest 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro.
notes: The hard-boiled eggs and olives are traditional elements of the 'pino' filling.
Pastel de Papas can be prepared ahead of time and baked just before serving.
traditional_techniques: Pino preparation (the savory base for many Chilean dishes)

recipes.recipe_name: Heirloom Tomato Salad with Thyme-Infused Beef Glaze and Pickled Shallots
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine bone china plate with ample negative space, resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish. A neatly folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate. The Heirloom Tomato Salad features an artistic, flowing composition of vibrant diced and thinly sliced heirloom tomatoes in shades of red, orange, and yellow. Interspersed among the tomatoes are a few translucent pink, thinly sliced pickled shallots. Two to three small, perfectly seared Wagyu beef cubes, displaying a rich brown crust and a tender pink interior, are precisely placed within the tomato arrangement. A glossy, dark brown thyme-infused beef glaze is artfully drizzled over the components, providing a rich counterpoint. A few drops of golden extra virgin olive oil glisten on the surface. The dish is subtly garnished with delicate green micro basil leaves, adding a precise pop of color and freshness. All elements are meticulously arranged, showcasing sophisticated minimalism and culinary precision, with no overcrowding.
instructions: Thinly slice shallots. Combine sherry vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Pour hot liquid over sliced shallots. Set aside to cool and pickle.

Pour beef stock into a separate saucepan. Add 4 thyme sprigs and smashed garlic clove. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently, reducing stock by half to two-thirds until it forms a rich, syrupy glaze. Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Season glaze with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cut heirloom tomatoes. Dice some tomatoes into 1cm cubes. Thinly slice others into rounds or irregular shapes for visual contrast.

Pat Wagyu beef tenderloin dry. Season all sides with salt and pepper. Heat a small, heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Add a tiny amount of olive oil. Sear beef for 1-2 minutes per side for medium-rare, forming a deep crust. Remove from pan and rest for 5 minutes. Slice beef into 2-3 very small, precise cubes or medallions per serving.

To plate, arrange a mix of diced and thinly sliced heirloom tomatoes artistically on each plate, creating an organic, flowing composition. Place 2-3 small seared Wagyu beef pieces among the tomatoes. Scatter a few pickled shallot slices over the tomatoes. Drizzle the warm thyme-infused beef glaze sparingly over the components. Finish with a few drops of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. Garnish each plate with a few micro basil leaves or small thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cuban Black Beans and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Cuban Black Beans and Rice rests in a simple, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The dish presents a rustic, comforting medley of reddish-brown rice grains intermingled with dark, glossy black beans. Small, soft pieces of diced onion and green bell pepper are visible throughout, alongside tender flakes of crispy diced bacon. The rice is cooked to a tender, slightly moist consistency, showing distinct grains. A few vibrant green chopped cilantro leaves are scattered casually over the top. A bright green lime wedge is placed on the bowl's rim. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-toned wooden dining table, with a casually folded, off-white cloth napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light from above illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for a bright finish
Garnish with fresh cilantro

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion and green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained black beans and rice to the pot. Stir well to combine and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and add the bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let the pot stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Fluff the rice and beans with a fork. Stir in the cooked bacon.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean & Rice Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Homely black bean and rice fritters are casually arranged on a rustic, matte ceramic plate. The fritters are small, roughly circular patties, about 6 cm in diameter, with a beautiful golden-brown, slightly irregular crust from pan-frying. Their texture appears crisp on the exterior, contrasting with the soft, slightly lumpy interior of mashed black beans and rice grains. Scattered throughout are flecks of finely diced onion and vibrant green cilantro. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro leaves rests on top of some fritters, adding a pop of natural green color. The plate is positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. The overall presentation is unpretentious, focusing on comfort and approachability.
instructions: Drain and rinse black beans. Mash them in a bowl with a fork until mostly broken, leaving some whole.
Add cooked rice, egg, flour, finely diced onion, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix well until combined.
Heat 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Scoop about 30g of the mixture per fritter. Form into small, flattened patties, about 5-6 cm in diameter.
Carefully place fritters into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Garlic Bruschetta with Crispy Chicken Skin
recipes.visual_description: Rustic Italian bruschetta presented on a natural light bamboo serving board. Slices of golden-brown toasted sourdough bread are generously topped with a vibrant, chunky red fermented tomato and garlic mixture. The fermented tomatoes are diced, showcasing their natural texture, while small, pale pickled mushroom slices are artfully scattered amongst the tomatoes. Irregular, golden-amber shards of rendered crispy chicken skin add a savory crunch, contrasting with the soft, juicy tomato. Fresh green oregano leaves are sparingly placed for aromatic garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, highlighting the natural colors and textures. Earthy-toned, handcrafted ceramic bowls hold any extra fermented tomato mixture or pickled mushrooms on the side, emphasizing an ingredient-focused, sustainable approach. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a clean, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an antipasto or light snack, ideal for sharing.
Offer additional small bowls of pickled mushrooms or fermented tomatoes on the side for guests to add more.

ingredients.name: Chicken skin
ingredients.quantity: from 2-3 chicken thighs/breasts (reserve meat for other uses)

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 4 cloves, peeled, thinly sliced; 2 cloves, minced

instructions: Dice tomatoes. Thinly slice 4 garlic cloves. Combine diced tomatoes, sliced garlic, 5g sea salt, and half the oregano leaves in a clean glass jar. Press down to submerge ingredients. Loosely cover the jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Gently burp the jar daily to release gas. Taste for desired tanginess.

In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, and sugar. Bring the mixture to a boil. Add sliced mushrooms. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let mushrooms cool completely in the pickling liquid.

Remove chicken skin from chicken pieces. Scrape off any excess fat from the underside of the skin. Cut the chicken skin into irregular 2-3 cm pieces. Place skin pieces in a cold pan. Cook over medium-low heat. Slowly render the fat until the skin pieces are deeply golden and very crispy. This takes approximately 10-15 minutes. Drain crispy skin pieces on a paper towel. Season immediately with a pinch of salt. Reserve rendered chicken fat for other cooking.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly brush both sides of the sourdough bread slices with olive oil. Toast bread in the oven until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes.

Drain the fermented tomato mixture. Roughly chop any larger pieces of fermented tomato. In a small bowl, combine the drained fermented tomato mixture with the remaining fresh oregano leaves and the 2 minced garlic cloves. Stir in 50ml of extra virgin olive oil. Season with freshly ground black pepper to taste.

Spoon a generous amount of the fermented tomato mixture onto each toasted sourdough bread slice. Arrange several pickled mushroom slices on top of the tomato mixture. Crumble the golden-amber shards of crispy chicken skin over each bruschetta. Serve immediately on a communal platter.
notes: Ensure the fermentation jar is clean and loosely covered to allow gases to escape.
The crispiness of the chicken skin is crucial; cook slowly to render fat fully and achieve maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, golden-brown Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is presented on a round white porcelain plate. The risotto is fluid and spreads naturally, not mounded, with visible tender chicken cubes and sliced sautéed mushrooms integrated throughout. Resting centrally on top is a perfectly poached egg, its vibrant yellow yolk visible and ready to break. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese adorn the top. The chicken is cut into clean 2 cm cubes, showcasing its golden-brown sear. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a warm wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside the dish. Natural, even light highlights the rich textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional, yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot, as risotto loses its creamy texture quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a crisp, dry Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Slice the mushrooms. Mince the garlic.

In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges. This is toasting the rice.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed. This deglazes the pan.

Begin adding hot chicken broth, one ladleful (approx. 125 ml) at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and fluid, al dente.

Stir in the cooked chicken cubes and half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should be fluid and not dry. This is mantecatura.

While risotto finishes, poach eggs. Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add white vinegar. Carefully crack each egg into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Ladle risotto onto individual plates. Top each serving with a poached egg. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and remaining grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Supreme with Black Garlic Risotto and Consommé Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with generous negative space. A free-flowing, dark, creamy black garlic risotto forms an organic pool. Perched elegantly atop the risotto is a whole chicken supreme, its skin rendered perfectly crisp and golden-brown. The chicken is not sliced. A glossy, amber chicken consommé reduction is artfully drizzled around the base of the chicken and risotto, creating a subtle sheen. The dish is garnished with a few precisely cut bright green chive batons, offering a delicate contrast. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle, and classic silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and sophisticated minimalism.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Consommé: Combine cold chicken stock with diced carrot, celery, leek, and lightly whisked egg whites in a large pot. Slowly bring to a simmer, stirring gently until raft forms. Stop stirring. Simmer uncovered for 45-60 minutes without disturbing. Strain consommé carefully through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Reduce clarified consommé over medium heat until it coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken Supreme: Season chicken supreme pieces with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal each piece individually. Cook in a sous vide bath at 63°C for 90 minutes. Remove chicken from bags. Pat skin thoroughly dry. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook for 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Prepare Black Garlic Risotto: Peel black garlic cloves. Mash two heads into a smooth paste. Thinly slice cloves from the remaining head. Mince shallots finely. Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté minced shallots until translucent. Add Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine evaporates. Begin adding warm chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed before adding more. After 10 minutes, stir in black garlic paste. Continue adding stock and stirring for another 8-10 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy. Stir in grated Parmesan, unsalted butter, and sliced black garlic. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid.

Assemble Dish: Ladle a generous, organic pool of black garlic risotto onto the center of each plate. Carefully place one rested chicken supreme on top of the risotto, skin-side up. Drizzle a precise amount of the reduced chicken consommé around the base of the chicken and risotto. Garnish with finely cut chive batons over the chicken and risotto.
notes: Precision is key for this dish. Ensure accurate temperatures and timing for all components.
The consommé reduction should be highly concentrated to provide intense flavor without overwhelming the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Teriyaki Salmon with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Teriyaki Salmon is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim. A generous portion of pan-seared salmon, skin-side up and beautifully browned, rests slightly off-center. Its rich, dark teriyaki glaze glistens. Beside the salmon, a natural mound of fluffy white short-grain rice is neatly placed. A small cluster of bright green blanched green beans, cut into 5cm pieces, adds a contrasting color and texture. The plate is on a well-used, light wooden kitchen table. A set of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate. A small, patterned ceramic bowl, suitable for miso soup, is nearby. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious and comforting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice.
Offer a small side dish of pickled ginger or pickled daikon.
Accompany with a simple clear soup or miso soup.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Use a rice cooker or stovetop method.
Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic in a small saucepan. Whisk well.
Bring sauce to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
