Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon fillets. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Pour about half of the teriyaki sauce over the salmon. Spoon sauce over the fillets as they cook.
Cook for another 4-6 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily.
Serve salmon immediately with steamed rice and blanched green beans. Drizzle remaining teriyaki sauce over the salmon.
notes: Adjust sugar in the teriyaki sauce to your preference.
For crispier skin, ensure salmon is very dry before searing.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing salmon.
traditional_techniques: Ichiju-sansai (concept of one soup, three dishes, simplified for home cooking)

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Fermented Chickpeas with Carrot Top Pesto
recipes.visual_description: Crispy Fermented Chickpeas are arranged in a small, unglazed, natural ceramic bowl with a matte finish. The chickpeas are golden brown, slightly irregular in shape, showcasing their natural texture. A vibrant green Carrot Top Pesto, smooth and rich, is presented in a smaller, matching ceramic dish beside the chickpeas. The entire composition sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin is casually folded beneath. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the earthy tones of the bowls and the vivid green of the pesto against the warm, rustic chickpeas. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements like a blurred plant. The focus is entirely on the pure, unadorned ingredients and their natural beauty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a communal snack for sharing.
Offer small, individual portions in natural ceramic bowls.
instructions: Rinse chickpeas. Place in large jar.
Add 15g salt. Cover with 750ml filtered water.
Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days. Bubbles indicate fermentation.
Taste for tanginess. Drain fermented chickpeas. Rinse thoroughly.
Pat chickpeas very dry with a clean cloth. This is crucial for crispiness.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Toss dried chickpeas with 15ml olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and 2g black pepper.
Spread in single layer on baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes. Stir halfway.
Chickpeas are crispy when golden and firm. Cool completely. They will crisp further.
Wash carrot tops well. Discard thick stems.
Toast sunflower seeds lightly in dry pan.
Combine carrot tops, toasted seeds, garlic, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, 2g salt, and 2g black pepper in food processor.
Pulse until finely chopped. Slowly drizzle in 60ml olive oil while processing until smooth.
Adjust consistency with more oil if needed. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve crispy fermented chickpeas in small bowls. Serve carrot top pesto alongside for dipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Macadamia Nut Tart with Blueberry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of chocolate macadamia nut tart is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain plate, positioned slightly off-center. The tart features a golden-brown, crisp pastry shell with a clean cut, revealing a rich, dark brown chocolate cream cheese filling studded with visible chunks of roasted macadamia nuts. Beside the tart, a vibrant purple blueberry coulis is artfully pooled, its glossy surface reflecting light. A few delicate, irregularly shaped white meringue kisses are placed near the tart, adding a contrasting texture and height. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A silver dessert fork rests beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin is placed nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtle, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare the pastry dough: Combine flour, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Add egg yolk; mix until dough forms. Flatten into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Blind bake the tart shell: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out dough to fit a 20 cm tart pan. Press into pan, trim edges. Prick base with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Cool.

Prepare chocolate cream cheese filling: Melt chopped dark chocolate over a bain-marie or in a microwave. Whisk softened cream cheese and granulated sugar until smooth. Beat in egg and vanilla extract. Stir in melted chocolate and heavy cream until well combined. Fold in chopped macadamia nuts.
Bake the tart: Pour filling into the cooled tart shell. Bake at 160°C for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center has a slight wobble. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Make blueberry coulis: Combine blueberries, granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, mashing berries slightly, until thickened. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth coulis. Cool completely.

Prepare meringue kisses: Preheat oven to 100°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Whisk egg white until soft peaks form. Gradually add caster sugar, one tablespoon at a time, continuing to whisk until stiff, glossy peaks form. Pipe small meringue kisses onto the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 60-75 minutes, or until dry and crisp. Turn off oven and let them cool inside.

Assemble and serve: Cut the cooled tart into 4 equal wedges. Place one wedge on each serving plate. Spoon a pool or drizzle of blueberry coulis beside the tart. Garnish with a few meringue kisses and a sprinkle of fresh blueberries or a few additional chopped macadamia nuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Blueberry Delice with Macadamia Tuile and Cream Cheese Cloud
recipes.visual_description: A rectangular slice of dark chocolate delice anchors the composition, its surface a deep, glossy brown. On top rests a thin, vibrant disc of translucent blueberry gel, precisely cut. A delicate, golden macadamia tuile, organically shaped, leans elegantly against the delice. Beside these, a cloud of pristine white cream cheese foam sits, its airy texture contrasting the richness. Scattered around the plate are a few perfectly ripe, plump blueberries. The plate is white bone china, presenting abundant negative space. The setting features a premium grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows.

ingredients.name: gelatin leaves, bloomed in cold water

instructions: Melt chocolate, cream, and butter in a heatproof bowl over a bain-marie. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs and caster sugar until pale and fluffy.
Gradually fold the warm chocolate mixture into the egg mixture until combined.
Pour into a 20x10 cm rectangular mould. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until firm.
Combine blueberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Simmer gently until blueberries soften.
Blend mixture until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear gel.
Return purée to saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour onto a flat tray lined with parchment paper, creating a thin layer. Chill until set.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk melted butter, icing sugar, flour, and egg white until smooth.
Stir in finely chopped macadamia nuts.
Drop small spoonfuls onto prepared baking sheet. Spread thinly into desired organic shapes.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Bloom gelatin leaves in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess water.
Gently heat a small portion (approx. 20ml) of the double cream until warm. Dissolve bloomed gelatin in warm cream.
In a bowl, whisk softened cream cheese and icing sugar until smooth.
Gradually whisk in remaining cold double cream and the gelatin mixture.
Pour into a siphon bottle and charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Or, whip with an electric mixer until light and airy. Chill until serving.
Carefully cut the chilled chocolate delice into 4 equal rectangular portions (approx. 5x10 cm each).
Cut the set blueberry gel into discs or shapes to fit on top of the delice slices.
Place one chocolate delice portion onto the center-left of each plate.
Gently place a blueberry gel piece on top of the delice.
Lean one macadamia tuile against the delice.
Dispense a cloud of cream cheese foam to the right of the delice.
Arrange 3 fresh blueberries artistically around the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Broccoli Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken and Broccoli Rice Bake is served on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The dish presents a warm, inviting mix of golden-brown melted cheddar on top, revealing creamy white rice, tender green broccoli florets, and substantial chunks of cooked chicken beneath. Diced red bell pepper and onion pieces add flecks of vibrant color throughout the cohesive mixture. The texture is soft and comforting, with the occasional crispness from the baked cheese. The components are naturally intertwined, creating a hearty, cohesive look. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded cotton napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The background is a soft blur of a homely kitchen, with hints of a ceramic mug. Lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting natural kitchen light.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion and bell pepper into 1 cm pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add chicken cubes. Cook until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add butter to the same skillet. Melt butter.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in 150g shredded cheddar cheese until melted. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Add cooked chicken, diced onion, diced bell pepper, cooked rice, and broccoli florets to the sauce. Stir well to combine.
Transfer mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet.
Sprinkle remaining 50g shredded cheddar cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and cheese is melted and golden.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Matar Pulao
recipes.visual_description: The Chicken Matar Pulao is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, mounded gently in the center. Fluffy, aromatic basmati rice forms the base, interspersed with vibrant green peas and golden-brown seared chicken chunks (3-4 cm). Thinly sliced caramelized onions are visible throughout the dish. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish exhibits warm, earthy tones from the spices, contrasting with the vivid green. The texture is light and inviting. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small, traditional stainless steel Katori holding raita, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint).
Accompany with pickled onions or a fresh kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion salad).
Enjoy with a simple lemon wedge for added zest.
instructions: Wash basmati rice thoroughly. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.
Heat oil or ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add black mustard seeds, cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and green cardamom pods. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced onion. Sauté, stirring frequently, until golden brown and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (slit lengthwise). Sauté for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in ground coriander, cayenne pepper powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add green peas. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained basmati rice to the pot. Gently mix for 1 minute, ensuring not to break the rice grains.
Pour in 600ml hot water. Stir gently to combine. Bring to a rolling boil.

Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until all water is absorbed and rice is tender. (If using a pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle, then simmer for 5 minutes, turn off heat, and let pressure release naturally).
Remove from heat and let the pulao rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Gently fluff the rice with a fork to separate the grains.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves before serving.
notes: Soaking Basmati rice is crucial for achieving distinct, fluffy grains.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust green chilies and cayenne pepper to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Dum cooking (slow cooking rice with steam)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Almond Crumble with Cacao Dust
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Fermented Apple & Almond Crumble is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a soft, earthy tone. The base features glistening, pale yellow fermented apple cubes, some with natural red skin visible, arranged organically. A generous, loose scattering of golden-brown almond crumble, showcasing irregular textures, tops the apples. A delicate, subtle dusting of dark cocoa powder creates a soft contrast over the crumble. A few toasted almond flakes are placed with intention for visual interest and a hint of crunch. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing ample negative space within the bowl. The bowl rests on a light-colored, matte stone surface, accompanied by a small, unglazed ceramic spoon. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed. The background is clean and slightly out of focus, possibly revealing subtle green plant elements, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a lighter, modern dessert. Can be enjoyed with a small spoon.
Pair with a small, strong Greek coffee.
instructions: Wash apples. Core and cut apples into 1.5 cm cubes. Do not peel.
Prepare brine: Dissolve salt in water.
Place apple cubes, cinnamon stick, and cloves into a clean glass jar.
Pour brine over apples. Ensure apples are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Seal jar loosely or use an airlock lid.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Check daily for small bubbles.
Taste after 3 days. When desired tanginess is reached, refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Combine oats, ground almonds, date syrup, olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix until crumbly.
Spread crumble mixture evenly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Stir halfway through.
Cool crumble completely.
Divide fermented apples into 4 individual serving bowls.
Spoon almond crumble generously over apples.
Dust lightly with unsweetened cocoa powder.
Garnish with toasted almond flakes.
notes: Fermentation time varies based on room temperature and desired tanginess. Taste daily after day 3.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken with Traditional Greek Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Grilled Chicken with Traditional Greek Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, centered on a simple wooden table. Two substantial, golden-brown grilled chicken chunks, their surfaces showing char marks from grilling, are positioned prominently. Beside the chicken, a vibrant Greek salad is artfully arranged. It features plump red tomato wedges, thick green cucumber half-moons, thin white and pink radish rounds, thinly sliced purple red onion rings, and shiny black Kalamata olives. Fresh, roughly torn mixed salad greens form a base, with creamy white feta cheese generously crumbled over the top. A light drizzle of golden olive oil dressing glistens on the ingredients. A fresh sprig of green oregano and a bright yellow lemon wedge serve as garnishes. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate and hints of a subtle, casually elegant restaurant background, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Mixed salad greens (e.g., Romaine, Lollo Rosso)

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt, pepper, dried oregano, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 30 ml olive oil. Marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Prepare the dressing: Whisk together remaining 90 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, juice of half a lemon, 2 minced garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
Wash and prepare vegetables. Cut tomatoes into large wedges. Cut cucumber into thick half-moon slices. Thinly slice radishes into rounds. Thinly slice red onion into rings. Roughly tear salad greens.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Grill chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Combine tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, red onion, olives, and salad greens in a large bowl.
Crumble feta cheese over the salad ingredients. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Slice rested chicken into thick chunks. Arrange chicken and salad on serving plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Tomato, Black Garlic Fluid Gel, Raspberry
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate, generously proportioned, serves as the canvas for this minimalist composition. At the center, four to five perfectly peeled, glossy compressed cherry tomatoes, their vibrant red hues intensified by the compression, are artfully placed in a natural, slightly asymmetric cluster. Each tomato is plump and retains its spherical shape. Scattered among and beside the tomatoes are four to five fresh, plump raspberries, their deep red contrasting with the tomatoes' brighter tone, showcasing their natural, unblemished texture. A small, intentional smear or a few precise dots of a rich, obsidian-black black garlic fluid gel are strategically positioned, adding a striking color contrast and a subtle, viscous texture. Delicate droplets of vivid emerald-green basil oil are meticulously placed around the elements, offering an aromatic accent and a final touch of color. The plating is characterized by abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision and simplicity of each component. The scene is set on a premium grey veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and a single piece of modern designer flatware rest discreetly to the side.
instructions: Blanch cherry tomatoes quickly in boiling water. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Peel skins carefully.
Make a simple syrup: Heat 50g sugar and 100ml water until sugar dissolves. Let cool completely.
Place peeled tomatoes in a vacuum-seal bag with cooled simple syrup. Vacuum seal on high pressure. If no vacuum sealer, gently press tomatoes in a container with syrup for 1 hour.
Blend black garlic cloves with 50ml water until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Heat strained black garlic liquid gently. Whisk in agar-agar until dissolved. Bring to a simmer for 1 minute.
Pour liquid onto a shallow tray. Chill until set.
Once set, blend the gelled black garlic until perfectly smooth and fluid. Store in a squeeze bottle.
Blanch basil leaves briefly in boiling water. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze out excess water.
Blend blanched basil with 50ml neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a coffee filter or superbag for clear oil.
On each plate, artfully arrange 4-5 compressed tomatoes. Place 4-5 fresh raspberries around them.
Add small, precise dots or a delicate smear of black garlic fluid gel.
Drizzle a few drops of basil oil around the components. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore with Rigatoni is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table. The rigatoni pasta, cooked al dente, forms a neat base, coated lightly in the rich, rustic tomato sauce. A tender, whole seared chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown, is placed centrally atop the pasta. The vibrant red sauce, teeming with browned sliced mushrooms, diced softened onions, and strips of red bell pepper, generously covers the chicken and pasta. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout the sauce, adding pops of color. Fresh, torn basil leaves are sprinkled over the dish, providing a contrasting green accent. Grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese lightly dusts the top. The textures are varied: tender chicken, soft vegetables, and firm pasta. The scene is well-lit with natural, even light, and a simple cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. A traditional fork and spoon are placed to the side. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the food to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper strips to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze. Cook until wine is nearly evaporated.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and halved cherry tomatoes to the pan. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pan. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve. Plate rigatoni. Top with a chicken thigh and generous spoonfuls of the cacciatore sauce. Garnish with additional fresh basil and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The red wine can be omitted or substituted with extra chicken broth if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Plant-Based 'Chicken' with Savory Cherry Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two golden-brown, pan-seared plant-based chicken breasts are arranged centrally. A generous pool of glossy, deep ruby-red savory cherry sauce cascades over the chicken, pooling slightly at the base. Beside the chicken, a creamy, pale yellow mound of polenta provides a soft textural contrast. Five vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to crisp-tender perfection, are neatly placed alongside. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the chicken, adding a touch of vibrant green. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware rest beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Pat plant-based chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add plant-based chicken. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until heated through. Target internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for thorough cooking. Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallots to the same skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until liquid slightly reduces.
Add vegetable broth and pitted cherries. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cherries soften and sauce slightly thickens. Cherries should burst.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in maple syrup, if using, to balance flavors. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return seared plant-based chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Serve immediately with creamy polenta or wild rice and blanched asparagus or broccolini. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: For plant-based chicken, choose a high-quality product that sears well and holds its shape.
This dish pairs well with a side of creamy polenta, wild rice pilaf, or roasted root vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Longganisa Adobo Noodles with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, savory Pork and Longganisa Adobo Noodle dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The rich brown egg noodles are generously coated in a glossy, dark adobo sauce, intertwined with tender, braised pork cubes and savory, caramelized longganisa slices. Scattered atop are golden-brown, crispy fried potato cubes, contrasting in texture and color. Freshly diced bright red tomato pieces and vibrant green sliced spring onion garnish the dish, adding a pop of color. Adjacent to the bowl, a small side bowl holds fluffy, white jasmine rice. A ramekin of creamy garlic mayonnaise sits nearby, ready for dipping the potatoes. A crisp, toasted slice of crusty bread leans against the rice bowl. The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's inviting textures and warm tones. Traditional flatware is neatly placed beside the bowl, complementing the approachable restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with calamansi (Filipino lime) wedges for an extra zest.
Offer patis (fish sauce) on the side for those who prefer more savory depth.
Best enjoyed family-style, though plated here for individual portions.

ingredients.name: Dried rice noodles or egg noodles

instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Heat 80ml oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add potato cubes. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt. Set aside.

In the same pan, drain excess oil, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Add pork cubes. Sear until browned on all sides. Add sliced longganisa. Cook until lightly browned. Remove pork and longganisa from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant. Add diced tomato. Cook until softened.

Return pork and longganisa to the pan. Add soy sauce, cane vinegar, brown sugar, crushed black peppercorns, bay leaves, and 250ml water. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 30-40 minutes, or until pork is tender. Remove bay leaves.
While pork simmers, prepare noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Add cooked noodles to the adobo mixture in the pan. Toss gently to coat noodles evenly with sauce.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with 1 minced garlic clove. Mix well.

Divide adobo noodles among 4 plates. Top with crispy potatoes. Garnish with sliced spring onion. Serve with warm jasmine rice, garlic mayonnaise, and toasted bread on the side. Optionally, sprinkle grated cheese over the crispy potatoes.
notes: Adjust sweetness, sourness, and saltiness of the adobo sauce to personal preference.
For a spicier kick, add a few bird's eye chilies (siling labuyo) during the adobo simmering process.
Using Filipino brands of soy sauce and vinegar enhances the authentic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Pork and Sausage Ragout with Cheesy Potato-Apple Mash and Garlic Bread
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and inviting main course presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of rich, dark red pork and sausage ragout, studded with vibrant green peas, is spooned over a bed of golden-hued, wide pappardelle noodles. The ragout exhibits a thick, clinging texture with visible diced pork and crumbled sausage, hinting at its slow-simmered depth. Beside the pasta, a neatly mounded scoop of creamy, pale yellow potato-apple mash sits, its surface gently textured. A golden-brown, crispy slice of garlic bread, lightly browned with visible minced garlic and melted cheese, leans elegantly against the mash. The dish showcases a balanced composition with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and warm, inviting colors. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, creating a casual yet refined bistro ambiance.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (Russet or Yukon Gold), peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Apple (firm, sweet-tart), peeled, cored, and cut into 2 cm chunks
Fresh parsley or basil for garnish

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground pork and sausage. Break up meat with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, coffee, sugar, bay leaves, and oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally. The ragout should be thick and rich.
While ragout simmers, place potato and apple chunks in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes and apples thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Mash with a potato masher until smooth. Stir in mayonnaise, 50g grated Parmesan cheese, butter, salt, and white pepper. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette lengthwise. In a small bowl, combine 60 ml olive oil, 3 cloves minced garlic, and dried parsley (if using). Brush mixture generously over cut sides of bread. Sprinkle with 30g grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake garlic bread for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crispy.
After ragout has simmered, remove bay leaves. Stir in frozen green peas. Cook for 5 minutes until peas are tender and heated through. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pappardelle or tagliatelle noodles. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.

Divide cooked noodles among four plates. Spoon a generous portion of ragout over the noodles. Place a scoop of potato-apple mash beside the ragout. Lean a slice of garlic bread against the mash or plate edge. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti with Sun-Dried Tomato, Anchovy, and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of golden spaghetti is casually mounded on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pasta strands are coated in a rich, rustic sauce, visibly flecked with deep reddish-brown pieces of roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes, subtle hints of softened diced onion, and small slivers of thinly sliced garlic. The sauce has a glossy, emulsified texture, clinging naturally to the pasta. A light scattering of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese sits on top, along with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple fork and a casually placed cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish in a natural, unpretentious manner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil
ingredients.quantity: 100g, drained and roughly chopped (reserve 2 tbsp oil)

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain the spaghetti.
While pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp of reserved sun-dried tomato oil (or olive oil) in a large pan over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced garlic, minced anchovy fillets, and optional red pepper flakes to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until anchovies dissolve.
Stir in the roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the butter to the pan. Let it melt and coat the mixture.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan with the sauce. Toss well to combine.
Pour in 125ml of the reserved pasta water. Add most of the grated Parmesan. Toss continuously until a creamy sauce forms, adding more pasta water if needed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining grated Parmesan.
notes: Adjust the amount of anchovy to your preference; they melt into the sauce and provide a deep umami flavor, not an overtly 'fishy' taste.
Use good quality sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil for best flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, homely portion of penne pasta is casually piled in a rustic, round, off-white ceramic bowl, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange sauce, with visible pieces of finely diced onion, minced garlic, and thin slices of dark red sun-dried tomatoes interspersed throughout. A light dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the top. The sauce has a comforting, slightly glossy texture, clinging well to the penne. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a simple, comforting home-cooked meal. A plain metal fork is placed beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting.
instructions: Cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Before draining, reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, prepare the sauce. Drain sun-dried tomatoes and slice them thinly. Mince garlic. Finely dice the onion.
Heat butter and olive oil in a large deep pan or skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
Stir in sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano to the sauce. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce. Toss well to coat all pasta evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Continue tossing for 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh torn basil leaves and an extra sprinkle of grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti with Sun-Dried Tomato, Anchovy, and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of golden spaghetti is casually mounded on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pasta strands are coated in a rich, rustic sauce, visibly flecked with deep reddish-brown pieces of roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes, subtle hints of softened diced onion, and small slivers of thinly sliced garlic. The sauce has a glossy, emulsified texture, clinging naturally to the pasta. A light scattering of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese sits on top, along with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple fork and a casually placed cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish in a natural, unpretentious manner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.

Before draining, reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain the spaghetti.
While pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp of reserved sun-dried tomato oil (or olive oil) in a large pan over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced garlic, minced anchovy fillets, and optional red pepper flakes to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until anchovies dissolve.
Stir in the roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the butter to the pan. Let it melt and coat the mixture.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan with the sauce. Toss well to combine.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Beef and Mozzarella Casserole
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Baked Beef and Mozzarella Casserole is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The golden-brown crust of melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese covers a rich, deep red tomato sauce, revealing tender, browned ground beef and soft, diced onions beneath. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, adding a vibrant color contrast. The casserole is a generous, comforting mound, slightly asymmetrical on the plate. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A simple metal fork and knife rest beside the plate on a casually draped, textured cloth napkin. The background hints at a lived-in, cozy family kitchen, reinforcing the homely comfort food aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Accompany with a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat ovens to 190°C (375°F).
Heat olive oil in large, heavy-bottomed pots or skillets over medium-high heat. Brown ground beef in batches. Break up beef with a spoon as it cooks. Drain excess fat.
Remove beef. Add diced onions to the same pots. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic to onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return browned beef to pots. Add crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow flavors to meld.
Divide beef mixture evenly among several large baking dishes. Spread evenly.
Top each dish generously with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden-brown. For a darker crust, broil for the last few minutes, watching carefully.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish each serving with fresh chopped basil.
notes: This casserole is excellent for meal preparation and reheats well.
Adjust salt and pepper to personal preference after simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Zero-Waste Bell Pepper Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown with a crisp skin, rests centrally on a cream-toned handcrafted ceramic plate. Its natural contours are preserved, presented as a whole piece. Alongside, a neat, small mound of fluffy white fermented rice provides a soft contrast. A vibrant, finely minced salsa, made from the red bell pepper and red onion trim, is artfully spooned next to the chicken, showcasing a medley of crimson and pale purple hues. The salsa's rough, natural texture offers a delightful visual counterpoint to the smooth chicken and rice. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space to emphasize the purity of each ingredient. The setting features a light bamboo surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A subtle green plant in the background adds a touch of organic life, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Place rice in a bowl, cover with 400ml water and a pinch of salt. Let soak at room temperature for 12-24 hours. Drain and rinse well before cooking.

Dice one and a half bell peppers and half of the red onion into 1cm pieces. Set aside for cooking with chicken. Reserve all bell pepper tops, bottoms, cores, and onion outer layers/root ends for the salsa.
Finely mince all reserved bell pepper and onion trim for the salsa. Combine in a small bowl with apple cider vinegar, 15ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Stir well and let sit.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and let rest.
In the same pan, add diced bell peppers and onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

Cook the fermented rice: Combine drained rice with 400ml fresh water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Plate individual portions. Place a scoop of fermented rice on one side of the plate. Arrange sautéed bell peppers and onion next to the rice. Place one pan-seared chicken thigh on the plate. Spoon a generous amount of the zero-waste bell pepper salsa alongside the chicken. Garnish with a few fresh parsley leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb with Fermented Greens & Skordalia
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Braised Lamb with Fermented Greens and Skordalia is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone. A large, rustic chunk of fork-tender braised lamb, its surface a rich, deep brown, is placed slightly off-center. Alongside, a generous, creamy dollop of off-white skordalia shows a subtle, textured consistency. A vibrant pile of deep green fermented greens, lightly wilted, rests next to the lamb, offering a bright contrast. A few fresh oregano leaves are simply scattered over the lamb and greens. The composition is natural and unforced, with ample negative space. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural overhead lighting. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural plant elements in soft focus, emphasizing sustainable aesthetics.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping into the lamb juices and skordalia.
Accompanied by a simple village salad (Horiatiki salata) without lettuce.

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., kale, chard), tough stems removed, chopped

instructions: Prepare Fermented Greens (5-7 days in advance): Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 litre filtered water to make brine. Pack chopped seasonal greens, sliced garlic, and optional dill sprigs into a clean jar. Pour brine over greens, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar with an airlock lid or loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Cut lamb shoulder into 4-5 large, rustic chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear lamb chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove lamb from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce the wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, lamb stock (use water if no stock), dried oregano, and bay leaves. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return seared lamb chunks to the pot. Ensure lamb is mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot with a lid.
Braise in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls apart. Remove bay leaves before serving. Check seasoning.
Prepare Skordalia: Soak stale bread in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess water very thoroughly.
In a food processor, combine the squeezed bread, peeled garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt. Process until smooth.

Slowly drizzle in red wine vinegar and then extra virgin olive oil while processing, until a creamy, thick dip forms. Adjust consistency with a tablespoon of water if too thick. Taste and adjust salt.

To serve, drain the fermented greens. Lightly sauté them in the remaining 30ml olive oil for 2-3 minutes if desired, or serve as is. Serve braised lamb chunks with a generous dollop of skordalia and a side of the fermented greens.
notes: Using bone-in lamb shoulder for braising enriches the sauce significantly. The bones can also be used to make lamb stock for a zero-waste approach.
The fermented greens can be prepared up to a week in advance, enhancing their flavor and tanginess.
traditional_techniques: Braising (common for lamb dishes in Greek cuisine)
Use of Greek oregano and olive oil as primary flavorings

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Italian Beef and Pasta Soup
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Italian Beef and Pasta Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. The rich, amber-brown broth fills the bowl, studded with tender, irregular chunks of slow-cooked beef. Small, al dente pasta shapes are suspended throughout the liquid, alongside soft, diced carrots, celery, and onions, adding natural earthy tones. A generous scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color and freshness against the warm hues of the soup. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese melts gently on the surface, creating small, inviting pools. The presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a comforting, homemade meal. A simple spoon rests beside the bowl on the wooden table. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the cozy atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Parmesan Cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80g, freshly grated, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh Parsley
ingredients.quantity: a small bunch, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef cubes. Brown beef on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, and dried basil. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add beef broth, diced tomatoes, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Remove bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the surface if desired.
Add pasta to the soup. Cook according to package directions, usually 8-12 minutes, until al dente.
Stir in 80g grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For a richer flavor, brown the beef well before adding vegetables.
Adjust pasta quantity to your preference for a thicker or thinner soup.
Leftovers taste even better the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Chicken & Cheese Quesadillas
recipes.visual_description: A homely serving of golden-brown mini chicken and cheese quesadilla wedges is presented on a simple, rustic off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used light wooden dining table. The quesadillas are cut into neat triangles, revealing melted yellow cheese and a savory filling of diced chicken, green bell pepper, and onion. The chicken is cooked through. The cheese slightly oozes from the sides. The wedges are casually stacked, appearing natural and inviting. A small, unadorned ceramic bowl of vibrant red salsa and another of creamy white sour cream are placed nearby. A casually folded linen napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere, perfect for a quick, satisfying lunch. The focus is entirely on the inviting food, with minimal, authentic background elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream for dipping.
Often served informally as a quick lunch or appetizer.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 1 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 10 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 5 ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the pan with vegetables. Stir in ground cumin and chili powder. Mix well.
Lay one tortilla flat. Sprinkle half of the shredded cheese over one half of the tortilla.
Spoon half of the chicken and vegetable mixture over the cheese.
Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling to create a half-moon shape.
Repeat for remaining tortillas and filling.
Heat a clean non-stick pan over medium heat. Place one quesadilla in the hot pan.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cheese is melted. Repeat for all quesadillas.
Remove quesadillas from pan. Cut each into 2 or 3 wedges.
Serve immediately with salsa and sour cream on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken & Halloumi Skewers with Lemon-Herb Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken & Halloumi Skewers is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. Three skewers, loaded with vibrant ingredients, are arranged parallel on the plate. Succulent, seared chicken breast chunks, golden-brown halloumi cubes, charred red and green bell pepper pieces, softened red onion chunks, and bursting whole cherry tomatoes are threaded together. A light drizzle of bright green lemon-herb dressing glistens over the skewers. Fresh parsley sprigs and a quartered lemon wedge garnish the side of the plate. The composition has balanced negative space. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the fresh colors and varied textures of the grilled ingredients. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, completing the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread.
Accompany with a side of creamy Tzatziki sauce.
Pair with a simple Greek salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes.
Cut halloumi into 2.5 cm cubes.
Chop red and green bell peppers into 3 cm pieces.
Cut red onion into 3 cm pieces.
Mince garlic. Finely chop fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, 30 ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, 3 g dried oregano, 15 ml lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Thread chicken cubes, halloumi cubes, bell pepper pieces, red onion pieces, and cherry tomatoes onto skewers. Alternate ingredients for visual appeal.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Brush skewers with remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Grill skewers for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is cooked through. Halloumi should be golden and slightly charred.
While skewers cook, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, combine remaining minced garlic, 45 ml lemon juice, 2 g dried oregano, and chopped fresh parsley. Whisk well.
Remove skewers from heat. Drizzle with lemon-herb dressing. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Provençal with Olives and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a rich golden-brown, slightly crispy skin, contrasting with its tender interior. A generous portion of vibrant, rustic Provençal sauce surrounds the chicken, featuring discernible diced red and yellow bell peppers, softened yellow onion, and dark, plump Kalamata olives. The sauce has a deep red hue from the tomatoes, with hints of green from fresh thyme sprigs. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The plating is organized yet organic, allowing moderate negative space around the components. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Pair with a light green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Accompany with simple boiled potatoes or rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced yellow onion, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, chicken broth, Herbes de Provence, and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from oven. Stir in pitted Kalamata olives.
Let chicken rest in the sauce for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs are centered, featuring deeply seared, golden-brown skin glazed with a vibrant red tomato ragu. The sauce is thick and rustic, containing visible chunks of softened yellow onion, earthy-brown halved cremini mushrooms, and blistered red cherry tomatoes. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered loosely over the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a small plate of crusty ciabatta bread. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the glossy texture of the sauce and the organic arrangement of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta or focaccia to mop up the sauce.
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
Present in a wide shallow bowl to highlight the rustic braise.
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion and halved mushrooms to the skillet.
Sauté for 5 minutes until onions are translucent and mushrooms are browned.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in fresh torn basil and serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality canned San Marzano tomatoes for the most authentic flavor profile.
Do not remove the chicken skin, as it provides essential fat and flavor to the braising liquid.
If the sauce is too thick, add a splash more chicken stock at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cabbage Larb Salad
recipes.special_requests: No carrot or almonds, rich in flavour, no gluten
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spicy Cabbage Larb Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. A generous bed of finely shredded green cabbage forms the base, providing a crisp, light green foundation. Over this, a mound of savory, aromatic minced beef, cooked until lightly browned, is artfully mounded. The beef is interspersed with vibrant green specks of chopped mint, cilantro, and spring onions, along with thin crimson slices of bird's eye chilies and delicate, translucent rings of shallots. Thinly sliced cucumber rounds and bright red cherry tomato halves are strategically arranged around the beef, adding freshness and contrasting color. A glistening, clear lime-fish sauce dressing lightly coats the ingredients, reflecting the natural, even lighting. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin and a small, traditional ceramic bowl of sticky rice, embodying a modern bistro setting with authentic Thai cultural elements. The scene is uncluttered, focusing entirely on the dish's fresh, appealing presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm sticky rice (Khao Niao) on the side to complement the spicy and savory flavors.
Offer additional fresh herbs like basil or saw-leaf coriander for personal preference.
Traditionally eaten with hands, scooping the salad and sticky rice together.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat.
Add minced beef. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Transfer cooked beef to a large mixing bowl. Allow to cool slightly.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, sliced shallots, sliced chilies, and toasted rice powder to the beef. Mix well.
Add chopped mint, cilantro, and spring onions to the beef mixture. Toss gently to combine.
In a separate large serving bowl, arrange the shredded green cabbage as a base.
Top the cabbage with the thinly sliced cucumber and halved cherry tomatoes.
Spoon the beef mixture evenly over the vegetables.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of chilies to suit your preferred spice level.
Toasted rice powder (Khao Khua) is crucial for authentic Larb flavor and texture. It adds a nutty aroma and slight crunch.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: spicy, sour, salty, and sweet (though sweet is minimal here, it's balanced by the others).

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Beer-Braised Chicken with Saffron Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Beer-Braised Chicken and Saffron Tomato Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently atop a generous bed of vibrant, saffron-infused rice. The chicken is tender, pulled from the bone, showcasing its rich, braised texture. A glistening, reddish-brown sauce, thickened from the braising liquid, is spooned over the chicken and rice, revealing hints of diced tomatoes and onions. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled lightly over the dish for color and freshness. The plate maintains moderate negative space, enhancing the professional yet approachable restaurant style. A simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin complete the modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., stout or dark ale)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, garlic, and red bell pepper to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften and onion is translucent.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and bay leaf. Stir well.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, prepare saffron rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
In a medium saucepan, combine rice with 600 ml water and a pinch of saffron threads. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Remove bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce if desired.
Serve chicken thighs over saffron rice. Spoon plenty of the rich braising sauce over the chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For richer flavor, use a dark, malty beer like a stout or porter.
The sauce can be made thicker by simmering on the stovetop for a few minutes after removing the chicken, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Lettuce Beef Larb Salad
recipes.special_requests: No carrot or almonds, rich in flavour, low gluten
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh Lettuce Beef Larb Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro. The cooked minced beef, rich brown with hints of red chili, is centrally mounded. It is generously mixed with bright green chopped mint, cilantro, and sliced green onions, with translucent slices of shallot visible throughout. Around the base of the beef mound, crisp, broad lettuce leaves are artfully arranged, some slightly overlapping. Thin, translucent slices of cool cucumber and delicate rings of red onion are nestled among the lettuce, adding contrasting textures and colors. A light sprinkle of fine, pale toasted rice powder and a few extra red chili flakes garnish the top of the beef. The overall composition is clean and professional, with thoughtful negative space. Standard flatware (fork and spoon) rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a fresh, inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm sticky rice or jasmine rice on the side.
Provide extra fresh vegetables like long beans, cabbage wedges, or more lettuce for diners to scoop and wrap the larb.
Offer a small bowl of extra chili flakes or a lime wedge for personalized seasoning.
instructions: Toast glutinous rice in a dry pan over medium heat. Stir constantly until golden brown and fragrant. Remove from heat. Grind in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder until a fine powder forms. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add minced beef. Cook, breaking up lumps, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
In a bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chili flakes. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add cooked beef, thinly sliced shallots, roughly chopped mint, roughly chopped cilantro, and thinly sliced green onions to the dressing. Mix well.
Stir in the toasted rice powder. Mix thoroughly to combine.
Arrange crisp lettuce leaves, thinly sliced cucumber, and thinly sliced red onion on a serving platter or individual plates.
Spoon the beef larb mixture onto the platter or plates. Serve immediately.
notes: For a spicier dish, increase the amount of dried chili flakes.
Use fresh, good quality herbs for the best flavor.
traditional_techniques: Making Khao Khua (toasted glutinous rice powder)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cucumber and Herb Salad with Savory Beef
recipes.special_requests: No carrot or almonds, rich in flavour and ingredients
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh Thai-style salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a lively array of colors and textures. A generous bed of crisp mixed leafy greens forms the base, topped with thinly sliced cucumbers, vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, and delicate slivers of red onion. A modest portion of savory, browned minced beef, seasoned with garlic and chili, is scattered artfully amongst the vegetables, not dominating the plate. Abundant fresh green herbs—chopped mint, cilantro, and Thai basil—are generously mixed throughout and lightly garnished on top, providing aromatic contrast. The salad is lightly coated in a clear, tangy lime-fish sauce dressing, glistening subtly. The arrangement is organic and flowing, allowing each component to be clearly visible without overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Thai flatware, with natural, even lighting illuminating the fresh ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sticky rice or fresh lettuce leaves for wrapping.

ingredients.name: Palm sugar
ingredients.quantity: 1 tablespoon, dissolved in a little warm water if hard

instructions: Prepare the salad vegetables. In a large bowl, combine sliced cucumbers, mixed greens, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced red onion. Add chopped mint, cilantro, and Thai basil.

Cook the beef. Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic and half of the sliced chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add beef mince. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, approximately 5-7 minutes. Drain any excess fat.
Prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar until sugar is dissolved. Add remaining sliced chilies.
Assemble the salad. Add the cooked beef to the bowl with the prepared vegetables and herbs. Pour the dressing over the salad. Add roasted glutinous rice powder.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients thoroughly. Ensure even distribution of dressing and beef.
Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Using roasted glutinous rice powder (Khao Khua) for nutty aroma and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Papaya and Herb Salad with Seared Beef
recipes.special_requests: No carrot or almonds, rich in flavour and ingredients
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Green Papaya and Herb Salad presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The shredded green papaya forms the base, intermingled with halved bright red cherry tomatoes, crisp green long bean pieces, and thin slices of red onion and red bell pepper. Fresh torn mint, cilantro, and Thai basil leaves are visibly tossed throughout, adding pops of green. A light, clear peanut-lime dressing glistens on the ingredients, showing moisture. A very small, modest portion of thinly sliced, quickly seared beef, with a slightly browned edge, is artfully placed amongst the vegetables, not fanned. Crushed roasted peanuts are sprinkled over the top, adding texture. The arrangement is organic and flowing, showcasing the varied colors and textures. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and spoon, and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the freshness of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with sticky rice.
Can be accompanied by grilled chicken or fish on the side.
Often part of a larger meal with multiple dishes to share.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin or flank steak
ingredients.quantity: 150g, very thinly sliced against the grain

instructions: Prepare the dressing: In a bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, minced garlic, and sliced chilies. Whisk until palm sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Prepare the beef: Marinate thinly sliced beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, and black pepper for 10 minutes.
Sear the beef: Heat a skillet over high heat. Add beef slices in a single layer. Sear quickly for 30-60 seconds per side until just cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Prepare the vegetables: In a large mixing bowl, combine shredded green papaya, halved cherry tomatoes, and long bean pieces.
Assemble the salad: Pour dressing over the vegetables. Toss gently to coat. Add thinly sliced red onion, julienned red bell pepper, mint, cilantro, and Thai basil. Toss again.
Plate and garnish: Divide salad among four plates. Arrange seared beef slices sparingly on top of each salad. Sprinkle with crushed roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use a julienne peeler or a mandoline with a julienne blade for the papaya.
Adjust chili level to personal preference.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four main flavors: sour, sweet, salty, spicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Root Vegetables and Lemon-Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three thick, golden-brown chicken medallions, showing a crisp exterior and moist interior, are placed slightly off-center. Beside the chicken, a generous mound of roasted root vegetables – including earthy brown potato chunks, vibrant orange carrots, and creamy white parsnips – displays caramelized edges and tender textures. A glossy, light golden lemon-thyme pan sauce is spooned artfully over the chicken and vegetables, catching the light. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh thyme sprigs and a delicate, thin lemon wheel. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded grey cotton napkin placed to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its warm colors and inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 250 g, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Parsnips
ingredients.quantity: 250 g, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato, carrot, and parsnip chunks with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board, covered.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic and half of the fresh thyme sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in lemon juice and butter until butter is melted and sauce slightly thickened.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, slice each chicken breast into two or three thick medallions. Arrange roasted vegetables on plates. Place chicken medallions beside vegetables.
Spoon lemon-thyme sauce over chicken and vegetables. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs and a thin lemon slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Parmesan Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of creamy, pale yellow potato and Parmesan soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, set on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. The soup has a smooth, velvety texture, with steam gently rising. A casual sprinkle of freshly chopped vibrant green chives rests on the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl is accompanied by a simple, sturdy metal spoon and a casually folded, light-colored linen napkin to its side. Natural, soft, warm lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere typical of a homely family kitchen.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 150 g, grated, plus a rind (about 50 g)

instructions: Heat butter and olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Add the Parmesan rind.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are very tender.
Remove and discard the Parmesan rind from the soup.
Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer soup in batches to a blender and blend until smooth.
Stir in the grated Parmesan cheese and whole milk.
Heat soup gently for 5 minutes, do not boil. Stir until cheese is fully melted and incorporated.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Blue Cheese and Honey Toasts
recipes.visual_description: A collection of golden-brown toasted baguette slices are casually arranged on a rustic wooden serving board. Each toast is generously topped with soft, melted blue cheese, which has a creamy, slightly bubbling texture and distinct blue veining. A glossy drizzle of amber honey cascades over the cheese, pooling in some areas. Scattered over the honey and cheese are whole and roughly chopped walnut halves, adding a contrasting dark brown color and rugged texture. The arrangement is unpretentious and inviting, with some toasts slightly overlapping, suggesting a communal sharing style. The board is placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a small ceramic bowl with extra walnuts are visible in the soft, warm light of a homely kitchen setting. The focus is on the comforting, natural appearance of the snack, with all components clearly visible and appealing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Brush both sides of bread slices with olive oil.
Place slices on a baking tray.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Remove from oven.
Crumble blue cheese generously over each toast.
Return to oven for 2-3 minutes until cheese softens.
Remove from oven.
Drizzle honey over each toast.
Sprinkle with walnut halves.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Red Wine Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallions rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The two thick, round beef medallions feature a deep, golden-brown crust from searing, contrasting with a tender, pinkish-red interior. A rich, glossy red wine reduction is generously spooned over and around the beef, pooling elegantly on the plate. Beside the beef, a neatly stacked rectangular portion of golden-brown Dauphinoise potatoes, creamy and tender, provides a textural contrast. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the beef. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple dark wooden table surface and classic silver flatware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of the same dry red wine used in the reduction.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil to rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced shallots to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce wine by half. Add beef broth and thyme sprigs. Simmer until sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Spoon red wine reduction over beef medallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Rustic Baked Vegetable Rice is presented on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The rice is fluffy and moist, not dry, with visible chunks of browned eggplant cubes and thickly sliced mushrooms. Golden corn kernels and flecks of fresh green parsley are scattered throughout, adding color and texture. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, asymmetrical mound on the plate. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the food. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen. A simple fork rests beside the plate. The lighting is warm and cozy, emanating from kitchen fixtures, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the comforting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice onions into 1 cm pieces. Cut eggplants into 2 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms thickly. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onions. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in eggplant cubes and sliced mushrooms. Cook 10 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with oil and vegetable juices. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in diced tomatoes and vegetable broth. Add drained corn. Stir in dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring mixture to a boil. Remove from heat.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake 30-35 minutes. Rice should be tender and liquid absorbed.
Remove from oven. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in fresh chopped parsley.
Serve directly from the pot or portion onto plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom and Eggplant Risotto
