recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Shiso-Wrapped Chicken Katsu is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown, crispy katsu, sliced into thick, substantial pieces, is arranged neatly on one side of the plate. The vibrant green of the shiso leaves is subtly visible within the chicken. Adjacent to the katsu, a generous mound of finely shredded green cabbage provides a fresh, contrasting element. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the cabbage, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A small, traditional Japanese rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are placed beside the plate, emphasizing cultural authenticity. A folded light cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain white rice.
Offer a side of miso soup.
Accompany with pickled ginger or tsukemono (Japanese pickles).
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound chicken with a meat mallet to an even thickness of about 1 cm.
Season both sides of each chicken breast with salt and pepper.
Lay 4 shiso leaves over one side of each pounded chicken breast.
Roll each chicken breast tightly, starting from one short end, encasing the shiso leaves inside. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken roll in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Roll in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere crumbs firmly.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 170°C. Use a thermometer to monitor temperature.
Carefully lower 1-2 chicken katsu into the hot oil. Fry for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.
Remove katsu from oil and place on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain excess oil. Rest for 5 minutes.
Remove toothpicks. Slice each katsu into 2-3 thick, diagonal pieces. Do not fan slices.
Serve immediately with shredded green cabbage, a lemon wedge, and tonkatsu sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Green Chicken Curry is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The creamy, pale green curry sauce holds tender, simmered chicken chunks and vibrant green beans, cut into 4-5cm pieces. Thin, purple-red half-moon slices of red onion are visible throughout the dish, adding a subtle color contrast. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, dark green Thai basil leaves and a few bright red chili slices, providing pops of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A separate small white bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice sits beside the main dish. A simple cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is lit with natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined restaurant atmosphere with a minimal background.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat.
Add green curry paste. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Stir and cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Pour in coconut milk. Add torn kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Add green beans and sliced red onion. Cook for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh Thai basil leaves.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Garlic-Herb Sauce, Brown Rice Pilaf, and Roasted Delicata Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single, round, clean white porcelain dinner plate holds a well-composed individual portion. A pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two thick diagonal slices, is positioned slightly off-center, showcasing its golden-brown crust and tender interior. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat, slightly mounded portion of earthy brown rice and cannellini bean pilaf sits, flecked with vibrant green parsley and thyme. Around the central elements, several bright orange and green roasted delicata squash rings are artfully arranged, revealing their caramelized edges. A glossy, light brown garlic-herb sauce is generously spooned over the chicken, with a small pool at the base. Freshly chopped parsley and thyme are sprinkled over the chicken and pilaf for a final pop of color. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests near the chicken. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, with balanced colors and textures. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves
ingredients.quantity: 6, 4 minced for sauce, 2 minced for pilaf

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Prepare squash. Wash delicata squash. Trim ends. Halve lengthwise. Scoop out seeds. Cut into 1 cm thick rings.
Roast squash. Toss squash rings with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.

Cook brown rice. Rinse brown rice. Combine rice with 400ml water and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender.

Prepare pilaf. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced shallot and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Add cooked brown rice and rinsed cannellini beans. Stir well. Add 50ml chicken broth. Cook 3-5 minutes, until liquid is absorbed. Stir in half of chopped parsley and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare chicken. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Sear chicken. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 10-15 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.

Make sauce. While chicken rests, add 30g butter to the same skillet (off heat, or low heat if needed). Add 4 minced garlic cloves. Cook 1 minute, stirring. Deglaze with 100ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, until slightly reduced. Stir in remaining fresh parsley and thyme. Squeeze in 15ml lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.

Plate and serve. Slice each chicken breast diagonally into 2-3 thick pieces. Place a mound of brown rice pilaf on each plate. Arrange sliced chicken next to pilaf. Arrange roasted delicata squash rings around the chicken and pilaf. Spoon garlic-herb sauce over chicken. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Beef Fat Rice Cakes with Lemongrass-Lime Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve uniform, rectangular crispy rice cakes are meticulously arranged on a sleek, rectangular white porcelain platter. Each cake, approximately 4x4 cm, boasts a deep golden-brown, exceptionally crisp exterior. They are generously coated in a glistening, amber-hued lemongrass-lime glaze, which clings invitingly to their surfaces. A vibrant sprig of fresh coriander leaf adorns each canapé, providing a pop of green against the warm tones. Thin, bright red slivers of bird's eye chili are sparingly placed for visual contrast and a hint of heat. The arrangement is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space between pieces. The platter rests on a simple light wooden table surface, complemented by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors of the dish in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Press cooked Jasmine rice firmly into a flat, compact layer on a parchment-lined tray. Aim for 1.5 cm thickness. Chill for 30 minutes to firm.
Cut the chilled rice into uniform 4x4 cm rectangles. This yields 8-12 pieces.
Heat rendered beef fat and vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Fry rice cakes in batches until golden-brown and crispy on all sides. This takes about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove and drain on paper towels.
For the glaze, sauté minced shallot and garlic in a clean small saucepan with a splash of oil until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add minced lemongrass, fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice. Bring to a simmer.
Cook, stirring constantly, until the palm sugar dissolves and the glaze thickens slightly. This takes about 3-5 minutes. The glaze should coat a spoon.
Toss the crispy rice cakes gently in the warm glaze until evenly coated.
Arrange glazed rice cakes on a serving platter. Garnish each with a fresh coriander leaf and a thin slice of bird's eye chili, if using. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Meatballs with Tomato Basil Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A comforting single portion of al dente spaghetti, generously coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce, is mounded on an off-white, round ceramic plate. Three to four substantial, seared turkey meatballs, with a visibly textured, browned exterior, are nestled among the pasta, some partially submerged in the sauce. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the dish. The plate rests on a well-worn, light-brown wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded cream-colored cloth napkin lies beside the plate. Standard silver flatware, a fork and spoon, are placed alongside. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, conveying a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a comfortable home setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Finely mince 2 garlic cloves. Dice the onion. Roughly chop most basil leaves; reserve a few for garnish.
In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, 25 g grated Parmesan, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 12-16 equally sized meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Carefully add meatballs to the pot. Sear meatballs on all sides until well browned. Remove meatballs and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince remaining garlic clove and add to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Gently add browned meatballs back into the sauce. Ensure meatballs are submerged.
Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until meatballs are cooked through and tender. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Stir in chopped basil during the last 5 minutes of simmering.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in a separate pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Toss drained pasta with the tomato basil sauce and meatballs. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not overmix the meatball mixture; this can make the meatballs tough.
For best flavor, use high-quality canned crushed tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Sausage and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features thick, browned chunks of sausage, along with tender diced potatoes, sliced carrots, and softened onion, all simmered in a rich, reddish-brown tomato broth. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. Alongside the bowl, a small, separate mound of fluffy, white steamed rice is served. A simple side salad of crisp, vibrant green leaves, lightly dressed, sits on a smaller, plain white ceramic plate. A fresh lemon wedge accompanies the salad. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a humble cloth napkin and everyday flatware, bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light, emphasizing a comforting, homemade meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
A simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Prepare vegetables. Dice onion, mince garlic, slice carrots, dice potatoes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Brown well on all sides. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced carrots. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in diced potatoes, canned diced tomatoes with their juice, stock, dried thyme (if using), and bay leaf (if using). Bring to a simmer.

Return browned sausage to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and sausage is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Season with salt and pepper.

While stew simmers, prepare the rice. Rinse rice. In a saucepan, combine rice with 400ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Stir in butter and milk into the cooked rice for creaminess.
Prepare salad. Toss salad greens with a simple dressing of lemon juice and olive oil.
Serve hot stew alongside creamy rice and fresh green salad.
notes: This stew is even better the next day as flavors meld. Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Spiced Pork and Lentil Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain plate holds an inviting arrangement of golden-brown Thai Spiced Pork and Lentil Fritters. Each fritter, about 4-5 cm in diameter, boasts a crispy, irregular edge and a slightly domed center, revealing the subtle texture of lentils and minced pork within. The fritters are artfully stacked and spread across the plate, allowing for moderate negative space. A small, pristine white ramekin sits beside the fritters, filled with vibrant, translucent orange sweet chili sauce, generously studded with finely diced bright green cucumber and coarse, crushed roasted peanuts. Fresh, verdant coriander sprigs are thoughtfully placed on top of and around the fritters, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, set on a simple wooden table surface under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the food, showcasing its appetizing colors and textures.

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander
ingredients.quantity: 2 tbsp, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Rinse lentils. Cook lentils in boiling water until tender but still firm, about 20-25 minutes. Drain well. Mash lightly.

In a large bowl, combine mashed lentils, minced pork, red curry paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, julienned kaffir lime leaves, thinly sliced long beans, egg, and cornstarch. Add chopped fresh coriander.
Mix thoroughly until well combined. The mixture should be sticky.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 170°C.
Form the mixture into small, flat patties, about 4-5 cm in diameter and 1 cm thick.
Carefully place fritters into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan. Fry in batches.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure pork reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the dipping sauce, combine sweet chili sauce with diced cucumber and crushed roasted peanuts.
Serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce and fresh coriander sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Bell Peppers with Spiced Beef and Bulgur
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Stuffed Bell Peppers is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. Two vibrant bell pepper halves, one red and one yellow, are nestled side by side. Each pepper is generously filled with a rich, savory mixture of seasoned ground beef and fluffy bulgur, showcasing a rustic texture. Golden-brown melted mozzarella cheese forms a crust over the filling. The roasted bell pepper skins display slight charring, indicating a tender bite. A small, neat dollop of creamy white plain yogurt is placed beside the peppers. A sprig of fresh green mint or parsley garnishes the dish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the elements. Natural, even lighting highlights the colors and textures. A folded cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Lightly brush with olive oil. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 15 minutes until slightly softened.
Meanwhile, prepare the filling. Rinse bulgur in cold water. Drain well.
Mince onion and garlic. Roughly chop fresh mint and parsley.
Heat remaining olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef to the pan. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic, tomato paste, dried oregano, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add diced tomatoes and rinsed bulgur to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir well. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until bulgur absorbs liquid and softens slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in chopped fresh mint and parsley.
Flip roasted bell pepper halves. Fill each half generously with the beef and bulgur mixture. Do not overfill.
Grate mozzarella cheese. Sprinkle evenly over the stuffed bell peppers.
Return stuffed peppers to the oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly, and the filling is heated through. Beef internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Serve hot with a dollop of plain yogurt on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Noodle Salad with Crispy Tofu
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Thai Noodle Salad with Crispy Tofu is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The translucent rice vermicelli noodles form a loose base, topped with golden-brown, crispy 2cm tofu cubes. Thinly sliced red onion, julienned cucumber, and julienned carrot are mixed throughout, adding vibrant pops of red, green, and orange. The salad is casually arranged, allowing components to naturally touch and overlap. It is garnished with fresh green cilantro leaves and roughly chopped roasted peanuts. A very light dusting of finely grated parmesan cheese provides a subtle savory finish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, cozy lighting suggesting a home kitchen. A traditional Thai spoon and fork are placed beside the plate, and a casually folded cloth napkin completes the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a traditional Thai spoon and fork.
Offer extra condiments like chili flakes, sugar, or a small bowl of soy sauce on the side for diners to adjust flavor to their preference.
instructions: Press excess water from tofu. Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Fry tofu cubes until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Cook rice vermicelli noodles according to package instructions (usually soak in hot water or boil briefly). Drain thoroughly and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, soy sauce, palm sugar, minced garlic, and sliced chilies (if using) until sugar dissolves.
Thinly slice the red onion. Julienne the cucumber and carrot into thin strips.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked noodles, crispy tofu, sliced red onion, julienned cucumber, and julienned carrot.
Pour the dressing over the noodle mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Chop fresh cilantro and roasted peanuts.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with chopped cilantro, roasted peanuts, and a light sprinkle of finely grated parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure tofu is pressed well to achieve maximum crispiness when fried.
The parmesan cheese is a non-traditional addition for an extra savory note; adjust quantity to personal taste or omit for a more authentic Thai profile.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors in the dressing (Rod Chat)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Glass Noodle Salad with Crispy Garlic-Parmesan Topping
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, homely single portion of Spicy Thai Glass Noodle Salad rests on a simple, well-used ceramic plate with a subtle rim, centered on a rustic wooden kitchen table. The clear glass noodles are loosely piled, forming a natural base, intermingled with tender, diced ground chicken. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes, crisp julienned cucumber, and thinly sliced red onion are scattered throughout, adding pops of color and texture. Freshly chopped cilantro and whole mint leaves are visible, lending vibrant green accents. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown crispy garlic bits and slightly toasted, irregular parmesan crumbles are scattered over the top, providing a textural contrast and savory aroma. The salad is casually arranged, allowing components to naturally overlap. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, highlighting the natural colors. A simple fork or chopsticks rest beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges and sliced bird's eye chilies on the side for individual adjustment of flavor.
Traditionally enjoyed as a refreshing main course or part of a larger meal with other dishes.
Can be mixed at the table before eating.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 6 cloves (4 for dressing, 2 for crispy garlic)

instructions: Prepare crispy garlic-parmesan: Heat 60 ml vegetable oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Remove garlic with a slotted spoon. Add finely grated parmesan to the hot oil (off heat) and stir quickly to form crispy bits. Remove parmesan bits with slotted spoon. Drain garlic and parmesan on paper towel. Set aside.
Cook ground chicken: In a pan, cook ground chicken over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through. Break up lumps. Drain excess fat. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Set aside.

Cook noodles: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add glass noodles. Cook according to package instructions, usually 3-5 minutes, until tender but still slightly chewy. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Drain again thoroughly.

Make dressing: In a bowl, combine 4 minced garlic cloves, sliced bird's eye chilies, lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust for sweet, sour, salty, spicy balance.
Assemble salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked noodles, cooked chicken, sliced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, julienned cucumber, and julienned carrot.
Add dressing and herbs: Pour dressing over salad. Add chopped cilantro and mint leaves. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve: Divide salad among 4 plates. Sprinkle generously with crispy garlic and parmesan topping. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
Ensure glass noodles are well-drained to prevent a watery salad.
The crispy garlic-parmesan topping is best made fresh and added just before serving to maintain crispness.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the five flavors (sweet, sour, salty, spicy, umami) in the dressing.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Bell Pepper Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Beef and Bell Pepper Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The rich, reddish-brown stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, dark brown beef cubes nestled among vibrant chunks of red, yellow, and green bell peppers. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A simple, off-white ceramic side plate with a slice of crusty bread rests next to the bowl. A plain, folded linen napkin and a sturdy metal fork are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Traditionally, this stew can be served with small potato dumplings (nokedli) or boiled potatoes.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Toss with plain flour, salt, and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Do not burn paprika.
Return seared beef to the pot. Stir in diced tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add bell pepper chunks to the pot. Cook uncovered for another 15-20 minutes, until peppers are tender-crisp.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a deeper flavor, let the stew rest overnight in the refrigerator and reheat it the next day.
Adjust the amount of paprika to your preference for a milder or bolder flavor.
traditional_techniques: Layering paprika into a base of sautéed onions

recipes.recipe_name: Lentil Bolognese with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a generous portion of rigatoni pasta coated in a rich, dark red lentil bolognese. The rigatoni tubes are visibly filled with the hearty sauce, which has a rustic, thick texture with finely diced onion, carrot, celery, and tender green lentils throughout. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the top, providing a pop of color. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded off-white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. The background is a softly blurred, warm-toned bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a sprinkle of vegan Parmesan cheese.
instructions: Rinse lentils. Cook lentils in water according to package directions until tender. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape bottom of pot. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add cooked lentils, crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and dried oregano. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in nutritional yeast if desired.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 100ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta to the bolognese sauce. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Red Pepper Pesto Pasta with Broccolini
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Roasted Red Pepper Pesto Pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple light wooden table. The penne pasta is generously coated in a vibrant, rich orange-red pesto, showcasing its creamy texture. Dark green broccolini florets are interspersed throughout the pasta, offering a pleasing color contrast and tender-crisp texture. A few whole roasted walnuts are visible, adding visual interest and a subtle crunch. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves. Moderate negative space surrounds the pasta, ensuring a clean, uncluttered appearance. The scene is lit with natural, even lighting, creating soft shadows. A folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. The background suggests a modern bistro setting, subtly out of focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skins are charred and blistered.
Transfer roasted peppers to a bowl. Cover with cling film for 10 minutes. Peel skins from peppers. Discard skins.
In a food processor, combine peeled roasted peppers, walnuts, garlic, nutritional yeast, basil, lemon juice, and red pepper flakes. Pulse until roughly chopped.
Gradually drizzle in olive oil while processing until a smooth pesto forms. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, trim broccolini. Blanch broccolini in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water. Return pasta to the pot.
Add roasted red pepper pesto to the pasta. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water gradually, if needed, to achieve desired consistency.
Add blanched broccolini to the pasta. Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately.
